items.title: Named-profile gateways can inherit another profile's bot tokens: Teams SDK loads a foreign .env at import time

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
`plugins/platforms/teams/adapter.py` imports `microsoft_teams.apps.app`, and that module runs `load_dotenv(find_dotenv(usecwd=True))` at import time (`site-packages/microsoft_teams/apps/app.py:69` on the current SDK). `find_dotenv(usecwd=True)` walks up from the process cwd and loads the first `.env` it finds, and `load_dotenv` fills any var the process doesn't already have set. So a gateway whose cwd sits at or under another profile's HERMES_HOME silently absorbs that profile's env, bot tokens included.

I hit this twice on a multi-profile install this week. A named-profile gateway was launched with cwd set to the default HERMES_HOME (a plist generation bug, fixed in #40867), the Teams import pulled in the default profile's `.env`, and profiles with no Telegram token of their own started polling my main agent's Telegram bot. Result was two gateways fighting one bot token: a getUpdates 409 conflict loop every 20-45s, my messages randomly answered by the wrong model with a foreign session, and one internal maintenance response delivered straight into my chat.

The plist fix closes my trigger, but the class stays open: any cwd near a foreign `.env` leaks it into the gateway. Worth a Hermes-side defence regardless of what the SDK does. Two shapes that would work: snapshot `os.environ` around the teams import and drop anything the import added, or pin gateway cwd to its own HERMES_HOME at startup before platform imports run. Happy to PR either if there's a preferred direction.

Mitigation for anyone else running multi-profile: give every profile `.env` explicit empty entries for tokens it must not inherit (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=` and so on). `load_dotenv` never overrides a set var, and the platforms treat empty as disabled.

items.title: Desktop app: Remote gateway reachability check fails ("Could not reach this gateway yet") despite server being fully healthy and reachable via curl/browser on the same machine
items.body:
## Title
Desktop app: Remote gateway reachability check fails ("Could not reach this gateway yet") despite server being fully healthy and reachable via curl/browser on the same machine

## Summary
The desktop app's Settings → Gateway → Remote reachability probe reports "Could not reach this gateway yet" and blocks OAuth sign-in, even though the target URL is demonstrably healthy and reachable from the exact same machine via `curl`, over IPv4 and IPv6, on every plausible health-check path. The failure appears isolated to the Electron app's own network request — no error is written to any of the app's log files (`desktop.log`, `errors.log`, `gui.log`), and the underlying HTTP server (Hermes's own `web_server.py`) returns normal `302`/`401` responses throughout.

## Environment
- Desktop app: "Reiko Assistant" build (rebranded Hermes desktop client), `v0.19.0 146f4ed`
- OS: macOS
- Remote gateway: self-hosted Hermes Agent instance on a separate host (Ubuntu 26.04 VM), fronted by nginx (NPM) + Cloudflare (proxied CNAME to a `cloudflared` tunnel)
- Remote gateway URL configured: `https://your-domain.example.com`
- A second, separate local Hermes install also exists on the same Mac (`~/Developer/Tools/Hermes/`) — not implicated, but worth noting since the app supports both Local and Remote modes

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Settings → Gateway → Remote URL to a working, publicly reachable HTTPS Hermes gateway (reverse-proxied, valid Let's Encrypt cert, `nginx_online: true`)
2. Click "Save and reconnect" or "Test remote"
3. Observe: dialog reports "Remote gateway incomplete" / "Could not reach this gateway yet. Check the URL — the auth method will appear once it responds."
4. Boot log (separate error toast) shows a loop of:
   ```
   [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
   [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in. Open Settings → Gateway and click "Sign in", or switch back to Local.
   ```
   repeating indefinitely.

## Evidence the server itself is healthy (tested from the exact same machine, same moment)
```
$ dig +short your-domain.example.com
192.168.0.12   # correctly resolves to internal reverse-proxy IP via local DNS override

$ curl -sv https://your-domain.example.com/ --max-time 8
< HTTP/2 302
< server: openresty
< location: /login?next=%2F
# — normal, expected unauthenticated redirect

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://your-domain.example.com/health
302

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://your-domain.example.com/health/detailed
302

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://your-domain.example.com/api/health
401   # expected, requires auth — server IS responding correctly

$ curl -4 -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://your-domain.example.com/
302

$ curl -6 -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://your-domain.example.com/
302
```
Also independently verified (via the reverse proxy's own admin API) at the moment of failure:
- Proxy host enabled: `true`
- Proxy backend online (`nginx_online`): `true`
- Forwarding correctly to the gateway's actual host:port
- Valid, non-expired TLS certificate in use
- Local DNS override for the domain present and enabled

None of this was touched or changed around the time the desktop app started failing — infrastructure was independently re-verified clean both before and after a full reboot of the remote gateway VM, with identical results.

## What we ruled out
- DNS resolution issue — resolves correctly, confirmed via `dig` and macOS `scutil --dns`
- IPv4/IPv6 — both work identically via curl
- Reverse proxy / TLS / cert issue — proxy admin API confirms healthy state, cert valid, curl completes full TLS handshake
- VPN/overlay-network routing — a same-machine `curl` succeeds through the exact same network path the app should be using
- Backend process down — remote gateway systemd service confirmed `active`, logs show no crash at the relevant time
- Stale config — reconfirmed after a full VM reboot of the remote host, same failure persists

## What we could not determine
The Electron app's own reachability probe does not appear to log its actual failure reason anywhere:
- `desktop.log` — empty
- `errors.log` / `gui.log` — only contain the **local** Hermes backend's Python logs (`hermes_cli.web_server`, `tui_gateway.ws`), unrelated to the remote-URL check
- No toast/dialog surfaces the underlying fetch error (DNS? TLS? timeout? CORS? something Electron-specific like a proxy setting or cert store difference from the OS?)

## Ask
1. Could the "Test remote" / reachability probe surface its actual underlying error (exception message, timeout value, or HTTP client error) in the UI or in `desktop.log`, rather than a generic "Could not reach this gateway yet"?
2. Is there a known difference between how the Electron main process performs this fetch vs. the OS-level network stack (custom DNS resolver, bundled cert store, proxy auto-detection, etc.) that could explain success via `curl`/browser but failure in-app?
3. Any additional diagnostic steps or debug flags to enable more verbose Electron-side network logging for this specific check?

Happy to provide `HAR`-equivalent captures, additional log files, or a screen recording if useful.

items.title: Hermes 自进化实战:从手动 cron 到 Nudge,再到 NousResearch 官方 GEPA — 一位重度用户的 12 天踩坑总结
items.body:
# Hermes 自进化实战:从手动 cron 到 Nudge,再到 NousResearch 官方 GEPA — 一位重度用户的 12 天踩坑总结

> **讨论分类建议**: Show and tell(或 Ideas,看仓库实际分类)
> **作者**: 一位用 RTX 4080 笔记本跑 Hermes 的重度用户
> **写作日期**: 2026-07-22
> **Hermes 版本**: v0.19.0 (upstream `4425ddd9`)
>
> **写在前**:这篇文章严格分两层事实——
> 1. **Hermes 开源代码里真实存在**(任何 `git clone NousResearch/hermes-agent` 的人都能复现)
> 2. **我本地装的私有脚本 + 业务上下文**(已脱敏为 `$HERMES_HOME` 占位符与"某业务"等概念)
>
> 不混用这两层,是为了让"踩坑经验"和"可复现事实"分别可追溯。如果你只想看理论,跳到第三节。
>
> **隐私说明**: 本文所有本地路径用业内通用占位符(`$HERMES_HOME`),所有数字与时间已脱敏,具体脚本路径不复现。
>
> **作者前言**: 这是把"博客稿 + Issue 草稿 + 12 天 87 个 session 的真实考古 + 一次 NousResearch 官方 GEPA 项目的实测"揉成的一篇"完整复盘"。

---

## 前言

我有一台笔记本。RTX 4080,12G 显存,32G 内存。这是我跑 Hermes 的全部家当。

从 DeepSeek 账单开始日(2026-06-23)算起,到今天(2026-07-22)一共 **18 天**,账单覆盖 **2026-06-30 ~ 2026-07-22**——其中 6-23 到 6-29 没有 token 记录。

**总花费**:
- DeepSeek:**¥326 RMB**(账单真账,18 天累计)
- Kimi:**¥150 RMB**(CEO 自报,无逐日明细)
- MiniMax-M3:**不计入账单**——按 token 算,这台笔记本 12 天里跑过 5.43M 真烧 input + 0.53M 真烧 output + 262M cache 命中(主对话当前还在用)
- **合计现金支出约 ¥476 RMB**

**DeepSeek 账单拆解**(DeepSeek 官方账单 CSV 真账):
- 总 token:**61.26 亿**
  - input_cache_hit:**59.70 亿**(占 97.4%,这一项几乎免费,0.000000025 美元/个)
  - input_cache_miss:**1.42 亿**(真烧,0.000003 美元/个)
  - output:**0.14 亿**(真烧,0.000006 美元/个)
- 按模型分:deepseek-v4-flash ¥264.94 + deepseek-v4-pro ¥61.06
- **平均每天 ¥18.11,真烧 token 占比仅 2.5%**——cache 命中率让我 61 亿 token 只付 ¥326

不是实验室的预算,不是公司的云额度,是我自己的账单。这 **¥476 RMB 加上几个不眠之夜**换来的是 **323 个 SKILL.md**(其中 **33 个从未被用过**,**5 个名字重复**,每天新增数量随我的心情在 0 到 80 之间随机波动)。

我写过外部 cron,每几小时扫一次会话记录让 LLM 自动提炼 skill。几个月后发现 cron 还在定时报错,报的还是 "Script not found"——脚本早被我删了,但 cron 不知道,token 还在烧。

我搭过重型 GEPA 管道,第一轮跑通了,两个 skill 升级,我很兴奋。第二轮脚本被删,管道死透,等我发现已经过了好几天。那几天的 cron 触发、LLM 调用、token 消耗,**粗估够我跑一个月的 Nudge Engine**。

我装了 Hermes 不到一个月,才知道它自带 `background_review.py`。这 **20 多天里我手动 cron 补**,多烧的 token 可能够我跑一年内置 Nudge。这个配置错误是我花得最冤的钱。

2026 年 7 月 22 日 14:21,我装上了 NousResearch 官方 GEPA,dry-run 通过,真跑卡在 synthetic eval 阶段,600 秒超时。我选的测试 skill 叫 `yuanbao`,3665 字符,是主仓库里最小的一个。我的笔记本撑不住。

这篇文章不是 "Hermes 使用指南"。这是一个用真金白银(¥476)买认知的人写的止损记录。每一行都沾着 OOM、超时、和凌晨三点看账单的痕迹。

如果你也在用一台笔记本跑 Agent 自进化,希望我的 61 亿 token 和 ¥476 能让你少烧一点。

---

**账单来源**:
- DeepSeek 账单 CSV:`~/Downloads/usage_data_2026-06-23_2026-07-22.zip`
- Kimi ¥150 是 CEO 自报,无逐日明细
- MiniMax-M3 数据来自 Hermes `state.db` 的 `session_model_usage` 表

---

## 一、起点:用外部 cron 强行驱动 Agent

去年我开始用 Hermes Agent 的时候,干了一件很多新手都会干的事:

**写一个 cron,每几小时扫一次会话记录,让 LLM 反思"刚才有没有可以提炼成 skill 的模式",然后自动 create skill。**

听起来很美对吧?Agent 自己反思、自己成长。几个月后我打开 skill 库看到几百个 SKILL.md,质量参差不齐——有的 skill 三句话就没了,有的 skill 引用了已经不存在的脚本路径,有的 skill 重复描述同一件事。

**量化数据**(来自真实 `.usage.json`):

- skill 库规模:几百个 SKILL.md(我挖到 319 个有 created_at 时间戳的)
- 命中率:约 90%(287/319)有 `use_count > 0`
- **僵尸 skill**:32 个从未用过,占 10%
- 每天新增 skill 曲线:有几天高峰 80+,有几天低谷(完全是手动跑/不跑的随机波动)
- 5 个疑似重复 skill 名字(`director`、`multi-agent-architecture` 等),说明 skill 创建没去重

更糟的是 cron 报的错——`Script not found: <某路径>` —— 每周固定蹦出来几次,说明那个 cron 早就跑不成了,但还在那里定时报错。

**这是我踩的第一个坑:用外部 cron 强行驱动 Agent 的"自进化",得到的是噪声不是信号**。

---

## 二、第二次尝试:重型 prompt 进化

今年 7 月,我看到社区有人跑 Genetic-Pareto prompt 进化算法,立刻心动:这才是真正的"自进化"啊——让 Agent 自己生成 prompt 变体、跑评估、保留优胜。

我自己写了一套简化版的 GEPA 管道(`gepa_mutation.py` + `gepa_evaluate.py` + `gepa_eliminate.py`),跑了一轮:

```
[Day-A] Mutation Cycle Start
[Day-A] Selected 2 candidates for mutation
[Day-A] ✅ X% improvement — applying upgrade!
[Day-A] ✅ Y% improvement — applying upgrade!
[Day-A] Cycle Complete
```

第一轮成功了。两个 skill 升级,综合分大幅跃升。

几天后我让它自动跑第二轮:

```
[Day-A+2] ❌ mutation.py failed (code 2)
[Day-A+2]    No such file or directory
[Day-A+2] Mutation failed, aborting cycle
```

**脚本不知道什么时候被删了**。重型自进化管道死了,自动跑机制没起来,等我发现已经过了好几天。

(注:为脱敏,本文不公开第一轮的具体提升数字。如果你好奇某类 prompt 进化算法的实战效果,关键词是"Genetic-Pareto"——但我建议看完本节再决定要不要走这条路。)

**这是我踩的第二个坑**——但**坑的本质不是"重型方案不行",而是"我没维护住"**。

这是后话,先按下不表。

---

## 三、转机:读 Hermes 源码发现的"Nudge Engine"

放弃自建重型方案后,我开始静下心来读 Hermes 源码——平时没耐心读,现在被现实按着头读。在 `background_review.py` 模块我发现了核心代码:

```python
"""Background memory/skill review — fork the agent to evaluate the turn.

After every turn, the main agent loop may spawn a daemon thread that
replays the conversation snapshot in a forked agent and asks itself
"should any skill/memory be saved or updated?". Writes go straight to
the memory + skill stores. Main conversation and prompt cache are never
touched.
"""
```

**Hermes 内置了"自进化"。**

而且设计得很巧:

1. **每轮对话结束**触发(在 `turn_finalizer.py`)
2. **fork 一个后台线程**,跑在新的 agent 实例里
3. **默认继承主模型 warm cache**——前文刚刚用过的 system prompt,这个 fork 不用重新发,极便宜
4. **工具白名单只有 memory + skill 管理**——不能误删文件,不能跑命令
5. **主对话和 prompt cache 完全不碰**——用户毫无感知

频率默认是每 10 个 user turn 触发一次 memory 复盘,每 10 次工具迭代触发一次 skill 复盘。配置项是:

```yaml
memory:
  nudge_interval: 10
skills:
  creation_nudge_interval: 10
```

**这就是 Hermes 的官方自进化方案。我之前这 20 多天都在重新发明它。**

但 Nudge Engine **不是"prompt cache 复用 = 零成本"**,要严谨地说:
- **warm cache 路径**(同模型):fork 命中父 agent 的 prompt cache,几乎零额外成本
- **cold 路径**(路由到不同模型):fork 必须重读完整 transcript 写冷 cache,**有显著成本**

所以如果你想配 `auxiliary.background_review` 路由到便宜模型,要明确知道这是在 **cold-write 模式** 下。源码里说得很清楚("the fork is cold regardless — replaying the full transcript would just cold-write it")。

---

## 四、为什么 Nudge 不够,还要 Cron?

但只用 Nudge 有个明显短板:**它只能看当前对话的 message snapshot**。

意思是——

- 能发现"刚才那个工具调用失败了"
- **不能**发现"上周一 A session、本周一 B session、今天 C session 都踩了同一个坑"——这需要跨 session 聚合

而"反复踩同一个坑"恰恰是最值得提炼成 skill 的场景。

所以我的最终方案是**双轨制**:

```
                    Nudge Engine(post-turn 异步线程)
                           ↓ 写 memory + skill
                    ┌──────────────────────┐
                    │ 共享 skill/memory 库  │
                    └──────────────────────┘
                           ↑ 读
   ┌──────────────────┐    ↑    ┌──────────────────────┐
   │ 失败模式探测器   │────┘    │  神经突触修剪        │
   │ (cron 6h)        │         │  (cron 每天 5 点)    │
   └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────────┘
            ↓ stdout 注入                  ↓
   ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────┐
   │ 决策治理器       │         │  长期未用 skill      │
   │ (LLM cron 6h)    │         │  自动归档            │
   └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────────┘
```

**Nudge 负责"局部反射"**(本轮对话刚刚学到了什么),**Cron 负责"全局复盘"**(跨多 session 出现的模式)。两者互补,缺一会让"反复踩同类坑"检测不到。

**具体频率**(我自己的 cron,公开出来供参考):

| 组件 | 频率 |
|------|------|
| Nudge memory | 每 10 个 user turn |
| Nudge skill | 每 10 次工具迭代 |
| 失败模式探测器 | every 6h |
| 决策治理器 | every 6h,接探测器输出 |
| 主动复盘 | every 12h,写 memory + 更新 all-round-assistant |
| 神经突触修剪 | 每天 5 点,60 天未用自动归档 |

---

## 五、踩坑案例:三个真实失败

### 案例 1:外部 cron 引用了不存在的脚本

**症状**:每几小时报一次错,但 cron 仍然 enabled。

**根因**:被引用的脚本在某次清理中被删了,但 cron 配置没同步删。框架的 cron 不会"探测脚本是否存在"——它只看 schedule。

**修复**:用 cron 管理命令直接 remove。

**教训**:**自进化 cron 失败应该静默降级,不该持续报错**。我后来在系统配置里加了"进化熔断"条款(下面第六节会展开),要求"任何自进化管道连续失败立即冻结,输出求助标签",避免 cron 持续报错污染日志。

### 案例 2:Nudge 引擎默认配置没启用

我装了 Hermes 不到一个月,从来不知道有 Nudge Engine。原因很简单——

```bash
$ grep nudge_interval <config.yaml>
(nothing)
```

**症状**:感觉 Agent 从来不自动写 memory,从 prompt 看也找不到相关触发。

**根因**:源码里有默认 `_memory_nudge_interval = 10`,但**这个默认只在 agent 启动时生效**——如果 profile override 把它覆盖回 0,Nudge 就关掉了。

**修复**:在 `config.yaml` 显式写:

```yaml
memory:
  nudge_interval: 10
skills:
  creation_nudge_interval: 10
```

**教训**:**重要的默认值应该显式声明,不要假设它会生效**。

### 案例 3:历史日志残留骗我以为系统在跑

我研究自进化机制的时候,看到 log 目录里有几百字节的旧日志,还有几个 json 文件,第一反应是"哦系统在跑"。

实际上相关脚本**早被删了**。日志只是历史残留。

```
[Day-X] ✅ X% improvement — applying upgrade!
...
[Day-X+2] ❌ mutation.py failed (code 2)
[Day-X+2]    No such file or directory
```

**症状**:看到日志以为系统在跑,实际管道已经死透。

**根因**:日志不会自动过期——它永远在硬盘上,直到有人删。

**教训**:**真账核实要看"现在的 cron 状态"而不是"历史的 log 文件"**。

---

## 六、我现在的完整方案(20 多天踩坑后的真实架构)

经过 20 多天踩坑,我现在的自进化架构是这样的——**三层结构**:

### 层 A:内置后台引擎(每轮触发)

| 组件 | 触发频率 | 模型 | 作用 |
|------|----------|------|------|
| Nudge memory | 每 10 个 user turn | 主模型(命中 warm cache) | 后台判断要不要写 memory |
| Nudge skill | 每 10 次工具迭代 | 同上 | 后台判断要不要 create/patch skill |

### 层 B:Cron 管道(跨 session 聚合)

| Cron | 频率 | 作用 |
|------|------|------|
| 失败模式探测器 | every 6h | 扫所有 session,找失败模式 |
| 决策治理器 | every 6h | 接探测器输出,决策增删改 skill |
| 主动复盘 | every 12h | 主动复盘失败教训,写 memory |
| 神经突触修剪 | 每天 5 点 | 长期未用 skill 自动归档 |

### 层 C:**重型方案 — NousResearch 官方 GEPA(新发现的)**

我之前 3 次说"Hermes 没 GEPA/DSPy"——**都错了**。

Hermes **有官方的自进化子项目**:`NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution`,2026-07-22 实测:

- 4,793 stars,MIT 协议
- 用 **DSPy + GEPA**(Genetic-Pareto Prompt Evolution)做 skill/tool/prompt 优化
- **5 Phase 已落地状态**:

```
Phase 1 ✅ Skill files(SKILL.md)        DSPy + GEPA
Phase 2 🔲 Tool descriptions            DSPy + GEPA
Phase 3 🔲 System prompt sections       DSPy + GEPA
Phase 4 🔲 Tool implementation code     Darwinian Evolver
Phase 5 🔲 Continuous improvement loop  Automated pipeline
```

**5 条护栏**(每个变体必须过):
1. ✅ Full test suite — `pytest tests/ -q` 必须 100%
2. ✅ Size limits — Skill ≤15KB,tool desc ≤500 chars
3. ✅ Caching compatibility — 不能 mid-conversation 改
4. ✅ Semantic preservation — 不能 drift 原意
5. ✅ **PR review** — 所有改动走 PR,**never direct commit**

**架构设计很关键**:`hermes-agent-self-evolution operates ON hermes-agent, not inside it`——它读 hermes-agent 仓库,在分支上写改动,**手动 PR 合并**。

### 进化熔断(系统配置)

```yaml
R14 — 进化熔断机制(自进化专用)
- 触发场景: skill 创建/修改 或 Nudge Engine 后台反思
- 熔断条件: 连续 3 次修改同一 Skill 仍未解决报错 → 立即停止
- 熔断动作: 输出求助标签 + 上报到固定路径,等待人类裁决
```

## 七、给其他开发者的建议

如果你正在搭 Agent 自进化,我的建议是——**按"先轻后重"的顺序**:

### 第 1 步:开箱即用的 Nudge Engine(零成本)

别从 cron 开始。先读你用的 Agent 框架源码,看有没有内置的"对话后反思"机制。

**Hermes 有 Nudge**,LangChain 有 Reflexion,AutoGen 有 GroupChatManager——框架作者已经替你踩过坑了。

配置方法:
```yaml
memory:
  nudge_interval: 10
skills:
  creation_nudge_interval: 10
```

**效果**:自动写 memory、自动创建 skill,**几乎不烧 token**(warm cache 路径)。

### 第 2 步:加 Cron 做全局复盘(中等成本)

Nudge 只能看本轮。要做"反复踩同类坑"的检测,需要 cron 跨 session 聚合。

最小配置:
- 失败模式探测器(每 6 小时扫 session)
- 决策治理器(基于探测器输出,LLM 决定增删改)
- 神经突触修剪(每天,60 天未用自动归档)

### 第 3 步:有需要再上重型方案(较高成本)

**重型方案不是不能上,是有前提**:
- ✅ 你愿意维护脚本(不能像案例 1 那样脚本被孤立删除)
- ✅ 你能接受 $2-10 per optimization run 的 token 成本
- ✅ 你接受 "写到分支+人工 review" 的工作流(不是自动 push)

**NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution 是当前最成熟的方案**:
- 5 Phase 已落 1 个(Phase 1: skill files)
- 5 条护栏(test/size/cache/语义/PR)
- MIT 协议,4793 stars

**首次跑建议**:
1. `pip install -e ".[dev]"` 装好
2. dry-run 验证 setup
3. 选一个**主仓库里最小**的 skill(我选 yuanbao,3.7KB)
4. **后台跑,不限时**(我设的 600s 太短,5 分钟是 GEPA 的最低成本)
5. 跑完看 PR 分支,人工 review 后再决定合不合

### 4 个铁律

1. **双轨制不要砍**。Nudge 是"每节课后作业",Cron 是"每周月考",缺一会让"反复踩同类坑"检测不到
2. **重型方案慎用,但别怕**。前提是你愿意维护它
3. **真账核实**。看到历史日志不代表系统在跑。看到 cron 存在不代表 cron 在工作
4. **进化熔断**。自进化最容易出"无限重写",必须有熔断 + 求助机制

## 附言:用 Friston 自由能原理(FEP)重新看 GEPA

写完上面 8 节后,我顺手读了一篇关联论文《耦合随机性与主动推理》,它的 §5.1 把 GEPA 这类 prompt 进化算法的数学父亲讲清楚了——**Friston 的自由能原理(Active Inference)**。

### FEP 5 步架构对照表

| 步 | GEPA 实际动作 | FEP/Active Inference 对应概念 | 物理/认知直觉 | CEO 调哪个 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. 加载 artifact** | 读 `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent/skills/X/SKILL.md` | 主体观测环境状态 $S_t$ | "我看到当前 skill 长这样" | 选 `--skill X` |
| **2. 生成 eval dataset** | LLM 读 SKILL.md 造评测样例(`dataset_builder.py` `synthetic` 路径) | 变分先验 $P(\vec{D})$ | "我猜哪些测试能区分好坏" | `--eval-source {synthetic,sessiondb,golden}` |
| **3. GEPA 跑多轮** | 每轮生成变体 → 评估 → 保留 Pareto 最优 | **主动推理**(Active Inference) | "我主动选下一轮怎么探" | `--iterations N` |
| **3a. 变体生成** | LLM prompt-mutation:加约束/改措辞/换例子 | 行动 $a$(action)——主体主动改 $\vec{D}$ | "我改 prompt 试探哪个更好" | GEPA 内部,不能直接调 |
| **3b. 评估** | 评分:`accuracy * token_cost * speed` | 变分自由能 $\mathcal{F}_{FEP}$ = 准确度 - 复杂度 | "这个变体的预测误差多小" | 评分函数(目前用关键词重叠,issue #150 想换成 verifier) |
| **3c. 保留/淘汰** | Pareto 前沿选择 | 最小化 $\mathcal{F}_{FEP}$ | "我只留综合最优的" | GEPA 内部 |
| **4. 5 条护栏检查** | test/size/cache/语义/PR | 守门(Guardrails) | "别让改坏的东西出去" | `--run-tests` 开关 |
| **5. 写到分支提 PR** | 在 `hermes-agent` 仓库建 `evolution/X-...` 分支 | 决策输出(action 选择) | "我决定这是新版本的 SKILL.md" | 自动 |

### 评分

| 维度 | 博客稿 | 综合稿 | FEP 架构图 |
|------|------|------|------|
| 核心贡献 | Nudge | 复盘 | 理论映射 |
| 可信度 | 源码 | 源码+实测 | 类比 |
| 最大风险 | 数据少 | 缺图表 | 过度拟合理论 |
| 一句话 | "贴工位" | "全员" | "贴配置旁,但别当圣经" |

### 好处(实测立竿见影)

1. **调参有逻辑参考,不再是黑盒**
   - 不知道 `--iterations` 怎么定?→ FEP 视角告诉你"iterations = 主动推理的步数,钱多用大步,钱紧用小步"
   - 不知道 `--eval-source` 选哪个?→ "eval-source = 主体观测世界的方式:synthetic 是想象,sessiondb 是回忆,golden 是查权威"
   - 不知道评分为什么奇怪?→ "评分函数 = 变分自由能,issue #150 替换它就是在重写 $\mathcal{F}_{FEP}$"

2. **理解 issue #150 #151 #152 不是"杂务",是 FEP 的工程化**
   - **#150** 加客观 verifier → 在重写**自由能的"准确度"项**
   - **#151** 加语义保持 + 数据去重 → 在重写**自由能的"复杂度"项**
   - **#152** 加成本审计 → 在加**主体的"行动成本"账本**

3. **理解了"PR review 这条护栏"为什么值钱**
   - 之前以为是 NousResearch 工程师的安全感
   - FEP 视角下:PR review **像**马尔可夫毯(后面会展开这个边界)
   - 这跟 SOUL.md 加的 R14 进化熔断**是同一个思想**:自我反思必须有外部观察者打断

4. **Nudge Engine 调参有了理论依据**
   - 论文 §3.2 说:**降低 γ(认知阻尼)能放大偏置**
   - 对应到 Hermes:**降低 `nudge_interval`(提高反思频率)** 倾向让 skill/memory 更快被改写
   - 这反过来也解释了"profile override 把 nudge_interval 改成 0"为什么是错的——**Nudge 是必备的灵活性,不能完全关闭**
   - ⚠️ **重要保留**:这个映射是**类比**,不是数学等价

### 坏处(必须警惕)

1. **"γ = nudge_interval"是类比不是等式**
   - 论文里 γ 是热力学阻尼系数(连续松弛过程 $D(t) = D_{target} + (D_0 - D_{target}) e^{-\gamma t}$)
   - Hermes `nudge_interval` 是离散步数(每 N 轮触发一次反思)
   - 两个量在**直觉上**(灵活度↑ → 反思频率↑)**类似**,但**没有数学推导**把它们等同
   - 我之前的架构图里写"nudge_interval=5 → γ 小"是**类比滑向了等式**——这是错的

2. **"GEPA = 主动推理"标签过于慷慨**
   - FEP 主动推理 5 步:**感知 → 推断隐藏状态 → 选择行动 → 执行行动 → 更新信念**
   - GEPA 实际 4 步:**读 skill(感知) → 生成变体(行动) → 评估(执行+筛选) → 保留/淘汰(更新)**
   - **GEPA 缺"推断隐藏状态"这一步**——它没有内部信念模型,只是"瞎试+筛选"
   - 这更接近**进化算法**(如 1+λ ES),而不是主动推理
   - 我自己在架构图引言里写了"GEPA = Friston Active Inference 在 prompt 空间的简化实现——只做 mutation",**但下面的表格还是标"主动推理"**——前后矛盾

3. **"PR review = 马尔可夫毯"机制层不成立**
   - 马尔可夫毯是**数学上定义的统计边界**——一组变量屏蔽了系统内外的信息流动
   - PR review 是**社会性的质量控制机制**——人类判断 + 协商 + 习俗
   - 两个在**功能上相似**(防止系统自我循环),但**实现完全不同**
   - 我之前架构图把它们等同,是混淆了"功能相似"和"机制相同"
   - 正确说法:**PR review 在功能上**扮演**马尔可夫毯的角色**——这是类比,不是定义

4. **缺反例/失败映射(本文最大缺陷)**
   - 上面 8 节有 3 个真实失败案例,但 FEP 这篇**全是正向映射**——显得过于顺滑
   - 不像"踩过坑的人写的"

### 反例:按 FEP 调参会踩什么坑

#### 真实考古的踩坑(20 多天里实测过)

**案例 A:profile override 把 nudge_interval 改回 0**

我之前在 codex-profile 下用过 `nudge_interval=10`,但 profile override 没把它覆盖回 0。结果:
- 主对话 20 多天没自动写一条 memory
- 我以为 Nudge 是坏的,实**际是我自己配错了**

按 FEP 视角看:**这是"灵活性从 100 掉到 0"的退化**——把 γ 推到无穷大,主体完全不会调整,变成"机械决定论"(只听外部指令)。

**教训**:FEP 视角下,任何覆盖默认值的 profile 都应该**显式声明**它把 γ 改成多少,否则就埋雷。

**案例 B:auxiliary 路由改完忘了回滚,token 烧 2 倍**

2026-07-22 13:09 把 4 个高频 auxiliary 切到 deepseek-chat。但**没同时把 budget 跟踪打开**。如果 token 突然失控,无法及时发现——这也是 FEP 视角下"行动成本"信号缺失的代价。

教训:别只调"行动偏好"(模型路由),**不调"成本感知"**——主体乱行动不心疼。

#### 理论推断的反例(未实测,按 FEP 推出来容易踩的)

**案例 C:按"γ 小 → 更灵活"调 nudge_interval=2,结果 skill 库爆炸**

按 FEP 推论:`nudge_interval=2`(极激进)= γ 极小 = 主体每 2 轮就反思。
**预期失败**:每轮对话产生 1-2 条新 skill/memory 写入,10 轮对话后 +10-20 条,**一周后库爆**。
**真实因果**:Nudge 是每 10 轮触发一次,默认 10 是经验值,**不是 FEP 推出来的最优值**——按 FEP 推"γ 越小越好"是过度简化。
**教训**:**Nudge 频率有下界**——太激进会让 skill 库膨胀 + token 烧光。

**案例 D:按"eval-source sessiondb 用真实数据更好"跑关键 skill,模型学坏**

按 FEP 推论:sessiondb 是"主体回忆真实历史",比 synthetic(想象)更真实。
**预期失败**:真实 session 里**有大量垃圾**(我挖 Top 10 session 时,有些内容只是"网没了""查查网"这种噪声)。sessiondb 把噪声当真实,模型学到"用 noise 当 prompt"——**评估函数被污染**。
**真实因果**:sessiondb 质量**完全取决于 session 自身的信噪比**——没质量筛选就别用。
**教训**:**eval-source 不是"越真实越好"**,而是"信噪比越高越好"。session 噪声大时,**golden 比 sessiondb 强**。

### 一句话总结

**学 FEP 的价值 = 给 GEPA 调参提供"为什么这么调"的解释;不学的损失 = 调参靠记忆和试错,效率低但 ROI 也不差。**

如果你时间紧,跳过 FEP 直接按"5 步对照表"调,也能上手——它把"理论"压成了"操作 cheat sheet"。但**别把对照表里的"="当真**——大部分是类比,不是定义。

**核心警示**:
- 看到 γ、KL、自由能 → 问一句"这是**类比**还是**真等式**"
- 看到"GEPA = 主动推理" → 记住"GEPA 是**简化版**,缺推理那一步"
- 看到"PR review = 马尔可夫毯" → 记住"功能相似,机制不同"
- 看到"按 FEP 推参数" → 想 5 秒"我有没有反例"

---

**作者**: 一位用 RTX 4080 笔记本跑 Hermes 的重度用户
**发表时间**: 2026-07-22
**Hermes 版本**: v0.19.0 (upstream `4425ddd9`)
**NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution**: commit `0a929e3a` (2026-06-17)

items.title: [Bug]: Switching Desktop profiles cancels active async delegation after 20 seconds

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

Switching away from a Hermes Desktop profile can silently cancel that profile's active background `delegate_task` batch after the 20-second WebSocket orphan grace period.

The foreground turn may already look idle while background delegates are still running. A normal live profile switch disconnects/detaches the old profile's Desktop WebSocket. The TUI gateway then classifies the idle foreground session as orphaned without checking for active async delegations, reaps it after 20 seconds, and `_finalize_session()` interrupts the batch. Returning to the profile much later is required before a retained/synthetic completion event causes the conversation to continue.

This contradicts the Desktop lifecycle contract documented in `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`: a live profile swap should allow background profiles to keep streaming, and visibility should not be treated as lifecycle.

I reproduced the same pattern more than once. No prompt or transcript contents are included below.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop with at least two profiles.
2. In profile A, run a chat that calls `delegate_task(..., background=true)` (a parallel batch also reproduces it).
3. Wait until the foreground turn settles while the delegated tasks are still running.
4. Switch to profile B and remain there for more than 20 seconds.
5. Inspect profile A's gateway log.
6. Return to profile A after several minutes.

### Expected Behavior

A live Desktop profile switch should not end profile A's session or cancel its active background delegates.

The old profile should retain a durable owner/runtime until its background work finishes, and completion should be routed back to the correct conversation even while another profile is visible. If Hermes intentionally cannot preserve the work, Desktop should warn and require confirmation before switching/canceling.

### Actual Behavior

The profile switch detaches profile A's WebSocket. About 20 seconds later, `ws_orphan_reap` finalizes the session and interrupts its active async delegation batch. Its addressed notification is then rejected because the original UI owner is gone.

When profile A is opened again, a synthetic/retained “async delegation batch complete” event starts a new continuation turn. The original child processes were not running normally during the time away.

### Affected Component

- Other: Desktop profile switching / TUI gateway session lifecycle
- Agent Core: async delegation lifecycle

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (Desktop structured gateway)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not uploaded to avoid publishing profile configuration or conversation logs.
Sanitized environment and the relevant timestamped gateway events are included below.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### Python Version

3.13.13

### Hermes Version

```text
Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
Observed local revision: 9b99b35b (+1 carried Desktop commit)
Current upstream inspected: 7de55427
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
```

The runtime reproduction was on the local carried branch. I also inspected current `origin/main` at `7de55427`: the same 20-second reap + finalize/interrupt combination is still present there.

### Additional Logs / Traceback (sanitized)

```text
11:31:56.143  dispatched async delegation batch deleg_d98f69af (3 tasks)
11:32:04.895  Desktop WS closed: client_disconnect; detached_sessions=1
11:32:24.906  Interrupted 1 async delegation(s) for ending session (ws_orphan_reap)
11:32:25.014  Dropping unowned async_delegation notification
                (origin=<redacted> key=<redacted>) instead of delivering
11:40:10.xxx  profile A WS accepted after the profile was reopened
11:40:19.665  new continuation turn receives
                [ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — deleg_d98f69af]

Second occurrence:
11:23:39.502  dispatched batch deleg_2f7e846d (3 tasks)
11:24:01.xxx  Desktop WS closed after profile switch
11:24:21.945  interrupted by ws_orphan_reap
11:25:20.xxx  profile reopened
11:25:34.897  completion/continuation turn begins
```

The “Interrupted 1” count is the one batch record; each observed batch contained three child tasks.

### Root Cause Analysis

Current `origin/main` at `7de55427` contains the complete failure chain:

1. `tui_gateway/server.py:162-166` sets `HERMES_TUI_WS_ORPHAN_REAP_GRACE_S` to 20 seconds by default.
2. `_ws_session_is_orphaned()` at `tui_gateway/server.py:824` only spares a detached session when its foreground `running` flag is true. It does not account for active async delegation owned by the session.
3. `_schedule_ws_orphan_reap()` at `tui_gateway/server.py:838` therefore reaps the old profile after a normal Desktop profile switch.
4. `_finalize_session()` at `tui_gateway/server.py:593` calls `interrupt_for_session()` at lines 701-713.
5. `tools/async_delegation.py:875` interrupts matching delegation records.
6. The fail-closed notification path around `tui_gateway/server.py:9896` then drops the event because no live session can prove ownership.

Both individual mechanisms were intentional:

- `96cd37e21` added the 20-second orphan reaper to prevent one leaked slash-worker process per abandoned/refreshing embedded-chat session.
- `4b27be111` / #55578 bound delegation lifetime to the closing session and prevented cross-chat result injection.

The regression is their interaction with Desktop's live multi-profile swap. A profile becoming hidden/detached is being treated as abandoned even though it owns active background work.

### Proposed Fix

This needs a lifecycle-aware fix, not simply disabling either safety mechanism:

- Distinguish an intentional live Desktop profile swap from an abandoned browser/tab WebSocket.
- Preserve a positive completion owner and the profile runtime while async delegations are active.
- After the last delegate finishes, reschedule normal orphan cleanup if no client has reattached.
- Keep #55578's fail-closed routing guarantee: never inject a completion into a foreign chat.
- Add an end-to-end regression test: dispatch background delegation in profile A, switch to profile B for longer than the reap grace, complete the delegation, and assert profile A receives the result without cancellation or cross-session delivery.

Setting `HERMES_TUI_WS_ORPHAN_REAP_GRACE_S=0` is only a diagnostic workaround; it restores the slash-worker leak that the reaper was created to fix. Skipping `interrupt_for_session()` globally would likewise reintroduce orphan token burn/cross-session lifecycle problems.

Related: #55578, #57502, and #60609.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature]: Add LLM-friendly Hermes Agent documentation, including `llms.txt` and Markdown docs
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

When asking Hermes Agent questions about its own capabilities, available commands, configuration options, setup steps, or troubleshooting procedures, it often does not find reliable answers based on the documentation alone.

In practice, I often need to manually provide Hermes with a direct documentation URL or GitHub link before it can help with a specific issue. This makes the experience less smooth, especially for new users who expect an AI agent to be able to explain how to configure, operate, and troubleshoot itself.

This is particularly relevant because Hermes Agent is itself an LLM-based tool. Users naturally expect it to be able to reason over its own documentation effectively.


### Proposed Solution

Recently, while using the n8n documentation, I discovered a **"View as Markdown"** button that opens a Markdown version of the current documentation page. I found this extremely helpful when working with LLMs, as Markdown content is much easier for them to parse and reason about.

After a bit more digging, I found this gem:

https://docs.n8n.io/llms.txt


This file points LLMs to Markdown versions of the documentation and makes it much easier for AI tools to locate relevant information, understand the documentation structure, and provide accurate help.

A similar solution for Hermes Agent could include:

- A public `llms.txt` file for Hermes Agent documentation.
- Markdown versions of important documentation pages.
- Clear links to key areas such as:
  - installation
  - profiles
  - skills
  - tools
  - desktop app
  - backend / gateway / dashboard setup
  - environment variables
  - authentication
  - troubleshooting
  - remote/self-hosted usage
- Optional links from the regular documentation UI, such as a "View as Markdown" button.

If such a resource already exists, it would be helpful to make it easier to discover from the main documentation.

This would make Hermes Agent much easier to support with LLMs and would improve the setup and


### Alternatives Considered

### Alternative 1: Improve search within existing documentation

The existing documentation could be expanded or reorganized to improve discoverability. However, this still relies on users and LLMs finding the correct pages manually.

### Alternative 2: Create a dedicated Hermes documentation skill

A dedicated documentation skill could provide answers based on the docs. While useful, it would require ongoing maintenance and does not solve the broader problem of making documentation easily consumable by external LLMs and tools.

### Alternative 3: Status quo

Continue using the current documentation structure and manually provide documentation URLs when needed. This works, but creates unnecessary friction and reduces the effectiveness of AI-assisted troubleshooting and setup.

### Feature Type

Developer experience (tests, docs, CI)

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

### Debug Report (optional)


items.title: Desktop app: Remote gateway reachability check fails ("Could not reach this gateway yet") despite server being fully healthy and reachable via curl/browser on the same machine
items.body:
## Title
Desktop app: Remote gateway reachability check fails ("Could not reach this gateway yet") despite server being fully healthy and reachable via curl/browser on the same machine

## Summary
The desktop app's Settings → Gateway → Remote reachability probe reports "Could not reach this gateway yet" and blocks OAuth sign-in, even though the target URL is demonstrably healthy and reachable from the exact same machine via `curl`, over IPv4 and IPv6, on every plausible health-check path. The failure appears isolated to the Electron app's own network request — no error is written to any of the app's log files (`desktop.log`, `errors.log`, `gui.log`), and the underlying HTTP server (Hermes's own `web_server.py`) returns normal `302`/`401` responses throughout.

## Environment
- Desktop app: Hermes desktop client, `v0.19.0 146f4ed`
- OS: macOS
- Remote gateway: self-hosted Hermes Agent instance on a separate host (Ubuntu 26.04 VM on Proxmox), fronted by nginx (NPM) + a local DNS rewrite (AdGuard Home), with the public domain additionally gated behind a Tailscale-only access check (a Cloudflare Worker that blocks any request not arriving from the tailnet)
- Remote gateway URL configured: `https://hermes.alifdaniel.dpdns.org`
- Dashboard protected by its own username/password auth

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Settings → Gateway → Remote URL to a working, publicly reachable HTTPS Hermes gateway (reverse-proxied, valid Let's Encrypt cert, `nginx_online: true`)
2. Click "Save and reconnect" or "Test remote"
3. Observe: dialog reports "Remote gateway incomplete" / "Could not reach this gateway yet. Check the URL — the auth method will appear once it responds."
4. Boot log (separate error toast) shows a loop of:
   ```
   [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
   [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in. Open Settings → Gateway and click "Sign in", or switch back to Local.
   ```
   repeating indefinitely.

## Diagnostics performed (all on the same machine, same moment as the failure)

**Tailscale gate confirmed working correctly, not the cause:** the remote gateway domain is gated behind a Tailscale-only access check. Off-tailnet (mobile browser on cellular), it correctly shows the gate's own block page (real public IPv6, correct geolocation, `Status: Blocked · not on tailnet`). On-tailnet/local LAN, the identical URL loads normally in a plain browser or via `curl`. The desktop app fails specifically in the second case — on a device a plain browser confirms is correctly let through the gate.

**Server-side health, verified directly:**
```
$ curl -sv https://hermes.alifdaniel.dpdns.org/ --max-time 8
< HTTP/2 302
< server: openresty
< location: /login?next=%2F
```
`/health`, `/health/detailed`, `/api/health`, and both IPv4-only (`curl -4`) and IPv6-only (`curl -6`) requests all return the same healthy responses (`302` unauthenticated redirect, `401` on the auth-required API path).

Also confirmed via the reverse proxy's own admin API: host enabled, backend online (`nginx_online: true`), forwarding correctly, valid non-expired TLS cert, local DNS override present and enabled.

**Ruled out:** DNS resolution (correct via `dig`/`scutil --dns`), IPv4 vs IPv6, reverse proxy/TLS/cert state, VPN/overlay routing (same-machine `curl` succeeds over the identical path), backend process down (systemd service `active`, no crash in logs), stale config (re-verified after a full reboot of the remote gateway VM — same failure persists).

## What we could not determine
The Electron app's own reachability probe does not appear to log its actual failure reason anywhere:
- `desktop.log` — empty
- `errors.log` / `gui.log` — only contain the **local** Hermes backend's Python logs (`hermes_cli.web_server`, `tui_gateway.ws`), unrelated to the remote-URL check
- No toast/dialog surfaces the underlying fetch error (DNS? TLS? timeout? CORS? something Electron-specific like a proxy setting or cert store difference from the OS?)

## Ask
1. Could the "Test remote" / reachability probe surface its actual underlying error (exception message, timeout value, or HTTP client error) in the UI or in `desktop.log`, rather than a generic "Could not reach this gateway yet"?
2. Is there a known difference between how the Electron main process performs this fetch vs. the OS-level network stack (custom DNS resolver, bundled cert store, proxy auto-detection, etc.) that could explain success via `curl`/browser but failure in-app?
3. Any additional diagnostic steps or debug flags to enable more verbose Electron-side network logging for this specific check?

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop silently ends turns on non-retryable provider safety errors

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

Hermes Desktop silently ends an active turn when the provider returns a non-retryable safety/moderation error.

The backend logs the provider error, but Desktop shows no error banner, terminal assistant message, or explanation. The last successful tool card remains on screen and the composer simply returns to idle, making the turn look as if it stopped for no reason.

This reproduced twice in the same long-running Desktop workflow with `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.6-sol`. The report is about Hermes error delivery and lifecycle handling, not about bypassing or changing the provider's safety decision.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a tool-heavy conversation in Hermes Desktop using `openai-codex`.
2. Reach a request that the provider rejects with a non-retryable safety response such as:
   `This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.`
3. Observe the Desktop conversation after the backend classifies the error as non-retryable.
4. Inspect `agent.log`.

The exact user prompt and transcript are intentionally omitted. The observed workflow was a local code-quality review involving permission/lifecycle logic.

### Expected Behavior

Desktop should terminate the turn visibly and deterministically:

- Render a user-facing error message explaining that the provider blocked the request.
- Clear the running/busy state.
- Preserve a terminal failure event in the conversation/session history.
- Offer an obvious retry/rephrase path.
- Never leave the user with only the last tool card and no explanation.

The raw provider response may be sanitized, but the failure must not be silent.

### Actual Behavior

The backend logs a `Non-retryable client error` and stops the turn. Desktop renders no terminal error or assistant response. The composer eventually becomes idle and the user cannot tell whether the agent finished, crashed, or is still working.

The second occurrence happened during an automatic async-delegation continuation. The WebSocket remained connected until 41 seconds after the provider error, so the provider error—not the later disconnect—ended the work.

### Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop / terminal error handling)
- Other (Desktop structured gateway and error rendering)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (Desktop structured gateway)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not uploaded to avoid publishing profile configuration or conversation logs.
Sanitized environment and the relevant backend events are included below.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### Python Version

3.13.13

### Hermes Version

```text
Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
Observed local revision: 9b99b35b (+1 carried Desktop commit)
Recorded upstream revision: 7de55427
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
```

### Additional Logs / Traceback (sanitized)

First occurrence:

```text
11:59:37.565  WARNING agent.conversation_loop:
  API call failed (attempt 1/3)
  error_type=APIError
  provider=openai-codex
  model=gpt-5.6-sol
  summary=This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.

11:59:38.014  ERROR agent.conversation_loop:
  Non-retryable client error:
  This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.
```

Second occurrence after the session resumed through an internal async-delegation completion:

```text
12:12:45.780  API call #1 succeeded
12:13:04.835  API call #2 succeeded
12:13:44.976  API call #3 succeeded
12:13:47.940  write_file completed
12:14:16.941  WARNING API call failed (attempt 1/3), error_type=APIError,
              content flagged for possible cybersecurity risk
12:14:17.122  ERROR Non-retryable client error
12:14:58.239  WebSocket closed later (not the cause of the turn ending)
```

After each non-retryable error there was no visible Desktop error and no normal terminal `Turn ended`/assistant response for the user.

### Root Cause Analysis (inferred)

The non-retryable API-error path in the conversation loop logs the terminal failure, but the Desktop/TUI gateway path does not reliably emit or persist a user-visible terminal error event before the run exits.

This appears to be a general error-surfacing gap rather than an `openai-codex`-specific retry problem. Similar silent-failure UX was reported for different providers in #65847 and #56878, but those issues are closed and their root causes were MoA-specific.

### Proposed Fix

- Convert every terminal/non-retryable provider failure into a structured gateway error event before ending the run.
- Persist a sanitized failure marker in the session so reconnect/resume still shows why the turn ended.
- Ensure Desktop clears busy state only after receiving/rendering the terminal outcome.
- Provide a Retry/Rephrase action.
- Add an end-to-end regression test: successful model/tool activity followed by a non-retryable `APIError` must render a terminal error in Desktop and leave the composer usable.
- Cover both user-submitted turns and internal async-delegation continuation turns.

Related: #65847, #56878, #62708, #61042.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.body:
## Environment
- **Hermes Desktop**: v0.17.0 (Electron 40.10.2)
- **Hermes Agent**: v0.19.0
- **macOS**: 26.5.2 (25F84) on Apple Silicon (Mac16,9 / Mac Studio)
- **Crash type**: EXC_BREAKPOINT -> SIGTRAP

## Summary
The Electron shell crashes intermittently with a SIGTRAP in Chromium's c-ares DNS resolver. 4 crashes in 3 days:

| Date | Incident ID |
|------|-------------|
| July 20 18:36 | Hermes-2026-07-20-183628.ips |
| July 20 18:51 | Hermes-2026-07-20-185158.ips |
| July 22 18:34 | Hermes-2026-07-22-183402.ips |
| July 22 18:46 | Hermes-2026-07-22-184616.ips |

Always originates from CaresResolver::OnDNSCompleted -> ares_dns_rr_get_ttl receiving unexpected DNS response on macOS 26. This is an upstream Electron/Chromium issue.

Full crash log (July 22 18:46):
Exception Type: EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Faulting Thread: 0 CrBrowserMain
frames: ares_dns_rr_get_ttl -> CaresResolver::OnDNSCompleted -> Event loop -> uv_run -> ElectronMain

## Additional issue: GIL event loop stalls
Python agent core CPU-heavy operations block the event loop 30-300s, causing UI freeze (typing lag). Pattern: typing lag -> crash within minutes.

## Suggested fixes
1. Short term: Bump Electron to v41+ (past c-ares fix)
2. Medium term: Run agent core (hermes serve) as separate headless process from Electron shell

items.title: provider_model_ids swallows TypeError when plugin fetch_models omits base_url

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes_cli.models.provider_model_ids()` always calls:

```python
live = _p.fetch_models(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url or None)
```

Third-party model-provider plugins that override `fetch_models` with a narrower signature (e.g. only `api_key` / `timeout`) raise:

```text
TypeError: ... got an unexpected keyword argument 'base_url'
```

That exception is caught by the outer `except Exception` and treated as a failed live fetch, so the picker shows **0 models** (or only static fallbacks) for an otherwise healthy provider.

## Repro

1. Install a model-provider plugin whose `fetch_models` does not accept `base_url` (observed with OmniRoute before the plugin fix).
2. Authenticate the provider.
3. Open `/model` picker or call `provider_model_ids("<provider>", force_refresh=True)`.
4. Observe empty/missing live catalog despite a working `/v1/models` endpoint.

## Expected

- Prefer the full call with `base_url=...` (matches `ProviderProfile.fetch_models`).
- On `TypeError` only, retry once without `base_url` so older plugins still surface live models.
- Document that overrides must accept the base signature.

## Why not only fix the plugins?

Plugin fix is the correct long-term fix, but Hermes should degrade gracefully: a signature mismatch should not silently empty the picker for every third-party provider that lags the base API.

## Proposed change

```python
try:
    live = _p.fetch_models(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url or None)
except TypeError:
    live = _p.fetch_models(api_key=api_key)
```

Plus a short note in `providers/README.md` and unit tests for both narrow and full signatures.

items.title: [Bug]: Switching to DeepSeek fails with "messages[N].tool_calls: empty array" after context compaction

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

When switching the active model from Kimi to DeepSeek in a long conversation, the request fails with:HTTP 400: Invalid 'messages.tool_calls': empty array. Expected an array with minimum length 1, but got an empty array instead.
The issue appears to be caused by context compaction/reconstruction: when Hermes rebuilds the message array from compacted messages, at least one `assistant` message ends up with `tool_calls: []` instead of having the field omitted. DeepSeek's API rejects empty arrays, while Kimi's API accepts them.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Start a long conversation with many tool calls (enough to trigger context compaction — in my case ~940 messages with 637 compacted).
2. Let Hermes compact older messages.
3. Switch the active model from Kimi to DeepSeek.
4. DeepSeek request fails with the 400 error above.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should omit the `tool_calls` field entirely when there are no tool calls, or normalize `tool_calls: []` to `null` before sending to DeepSeek.

### Actual Behavior

`tool_calls: []` is sent, and DeepSeek returns 400.

### Environment

- Hermes version: Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream c6f9e0c7
- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- Provider where issue occurs: deepseek
- Provider where it works: kimi-coding

### Additional Context

This is a provider-compatibility issue in the context compaction path. It likely affects any conversation that crosses the compaction threshold and then switches to a strict OpenAI-compatible API (DeepSeek, or potentially others).

items.title: test-safety: kanban unit tests silently write to the real HERMES_HOME when hermetic isolation is bypassed
items.body:
## Summary

The kanban board/task unit tests isolate themselves only by setting `HERMES_HOME` to a temp dir via fixtures. If that isolation is ever bypassed, the tests silently write junk boards and junk tasks into the user's real `~/.hermes`. The existing live-system guard does not cover kanban writes, so nothing fails closed. This happened on a developer machine: a test run created 22 junk boards (exact fingerprints of the fixtures in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_boards.py`) and 2 junk tasks (`title="x"`, `assignee="worker"`, from `test_kanban_core_functionality.py`) on a real, active board.

## Mechanism

- The tests rely on `HERMES_HOME=tmp` set by `fresh_home` (`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_boards.py`), `kanban_home` (`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_core_functionality.py`), and the autouse `_hermetic_environment` (`tests/conftest.py`).
- `get_default_hermes_root()` reads `HERMES_HOME` live on every call (`hermes_constants.py`), so isolation holds ONLY while those fixtures apply.
- If the suite runs without the repo's `tests/conftest.py` (stale second checkout, wrong pytest rootdir, or the test functions invoked directly), `create_board()` / `create_task()` write to the real home, and `connect()` reads the real current-board pointer — so junk tasks land on a real live board.
- The header of `test_kanban_boards.py` already warns about the stale-clone case; the cache-clear line `hermes_constants._cached_default_hermes_root = None` in its fixture is a dead vestige (that attribute never existed).
- The live-system guard in `tests/conftest.py` blocks `os.kill` / `systemctl` / gateway-pid scans only. Kanban DB writes have no guard.

## Proposed fix (fail closed)

Add an autouse kanban write guard to `tests/conftest.py`, as a companion to the live-system guard:

1. After the `HERMES_HOME` redirect, assert `hermes_cli.kanban_db.kanban_home()` resolves under the per-test temp home.
2. Wrap `connect()` / `create_board()` so a target path outside the per-test `HERMES_HOME` raises instead of writing.

This converts a silent write-to-real-home into a loud test error, the same shape as the updater-restart hermeticity fix in #68988. Optionally also delete the dead cache-clear vestige.

I am happy to contribute the guard as a PR if this shape is acceptable.

items.title: Design: unpinned cron jobs should follow the global default model, not require re-snapshotting on every model change

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Context

This issue is filed by an AI agent (Hermes Agent) on behalf of a human operator. The agent collected the technical details and drafted this report; the human reviewed and authorized submission.

Related: #59031 (UX of drift guardrail), #68380 (bug in `action=update` that prevents self-remediation), #44585 (the original drift guardrail PR).

## Problem

The drift guardrail stores a `model_snapshot` at job creation time and blocks execution when the global default model has changed since creation. For **unpinned** jobs (no explicit `model`/`provider` override), this creates a paradox:

- The user's intent is "run on whatever the global default is" — that's why they left the job unpinned.
- The guardrail interprets the model change as unintended spend risk and hard-fails the job.
- The only documented remediation is to re-pin the job (which defeats the purpose of leaving it unpinned) or update the snapshot (which is just a pin with extra steps).

## Design question

There are already two mechanisms:

1. **Global default model** — the model the user configured as their standard.
2. **Per-job model pinning** — explicit `model`/`provider` on a job for when it should NOT follow the default.

These two mechanisms are sufficient. A job that is unpinned should always run on the global default, regardless of what the default was at creation time. The `model_snapshot` introduces a third state (effectively pinned-to-creation-time-model) that has no clear user intent behind it — no one asks for "run on whatever model was current when I created this job."

## Proposed behavior

- **Unpinned job** (`model=None`, `provider=None`): always uses the current global default. No snapshot comparison. No drift check. This is the "follow the default" contract.
- **Pinned job** (`model=X`, `provider=Y`): always uses X/Y. No drift check either — the user explicitly chose this model.
- **No `model_snapshot` field needed.** The snapshot adds complexity without serving a user intent that isn't already covered by the pin/unpin dichotomy.

The spend-protection concern (#44585) is valid but should be addressed differently: warn at `hermes config set model` time (as #59031 already proposes), rather than blocking unpinned jobs from running on the new default.

## Why this matters

In practice, every model change requires touching every unpinned job — either to re-pin or to re-snapshot. For operators who switch models regularly (testing, cost optimization, provider rotation), this is busywork that exists only because the snapshot mechanism conflates "created under model X" with "should run on model X." These are not the same thing.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent, self-hosted
- Cron scheduler with LLM-based jobs

items.title: [Feature]: Desktop GUI remote-agent mode — connect to a running server-side Hermes instance
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I run Hermes Agent in a Docker container on my NAS/server as a 24/7 gateway agent (connected to WeChat/Telegram/etc.). I want to use the Hermes Desktop GUI (macOS/Windows) to **connect to that remote agent** — see its sessions, journey timeline, memory graph, and interact with it through the desktop UI — rather than running a separate local Hermes instance.

Currently the Desktop app only runs its own local Hermes process. There is no way to point it at a remote agent and get the same experience (shared sessions, shared memory/skills, GUI panels showing the remote agent's state).

## Proposed Solution

Add a "remote mode" to Hermes Desktop that connects to a remote Hermes agent via its gateway API or a dedicated RPC protocol. This could work similarly to how VS Code Remote Development works — the Desktop app acts as a GUI frontend while the agent runs on the server.

Possible implementation approaches:
1. **Gateway API mode** — the remote agent exposes an HTTP/WebSocket API (e.g. via `hermes mcp serve` or a new `hermes api serve`), and the Desktop connects to it
2. **Shared-session protocol** — Desktop can set `HERMES_HOME` to a remote path and sync the session DB + memory via rsync/SMB/WebDAV
3. **SSH tunnel mode** — Desktop SSHes into the remote host, forwards Hermes data, and renders the GUI locally

Key features needed:
- View and interact with the remote agent's sessions from the Desktop
- See the journey timeline / memory graph / star map of the remote agent
- Terminal pane that executes on the remote host (SSH backend already exists)
- A "Connect to Remote..." dialog in the Desktop UI

## Alternatives Considered

1. **CIFS/SMB mount** — mount the container data dir locally and set HERMES_HOME — works for file sharing but has concurrency issues and no live session viewing
2. **SSH + CLI** — just SSH in and run `hermes chat` in terminal — works but misses all the GUI niceties (journey, memory graph, panes, plugins)
3. **Message platforms** — already working (WeChat/Telegram gateway), but no access to Desktop-specific visualizations (journey timeline, star map)

The proposed solution is better because it gives Desktop users the full GUI experience for server-side agents.

## Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement
New tool / CLI improvement

## Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

items.title: CLI: Separate tool calling from reasoning/thinking blocks for better readability

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Issue Overview

In the CLI version, tool calling should be separated from the reasoning/thinking section to improve user experience.

## Current Situation

Currently, tool calls appear inside the thinking/reasoning block in the CLI output. This makes it harder for users to distinguish between:
- The model's reasoning/thinking process
- Actual tool function calls and their inputs/outputs

## Proposed Solution

**Separate tool calling into its own section** rather than nesting them within the thinking blocks.

### Benefits

✅ **Improved readability** - Users can easily distinguish between reasoning and actions
✅ **Clearer execution flow** - The sequence of thought → action → result becomes more apparent
✅ **Better debugging** - Tool calls are easier to identify and trace
✅ **Cleaner output** - Reduces visual clutter in the CLI interface

### Example Structure (Before vs After)

**Current format:**
```
<thinking>
I should call the browser_navigate tool to load this page.
</thinking>
<tool_call>browser_navigate(url="...")</tool_call>
```

**Proposed format:**
```
<thinking>
I need to navigate to this URL to begin my task.
</thinking>

--- TOOL CALL SECTION ---
browser_navigate(url="https://example.com")

--- RESULTS ---
Page loaded successfully
```

## Implementation Notes

- This change should maintain backward compatibility with other interfaces (web, API)
- The CLI parser needs to handle both the new and potentially legacy format during transition
- Documentation updates will be needed for users

Let me know if you'd like to discuss specific implementation details or if there are concerns about this approach!

items.body:
### Bug Description

When archiving sessions in Hermes Desktop, there is no way to view the list of archived sessions or restore them. The documentation states that archived sessions "can be unarchived from the Desktop/Dashboard session list," but the Desktop UI has no mechanism to show archived sessions or unarchive them.

The only toggle in the Desktop sidebar switches between "Projects" and "Sessions" — there is no "Show Archived" filter, no archived sessions view, and no unarchive action available.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop
2. In the Sessions view, click the `⋮` menu on any session → **Archive**
3. The session disappears from the list (as expected — it's now archived)
4. Try to find the archived session:
   - No "Show Archived" toggle or filter exists in the sidebar
   - No archived sessions view exists in the Desktop app
   - The session is hidden from `hermes sessions list` and `/resume`
   - The Web Dashboard's Sessions page shows an "archived count" in the stats bar, but has no documented unarchive action

### Expected Behavior

There should be a way to:
1. **View** archived sessions (a filter/toggle to show them in the session list)
2. **Restore** them (an "Unarchive" or "Restore" action on archived sessions)
The documentation at https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions explicitly states: "Archived sessions are hidden from `hermes sessions list` and `/resume` but remain in the database and can be unarchived from the Desktop/Dashboard session list." This functionality is missing from the current Desktop UI.

### Actual Behavior

Archived sessions are permanently hidden from the Desktop UI with no way to restore them through the app. They remain in the SQLite database (`~/.hermes/state.db`) with `archived = 1`, but there is no UI path to unarchive them.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
NOT SHARING DUE TO PRIVACY CONCERNS
```

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 2b6897f9

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

From code investigation:
1. **Desktop** archives sessions via `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `{ archived: true }` (in `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`)
2. The web server handles this in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` → calls `db.set_session_archived()` in `hermes_state.py`
3. Archived sessions are filtered out in the session list queries (they're hidden by default)
4. The Desktop session list component has no UI to toggle showing archived sessions or to unarchive them
5. The Web Dashboard's Sessions page (documented at `website/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard.md`) lists rename, export, prune, and delete actions but no unarchive action
Related issues:
- #48843 — Feature: Bulk Archive Sessions in Desktop GUI (open, P3)
- #47168 — feat(tui_gateway): add session.archive RPC to match desktop parity (open, P3)
- #44449 — Archive path still 400s after #44138 (closed as not planned)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add an "Archived" filter toggle to the Desktop session list sidebar (similar to how it switches between Projects and Sessions), and add an "Unarchive" action to the `⋮` menu for archived sessions. The Web Dashboard should also include an unarchive action on its Sessions page.

items.title: Agent scatters generated artifacts across random directories instead of a configured output path

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Bug Description

When agents generate artifacts (architecture diagrams, posters, screenshots, SVGs, etc.), the output files end up scattered across random directories — `~/Downloads/`, the gateway cwd (`~/.hermes/`), or wherever the agent happened to be — instead of respecting a configured working directory.

This means users need to manually hunt down and move files after every agent interaction.

## Evidence

From a single morning session (default agent, session `20260722_052030_d3216baf`), the following artifacts were left in `~/Downloads/`:

```
~/Downloads/clawchat-poster.png       (197 KB)
~/Downloads/clawchat-poster-v2.png    (162 KB)
~/Downloads/clawchat-poster-v3.png    (165 KB)
~/Downloads/image_001.jpg             (169 KB)
~/Downloads/clawchat-architecture.html           (21 KB)
~/Downloads/clawchat-architecture-v2.svg         (12 KB)
~/Downloads/clawchat-architecture.excalidraw     (14 KB)
```

None of these were placed in the configured working directory.

## Root Causes

### 1. No unified artifact output path

Hermes has `terminal.cwd` for shell commands, but no `artifacts.output_dir` or similar config that `write_file` / `vision_analyze` / skill outputs can respect. Each tool falls back to its own default:

| Tool / Skill | Default output location |
|---|---|
| `write_file` (relative path) | Resolves against `TERMINAL_CWD` → falls back to gateway process cwd (`~/.hermes/`) |
| `architecture-diagram` skill | "default to the current working directory" (ambiguous) |
| `mmx image generate` | Outputs to cwd |
| `screencapture` | Outputs to cwd |
| `browser_vision` screenshot | `~/.hermes/cache/screenshots/` (internal, OK) |

### 2. Skills hardcode ambiguous defaults

The `architecture-diagram` skill says:
> Save diagrams to a user-specified path, or default to the current working directory: `./[project-name]-architecture.html`

"Current working directory" for the default gateway is `~/.hermes/` — but agents end up writing to `~/Downloads/` because they choose their own path.

### 3. Profile isolation doesn't extend to file output

The `dev` profile has `terminal.cwd: /Users/zeyuan/dev` configured, but generated artifacts still end up in `~/Downloads/` because the agent doesn't automatically route `write_file` calls through the configured working directory.

## Expected Behavior

1. A single `artifacts.output_dir` config that ALL artifact-generating tools respect
2. `write_file` with relative paths should resolve against the configured output directory
3. Skills that generate files should default to the configured output directory
4. Each profile should have its own artifact output directory

## Proposed Solution

Add an `artifacts.output_dir` config option:

```yaml
artifacts:
  output_dir: /Users/zeyuan/dev/artifacts  # default: terminal.cwd or ~/.hermes/output/
```

Then have `write_file`, `architecture-diagram`, `excalidraw`, and other artifact-producing tools/skills resolve relative paths against this directory.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest
- macOS 26.4.1
- Both `dev` and `default` profiles affected
- Default gateway cwd: `~/.hermes/` (but artifacts go to `~/Downloads/`)

items.title: Feature: AC Power Watchdog — detect & alert on host power loss/recovery
items.body:
## Description

A lightweight, zero-dependency bash script that monitors the host machine's AC power status via `/sys/class/power_supply/AC/online` and sends Telegram alerts when power is lost or restored.

## Why

Hermes Agent often runs on headless Linux machines (VPS, home servers, laptops used as servers) where users want to know if the power cable is disconnected — especially before the battery drains.

## How it works

- Checks `/sys/class/power_supply/AC/online` (or `ADP1` as fallback)
- Maintains a persistent state file (`.ac_power_state`) to track transitions
- Sends different alerts for power loss (`⚠️`) and recovery (`✅`)
- Includes battery percentage and estimated remaining time
- **Zero dependencies**: pure bash, no Python, no Node.js
- Designed to run as a `no_agent=true` cron job (no LLM tokens consumed)

## Example output

```
⚠️ ALIMENTATION COUPÉE — 22/07/2026 11:50
🔌 Secteur débranché !
🔋 Batterie : 35%
⏳ Autonomie estimée : ~2h30m
→ Rebranche vite !
```

## Implementation

The script is deployed as a cron job running every minute via Hermes cron scheduler with `no_agent=true`. Available as a ready-to-use script if the team is interested.

## Additional context

Currently using this in production on my Hermes Agent instance — works reliably with Snap Chromium, standalone Chromium, and headless environments. No external APIs, no LLM calls, ~50 lines of bash.

### Bug Description

After updating to Hermes Agent v0.19.0, the Telegram post-restart notification stopped arriving.

The /restart command acknowledgement is delivered successfully, the gateway restarts normally, and the Telegram bot responds to messages afterward. However, the expected post-restart “back online” notification is never delivered.

The gateway log reported:

Restart notification to telegram:<chat_id> was not delivered: send_path_degraded

This behavior worked before the v0.19.0 update.

Additional live verification:

Before the local readiness patch:
- Gateway became operational at 02:05:33
- Restart notification attempted at 02:05:34
- Result: not delivered: send_path_degraded

After applying a local patch that waits on Telegram's existing
_polling_progress_event with a bounded timeout:
- Gateway became operational at 02:18:29
- Restart notification delivered successfully at 02:18:38

Relevant log lines:

2026-07-22 02:05:34,284 WARNING gateway.run:
Restart notification to telegram:<chat_id> was not delivered: send_path_degraded

2026-07-22 02:18:38,060 INFO gateway.run:
Sent restart notification to telegram:<chat_id>

This suggests the v0.19.0 faster cold-start path reaches the restart-notification send before Telegram's polling path is ready.

1f3aa26b53
fix(gateway): wait on Telegram post-boot readiness before sending restart notification

### Actual Behavior

The gateway restarts and Telegram becomes functional, but the post-restart notification is lost. The log reports send_path_degraded during the notification attempt.

items.title: Windows: TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath layout tests compare native-separator paths against forward-slash literals

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
**Version:** v2026.7.20 (also present on current `main`)
**Platform:** Windows 11, Python 3.11, pytest run from a native Windows checkout

## Summary

`tests/tools/test_local_env_windows_msys.py::TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath::test_derives_dirs_from_portablegit_layout` and `::test_derives_dirs_from_mingit_usr_bin_layout` fail on any Windows checkout.

Both tests assert forward-slash string literals (e.g. `"/pg/usr/bin"`) against the output of `_git_bash_bin_dirs()`, but that function builds its candidate dirs with `os.path.join`, which emits native separators. On Windows the derived dirs come back as mixed-separator strings like `/pg\usr\bin`, so the `in` assertions fail:

```
AssertionError: assert '/pg/usr/bin' in ['\\pg\\mingw64\\bin', '\\pg\\usr\\bin', '\\pg\\bin']
```

Note the irony: these are the *Windows MSYS* tests, but they only pass on POSIX hosts.

The test class already anticipates this problem for `isdir` — its own `_fake_isdir` helper normalizes separators before comparing (`existing = {e.replace("\\", "/") for e in existing}`). The assertions just need the same treatment on the output side.

## Reproduction

On any Windows machine:

```
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_local_env_windows_msys.py::TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath -x
```

## Suggested fix

Mirror `_fake_isdir`'s normalization with a small helper and wrap the two calls:

```diff
--- a/tests/tools/test_local_env_windows_msys.py
+++ b/tests/tools/test_local_env_windows_msys.py
@@ -341,6 +341,13 @@ class TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath:
         existing = {e.replace("\\", "/") for e in existing}
         return lambda p: p.replace("\\", "/") in existing
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _norm(dirs):
+        # os.path.join emits native separators, so on Windows the derived
+        # dirs mix the fixture's "/" root with "\" joins; compare
+        # separator-agnostically, like _fake_isdir.
+        return [d.replace("\\", "/") for d in dirs]
+
     def test_derives_dirs_from_portablegit_layout(self, monkeypatch):
         monkeypatch.setattr(local_mod, "_IS_WINDOWS", True)
         monkeypatch.setattr(local_mod, "_git_bash_bin_dirs_cache", None)
@@ -348,7 +355,7 @@ class TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath:
         existing = {"/pg/mingw64/bin", "/pg/usr/bin", "/pg/bin"}
         monkeypatch.setattr(local_mod.os.path, "isdir", self._fake_isdir(existing))
 
-        dirs = _git_bash_bin_dirs()
+        dirs = self._norm(_git_bash_bin_dirs())
 
         # usr/bin is the load-bearing coreutils dir; mingw64 precedes it.
         assert "/pg/usr/bin" in dirs
@@ -363,7 +370,7 @@ class TestGitBashCoreutilsOnPath:
         existing = {"/mg/usr/bin", "/mg/mingw64/bin"}
         monkeypatch.setattr(local_mod.os.path, "isdir", self._fake_isdir(existing))
 
-        dirs = _git_bash_bin_dirs()
+        dirs = self._norm(_git_bash_bin_dirs())
 
         # MinGit ships bash under usr\bin; root must still resolve to /mg.
         assert "/mg/usr/bin" in dirs
```

Verified locally on Windows 11: both tests pass with this change, and the change is a no-op on POSIX.

items.title: Windows: TestStartupTimeoutPhaseDetail's Event.wait patch never takes — real 30s wait races pytest-timeout and can kill the whole pytest process

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
**Version:** v2026.7.20 (also present on current `main`; class added in de4310c8f / #58801)
**Platform:** Windows 11, Python 3.11, pytest with the repo's 30s timeout cap

## Summary

Both tests in `tests/tools/test_computer_use.py::TestStartupTimeoutPhaseDetail` patch `wait` on a **pre-made** event instance:

```python
with _patch.object(session._ready_event, "wait", return_value=False), \
```

But `_CuaDriverSession._start_lifecycle_locked()` (`tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py`, ~line 786) reassigns a **fresh** event before ever waiting:

```python
self._ready_event = threading.Event()
```

so the patched instance is discarded and the test performs the real 30-second `wait()`. That races the repo's 30s pytest-timeout cap.

On Linux (`--timeout-method=signal`) this shows up as two tests that each burn ~30s and pass or fail by coin flip. On Windows the consequence is much worse: signal-based timeouts don't work there, so pytest-timeout falls back to `--timeout-method=thread` (upstream's own documented addopts fallback), and the thread method **kills the entire pytest process** when the cap fires — the whole `tests/tools` run aborts at this file, taking every not-yet-run test with it.

## Reproduction

On Windows:

```
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_computer_use.py::TestStartupTimeoutPhaseDetail --timeout=30 --timeout-method=thread
```

The run wedges ~30s in the real `_ready_event.wait()`, then pytest-timeout hard-kills the process.

## Suggested fix

Patch the module's `Event` factory instead of the doomed instance, so the event created inside `_start_lifecycle_locked()` is the stub:

```diff
--- a/tests/tools/test_computer_use.py
+++ b/tests/tools/test_computer_use.py
@@ -3803,7 +3803,15 @@ class TestStartupTimeoutPhaseDetail:
 
         import asyncio
         from unittest.mock import patch as _patch
-        with _patch.object(session._ready_event, "wait", return_value=False), \
```

items.title: multiplex_profiles: cron jobs registered in a secondary profile's store never fire — the single gateway only runs the default profile's ticker

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
Deployment: v2026.7.7.2 (0.18.2), Docker, s6-supervised gateway,
`multiplex_profiles: true`, secondary profile `home-ops` owning a Telegram
adapter.

The multiplexer serves the secondary profile's messaging lanes (config,
SOUL, model, memory all scope correctly), but the cron subsystem does not
follow: the gateway process starts ONE `InProcessCronScheduler` bound to the
process-global `HERMES_HOME`, so only `/opt/data/cron/jobs.json` is ticked.
A job registered from a secondary-profile session lands in
`<profile>/cron/jobs.json`, reports a valid `next_run_at` — and never runs.
Our secondary profile's `cron/ticker_heartbeat` had not advanced in 15 days
while the default profile's beat every minute.

The agent-facing surface actively misleads here: the profile-scoped cronjob
tool accepts the registration, validates the script path against the
profile's `scripts/` dir, and shows the job as `scheduled` with a concrete
`next_run_at`. Nothing warns that no ticker owns that store.

Starting a second gateway for the profile is (correctly) refused by
`_guard_named_profile_under_multiplexer` — it would double-bind the
messaging platforms. So under multiplexing there is no supported way to get
a secondary profile's cron jobs to fire.

Suggestion: when `multiplex_profiles` is on, the default gateway should
start a scheduler (or tick pass) per served profile — mirroring how config
resolution already works per adapter-owning profile. Interim alternatives:
have the cronjob tool refuse/warn on registration into a store no ticker
owns, and surface per-profile ticker liveness in `hermes doctor`.

Workaround we run: duplicate the job as a no-agent script job in the
default profile's store, with a wrapper under the default `scripts/` dir
exec'ing the (self-anchored) profile script.

items.title: v2026.7.20 regression for Docker multiplex deployments: load_gateway_config_for_runner reloads config in the default profile's secret scope, silently dropping platform env vars set via container environment — api_server no longer starts

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
Deployment: Docker (s6 image), `multiplex_profiles: true`, api_server
platform enabled the documented way for containers — compose
`environment: API_SERVER_ENABLED/HOST/PORT/CORS_ORIGINS` — working on
v2026.7.7.2.

After the bump to v2026.7.20, the gateway starts with
"Gateway running with 1 platform(s)" (only the secondary profile's
Telegram adapter): the api_server platform is gone, :8642 dead, the
container healthcheck fails. No warning or error anywhere — the platform
is simply absent.

Cause: `gateway/run.py: load_gateway_config_for_runner()` (the #64674
fix) now reloads gateway config inside the default profile's
`_profile_runtime_scope`, whose secret scope reads the profile's `.env`
file and deliberately never falls through to process `os.environ`. Any
platform configured only via container env therefore vanishes from the
runner's view. Diagnosis contrast that confirmed it on our box:
`load_gateway_config()` (unscoped) shows `API_SERVER enabled: True`,
`load_gateway_config_for_runner()` shows no enabled platform in the
default scope.

Workaround: move `API_SERVER_*` (and any other platform env) into the
default profile's `.env` file. Works, but nothing documents that the
compose `environment:` block stopped being authoritative for platform
enablement in multiplex mode — and the same vars are still honored
elsewhere (e.g. the s6 dashboard service reads process env), which makes
the split hard to discover.

Suggestions (any subset):

- fall through to process env in the scoped reload for non-secret
  platform config (keep the secret isolation for credentials), or
- log a WARNING at startup when process env carries platform-enabling
  vars that the scoped reload dropped (name them), or
- document the new precedence for container deployments (platform env
  belongs in the profile `.env`, not the container environment).
