items.title: [Bug]: cron job `workdir` is applied as global process cwd and leaks into gateway sessions created during the run

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

### Summary

A cron job with a `workdir` set changes the working directory for the whole gateway
process, not just its own session. Any interactive (Signal/Telegram/etc.) session created
**while that cron job is running** inherits the cron job's `workdir` as its cwd, and
therefore auto-loads that directory's `AGENTS.md` into its system prompt as
`# Project Context — The following project context files have been loaded and should be
followed`.

The interactive session then follows the cron job's instructions instead of the user's
request. The effect is transient — the cwd is restored when the cron run ends — so it
presents as a rare, hard-to-reproduce race rather than a persistent misconfiguration.

### Version

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream `9de9c25f`
- Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, Signal gateway, local Ollama provider

### Impact

An interactive session can silently execute an unrelated scheduled task, including its
side effects (this instance sent an unrequested duplicate email and raced another session
on a shared file). It also means arbitrary `AGENTS.md` content becomes binding instructions
for a session the user believes is a plain chat.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a cron job with a `workdir` pointing at a directory containing an `AGENTS.md`
   whose body is a task (the documented pattern — `workdir` is described as "run in a
   specific directory with its AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md loaded"):

   ```
   hermes cron edit <id> --workdir /path/to/some-brief   # some-brief/AGENTS.md = "Produce a X brief..."
   ```

2. Wait for the job to fire. While it is still running, send an unrelated message from a
   messaging gateway (Signal) that starts a **new** session.

3. Inspect the new session's stored system prompt:

   ```sql
   select system_prompt from sessions where id = '<new_session_id>';
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The interactive session's cwd is independent of any concurrently running cron job. Its
system prompt contains no `# Project Context` from the cron job's `workdir`.

### Actual Behavior

The interactive session's system prompt contains:

```
Current working directory: /path/to/some-brief

# Project Context

The following project context files have been loaded and should be followed:

## AGENTS.md

# Daily Home + Server Brief
Produce a SHORT home + server brief...
```

…and the agent then performs the cron job's task instead of answering the user.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Sorry I ran this, but it exposes things I don't want to share.
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 9de9c25f

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Scope the cron job's working directory (and its project-context discovery) to that job's
session rather than mutating process-global state — e.g. carry cwd on the session/turn
context, or run the cron turn in a subprocess, instead of `chdir()` on the gateway process.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Windows subprocess reader thread crashes on non-UTF-8 output

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description
On Windows, the OpenAI SDK generates platform headers by calling `platform.platform()`. Python then follows:

```text
platform.platform()
→ platform.win32_ver()
→ platform._syscmd_ver()
→ subprocess.check_output("ver", text=True, shell=True)
→ subprocess.Popen._readerthread
```

## Observed Symptom
The subprocess reader thread can raise:

```text
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 in position 27: invalid continuation byte
```

The main process may still complete successfully (`completed: true`, exit code `0`).

## Attribution
The failure boundary is `platform._syscmd_ver()`, reached from the OpenAI SDK platform-header path. It is not attributed to Ollama, project-memory persistence, context compression, or Hermes `_git_stdout()`.

The exact source of byte `0xe9` remains context-dependent. A direct binary replay of `ver` on this machine produced ASCII-only output, so the issue may depend on active code page, locale, UTF-8 mode, shell state, or concurrent process context.

## Risk
- partial loss of subprocess diagnostics;
- reader thread termination;
- secondary errors potentially masked;
- smoke-test results that appear successful while diagnostic output was lost.

## Environment Observed
- OS: Windows 10
- Python: 3.11.0
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
- `locale.getencoding()`: `cp1252`
- `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`: `utf-8` in UTF-8 mode, `cp1252` otherwise

## Expected Behavior
Platform-header generation should not terminate a subprocess reader thread when Windows returns output that cannot be decoded using the selected text-stream encoding.

## Scope
Investigate the OpenAI SDK / Python `platform._syscmd_ver()` boundary independently from project-memory orchestration and compression-quality work. Avoid global monkeypatches of `subprocess`; prefer a narrowly scoped, supported fix or an upgrade if available.

items.title: Desktop: pinned sessions vanish after upgrade or cache clear (pinned state stored in ephemeral renderer localStorage, not backend)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
Description
Desktop pinned sessions (sidebar → Pin to top) disappear after:

App upgrade (swap+relaunch)
Cache cleanup (deleting Session Storage/ or Local Storage/leveldb)
Any renderer restart that invalidates localStorage
Root Cause
Pinned session IDs are stored only in the renderer's localStorage (Electron LevelDB). This storage is:

Ephemeral — cleared on upgrade, cache reset, or any leveldb corruption
Renderer-scoped — not shared across connections or profiles
Silent on failure — when the sidebar rebuilds and can't find a pinned ID in the session DB, it drops the pin without warning
The backend sessions table in state.db already tracks sessions with fields like id, title, started_at, ended_at, message_count, and source. Adding a pinned field there would give pinning the same durability as every other session property.

Evidence
From the project's own AGENTS.md (apps/desktop/):

"The backend is authoritative for anything another Hermes surface can also change. Treat the renderer's copy as a cache of that truth."

The current implementation violates this principle — pinned state is authoritative in the renderer's cache with no backend persistence.

Expected Behavior
sessions table in state.db gains a pinned (boolean) or pinned_at (timestamp) column
Pin/unpin actions are persisted via a lightweight backend API call
On sidebar load, pinned sessions are fetched from the authoritative backend source
Renderer may cache the list for responsiveness, but treats it as a cache that can be refreshed
Suggested Implementation
Minimal scope:

Add pinned column to sessions table (migration, nullable, default NULL)
Expose a simple PATCH /sessions/:id/pin / DELETE /sessions/:id/pin endpoint from the gateway (or extend existing session API)
Renderer uses these endpoints on pin/unpin, and fetches pinned-first on sidebar load
Environment
Hermes Desktop (Electron app)
macOS
Happens on every upgrade (swap+relaunch), cache clear, and any localStorage invalidation

items.title: [Bug]: Doubao seed-2-1 streaming tool_call JSON truncated — write_file silently fails

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Bug Description

Doubao seed-2-1 series (both pro and turbo) streams tool_call JSON that is **truncated mid-stream** when the `write_file` content parameter exceeds ~1000 characters (HTML generation). Hermes' stream parser receives incomplete JSON → substitutes `{}` → tool invocation silently fails → agent retries → user perceives agent as "unresponsive."

This is NOT the same as #33402 (Gemini parallel tool-call concatenation). This is a **single tool_call with a large argument** whose JSON stream ends before the closing `}`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes to use `doubao-seed-2-1-turbo-260628` via Volcengine Ark endpoint
2. Ask the agent to create an HTML file via `write_file` with substantial content (>1000 chars)
3. Observe agent.log:

```
WARNING agent.message_sanitization: Unrepairable tool_call arguments for write_file — replaced with empty object
(was: {"path": "/path/to/file.html", "content": "<!DOCTYPE html>...)
```

4. Cumulative: 30+ occurrences in a single session
5. Same prompt works correctly with `doubao-seed-2-0-pro-260215`

## Root Cause

**Model side:** Doubao seed-2-1 streaming output truncates nested JSON in tool_call arguments at unpredictable boundaries.

**Hermes side:** `chat_completion_helpers.py` L2618 hardcodes `stream=True` for all providers. There is no configuration path to request non-streaming mode for providers known to have streaming tool_call issues.

## Evidence

Direct API test (bypassing Hermes):

```
❌ seed-2-1 + stream=true → JSON truncated
✅ seed-2-1 + stream=false → JSON complete
✅ seed-2-0-pro + stream=true → JSON complete
```

## Proposed Fix

Add a provider-level `stream: false` configuration that Hermes respects at `chat_completion_helpers.py` L2618, allowing fallback to non-streaming mode for providers with known streaming tool_call quality issues.

```yaml
providers:
  volcengine:
    stream: false  # Hermes should honor this
```

Currently this config key is silently ignored because `stream=True` is hardcoded in the stream_kwargs construction.

## Cross-reference

Catalogued as **CF-0119** in the Channel Fracture Registry.

items.title: [Security] Custom endpoint API key stored in plaintext in config.yaml

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Problem

When saving a custom provider through the Desktop settings UI (Settings → Providers → Custom Endpoints → Edit Endpoint), the API key is stored as plaintext in `config.yaml`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop → Settings → Providers → Custom Endpoints → Edit Endpoint
2. Fill in the provider details (name, base URL, model, API key)
3. Save
4. Open `config.yaml`
5. Check `providers.<provider-id>.api_key` — the key is in **plaintext**

## Code-Level Confirmation

The issue is in `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, function `_write_custom_endpoint()`:

```python
# Lines 7387-7388: API key stored directly in plaintext
if body.api_key is not None and body.api_key.strip():
    entry["api_key"] = body.api_key.strip()
```

```python
# Lines 7397-7398: If "make default" is checked, the key is also copied to model section
if entry.get("api_key") and isinstance(cfg["model"], dict):
    cfg["model"]["api_key"] = entry["api_key"]
```

```python
# Line 7419: Entire config (with plaintext key) is written to config.yaml
save_config(cfg)
```

`save_config()` → `atomic_yaml_write()` → `yaml.dump()` → plaintext YAML. No encryption, no masking, no `.env` redirection.

## Expected vs Actual Behavior

Standard providers use `key_env` to reference an environment variable, keeping the actual key in `.env`:

```yaml
providers:
  <standard-provider>:
    key_env: PROVIDER_API_KEY    # ✅ references env var
```

Custom endpoints bypass this and store the raw key:

```yaml
providers:
  <custom-provider-id>:
    api_key: <plaintext>    # ❌ plaintext in config.yaml
```

## Verification

1. **Config file check** — Entered a key via UI, confirmed it appears in plaintext in `config.yaml`
2. **Code analysis** — Traced the full save path, confirmed no encryption/masking step
3. **Post-update retest** — Issue persists after applying the latest Hermes update

## Note

The Desktop UI masks the key in the input field, so users have no indication that it will be persisted in plaintext.

   ```yaml
   fallback_providers:
     - base_url: https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1

   ```

2. Open Hermes Desktop

Each model entry should display a clean, human-readable name (e.g., "Step Explore", "Step 3.5 Flash").

The model picker appears to be rendering the raw JSON array of model IDs as a single string entry, rather than iterating over the array and creating individual entries for each model. ## Summary

`PUT /api/memory/providers/honcho/config` fails to persist submitted field values when the first save merges into the resolved *global* Honcho config (no profile-local file yet). Pre-existing unit test fails on a clean checkout of `main` at `17155e3ae` (v0.19.0), no local modifications to the Honcho plugin or the test.

## Reproduction

```
pytest "tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_put_honcho_first_save_merges_into_resolved_config" -q
```

Test setup: seeds `~/.honcho/config.json` with `{"baseUrl": "https://kept.example", "hosts": {"hermes": {"workspace": "kept"}}}`, then `PUT`s `{"values": {"peerName": "eri"}}` to `/api/memory/providers/honcho/config?surface=declared`.

## Observed failure

```
AssertionError: assert {'workspace': 'kept'} == {'peerName': 'eri', 'workspace': 'kept'}
```

The response is `200 OK` and `baseUrl` is correctly preserved, but the submitted `peerName` never lands in `hosts.hermes` — the host block comes back with only the pre-existing `workspace` key, as if the merge silently dropped the new field (or wrote it somewhere else — the profile-local `honcho.json` was confirmed absent per the test's other assertion, so it isn't just landing there instead).

## Environment

- `hermes-agent` 0.19.0, commit `17155e3ae` (clean checkout, no local changes)
- Windows 11, Python 3.11 (venv)

## Impact

A user configuring Honcho memory for the first time (no pre-existing profile-local config) via the dashboard would have their submitted fields (e.g. `peerName`) silently discarded on save, while the request still reports success.

Found incidentally while reapplying local `hermes update` autostash conflicts in an unrelated area (credential pool); filing separately since it doesn't touch anything I changed.

items.title: Bug: Approval system is blind to destructive PowerShell / Windows paths on Windows hosts

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
# Bug: Approval system is blind to destructive PowerShell / Windows paths on Windows hosts

**Component:** `tools/approval.py` (dangerous-command approval) · **Severity:** High (silent security bypass on Windows)
**Related:** #5528 (configurable patterns) · **Analogue:** Claude Code Case 4, fixed in 2.1.162

## Summary
On Windows native (PowerShell), Hermes' `DANGEROUS_PATTERNS` are POSIX/Unix-shaped and case-sensitive, so
destructive Windows commands and Windows paths never match the guardrail and pass approval **silently**. This is
the same failure class as Claude Code's Windows permission bug (backslash + case-variant rules failing to match →
loop/false-negative, fixed 2.1.162).

## Root cause
`_normalize_command_for_detection()` applies **NFKC** normalization, but NFKC only collapses *glyph* lookalikes
(fullwidth slashes, mathematical-bold letters). It does **not**:
- convert `\` → `/` (Windows path separator),
- lowercase (Windows FS is case-insensitive),
- expand `~` / `%USERPROFILE%` to the resolved profile path.

The documented dangerous targets (`/etc/`, `~/.ssh/`, `~/.hermes/.env`) are all POSIX paths, so they never match
the Windows equivalents (`C:\Users\asad1\.ssh`, `C:\Users\asad1\AppData\Local\hermes\.env`, `D:\agency\...`).

## Concrete gaps (no destructive command was executed to verify — derived from the documented mechanism)
1. **Path separators not normalized** — `del C:\Windows\...` / `Remove-Item C:\Users\asad1\.ssh` never match `/etc/`.
2. **Case-sensitivity** — `rm -RF`, `GIT PUSH --FORCE`, `Remove-Item` won't match lowercase patterns.
3. **Shell drift** — PowerShell equivalents aren't in the set:
   - `rm -rf` → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` (aliases: `rm`/`del`/`rd`)
   - `curl … | sh` → `iwr … | iex` (Invoke-WebRequest | Invoke-Expression)
   - `kill -9 -1` / `pkill` → `Stop-Process -Force` / `taskkill /F`
   - `chmod 777` → `icacls … /grant Everyone:(F)`
   - `dd` → `diskpart` / `Format-Volume`
4. **Home-dir expansion** — `~` ≠ `C:\Users\asad1`.
5. **Drive-letter / UNC** — `C:`, `D:`, `\\server\share` forms uncovered.

## Proposed fix (minimum viable)
**A.** In `_normalize_command_for_detection()`, on Windows: replace `\` → `/`, lowercase, expand `~`/`%USERPROFILE%`/`$HOME` to the profile path. Closes gaps 1/2/4 in one step — mirrors how Claude fixed Case 4 (normalize rule paths, don't widen patterns).

**B.** Add a `DANGEROUS_PATTERNS_WIN` tier (gated to `local`/`ssh` backends on Windows), each pattern requiring the destructive flag so plain `rm tmp/file` still does NOT prompt:
- `(?i)\b(remove-item|rm|del|rd)\b.*?(-recurse|-r\b|-force|-f\b|/s|/q)`
- `(?i)\b(iwr|invoke-webrequest|curl|wget)\b.*?(\|\s*iex|\|\s*invoke-expression)`
- `(?i)\b(stop-process|taskkill)\b.*?(-force|/f)`
- `(?i)\b(format-volume|diskpart)\b`
- `(?i)icacls\b.*?(everyone|\*)\s*:\(f\)`
- `(?i)c:/users/[^/]+/\.ssh` · `(?i)c:/users/[^/]+/appdata/local/hermes/\.env` · `(?i)d:/agency/[^/]*\.env`

**C.** (follow-up, see #5528) make the pattern lists user-editable from `~/.hermes/config.yaml` so operators can add site-specific Windows rules without forking.

## Suggested tests (`tests/test_approval_windows.py`, skipped off-Windows)
- `Remove-Item D:/agency/test -Recurse -Force` → dangerous
- `rm -RF D:/agency/test` → dangerous (case + alias)
- `del C:\Users\asad1\.ssh\id_rsa` → dangerous (backslash normalized)
- `iwr https://x | iex` → dangerous
- `format-volume X:` → dangerous
- `rm tmp/file` → NOT dangerous · `ls C:\Users` → NOT dangerous

## Why it matters
On a Windows host this is a **silent** failure: the guardrail neither blocks nor prompts for destructive
PowerShell, and (per the Claude precedent) the same class also produces operator-loops. Until A + B ship, the
approval layer does not actually protect a Windows filesystem.

---
*Detailed audit + ready-to-adapt diff available on request (full writeup prepared locally: 5-gap analysis, 3-hunk
proposed patch, verification matrix). Happy to open a PR against the real `tools/approval.py` if a maintainer
confirms the pattern-list location.*

items.title: pip installs cannot use official bundled skills: wheel ships no skills/, forcing the skills.sh route where DANGEROUS false positives block install
items.body:
## Summary

On a pip install of hermes-agent, official bundled skills (e.g. `google-workspace`) are effectively uninstallable:

1. The wheel does not package the repo's `skills/` directory, so `tools/skills_sync.py` has no seed source and bundled skills are never seeded with `builtin` provenance.
2. The only remaining route is the skills.sh identifier (`skills-sh/nousresearch/hermes-agent/google-workspace`), which resolves to `community` trust.
3. `skills_guard` flags the skill's own scripts as DANGEROUS (false positives, see below), and a dangerous verdict on a community source cannot be overridden by `--force` (by design).

Net result: Hermes' own first-party skill is blocked by Hermes' own scanner, with no supported way through.

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.18.2 (pip install into a venv), Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12
- Wheel payload also verified against hermes-agent 0.19.0 from PyPI (see Root cause)

## Reproduction

```
$ hermes skills install skills-sh/nousresearch/hermes-agent/google-workspace
Fetching: skills-sh/nousresearch/hermes-agent/google-workspace
Quarantined to .hub/quarantine/google-workspace
Running security scan...
Scan: google-workspace (skills-sh/nousresearch/hermes-agent/google-workspace/community)  Verdict: DANGEROUS
  CRITICAL exfiltration   scripts/gws_bridge.py:104   "env["GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN"] = access_token"
  CRITICAL exfiltration   scripts/google_api.py:91    "env["GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE"] = str(TOKEN_PAT"
  HIGH     exfiltration   scripts/setup.py:388        "os.environ["OAUTHLIB_RELAX_TOKEN_SCOPE"] = "1""
  ... (10 findings total)
Decision: BLOCKED — Blocked (community source + dangerous verdict, 10 findings).
--force does not override a dangerous verdict.
```

The flagged lines are the skill's documented mechanism for handing the Hermes-managed OAuth token to the local `gws` subprocess — an env-var credential handoff to a child process, not exfiltration. Related false-positive report: #60709.

`hermes skills repair-official google-workspace --restore` does not help either: "No official optional skills directory found" (and `google-workspace` is bundled, not optional, in any case).

## Root cause

`hermes_constants.get_bundled_skills_dir()` resolves, in order: `HERMES_BUNDLED_SKILLS` env var → wheel data dir (`<sysconfig data>/skills`) → source-checkout relative path → `~/.hermes/skills` last resort. On a pip install the first three all miss:

- The wheel ships no skills payload: `unzip -l hermes_agent-0.19.0-*.whl | grep -c 'data/skills/'` → `0` (same for 0.18.2), so the already-implemented `<sysconfig data>/skills` path never fires.
- There is no source checkout.

The shell installer (`install.sh`) runs `tools/skills_sync.py` from the source checkout, which is how installer-based installs get bundled skills seeded as `builtin`. pip installs never get that step, and `_resolve_trust_level()` (correctly) refuses to grant `builtin`/`official` trust to user-supplied identifiers such as `official/<path>`. Every remaining route lands on `community`, where `INSTALL_POLICY` blocks `dangerous` unconditionally.

## Expected behavior

Official bundled skills should be installable with `builtin` provenance regardless of install method.

## Workaround we're using

A sparse checkout of this repo pinned to the installed release tag, exposed through the documented env override, then running the seeder directly:

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse --depth 1 --branch v2026.7.7.2 \
  https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent ~/hermes-agent-skills
git -C ~/hermes-agent-skills sparse-checkout set skills/productivity/google-workspace
HERMES_BUNDLED_SKILLS=$HOME/hermes-agent-skills/skills \
  ~/.hermes-venv/bin/python \
  ~/.hermes-venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tools/skills_sync.py
```

This seeds the skill as `builtin` with `.bundled_manifest` hash tracking (`hermes skills list` shows `builtin/builtin`), but first-party skills shouldn't require this.

## Suggested fixes

1. Package `skills/` (and `optional-skills/`) as wheel data files so pip installs seed bundled skills exactly like installer/source installs — the resolution path for `<sysconfig data>/skills` already exists in `get_bundled_skills_dir()`.
2. Alternatively (or additionally): when the fetched content provenance is this repository at the installed release tag, resolve trust as `official` for bundled skill paths.
3. Independently, tune the guard rules producing these false positives (#60709) — env-var credential handoff to a local subprocess is the standard pattern for CLI bridges.

items.title: fix(anthropic): sanitize empty/whitespace-only text blocks to prevent permanent HTTP 400 after compression

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug

When context compression (or certain tool-call flows) produces an assistant message with an empty or whitespace-only text content block, the Anthropic Messages API rejects the request with:

```
HTTP 400: messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text
```

Because the empty block is stored in session history and replayed verbatim on every subsequent turn, **the session is permanently stuck** — every message produces the same 400.

Same class of bug as anthropics/claude-code#23390 and anthropics/claude-code#23440.

## Root cause

`_sanitize_replay_block()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` rebuilds stored text blocks with `"text": b.get("text", "")` — it never coerces empty/whitespace text to a non-whitespace placeholder. The final assistant-content guard only catches a fully empty block list, not a list containing a whitespace-only text block.

The **Bedrock adapter** already has the correct fix via `_safe_text()` (ref issue #9486). The Anthropic path never got the same treatment.

## Fix

Two edits in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`:

1. In `_sanitize_replay_block()`, coerce empty/whitespace text to `"(empty)"` placeholder (mirroring `bedrock_adapter._safe_text()`).
2. In `_convert_assistant_message()`, add a list-walk after the existing `not effective` guard to catch surviving whitespace-only text blocks.

Both edits are self-healing: sessions that stored empty text blocks automatically recover on next API call after fix deployment.

## Affected versions

Confirmed on v0.19.0 (git install, 163fab8d). Likely affects all versions using the native Anthropic adapter path (not Bedrock, which already has the fix).

items.body:
+# Feature Request: Background review should propose, not silently write
+
+**Repo**: NousResearch/hermes-agent
+**Label**: enhancement
+
+## Problem
+
+The background review fork (`agent/background_review.py`) silently writes to MEMORY.md and USER.md every N turns (controlled by `memory.nudge_interval`, default 10). This bypasses the user's SOUL.md rules that explicitly state:
+
+> **总则：所有文件写入/修改/删除，必须先问用户同意。不自作主张。**
+
+The fork inherits the SOUL.md system prompt but its task instruction says "Review and save to memory" — and since there's no user present in the fork thread, it has no way to ask for consent. The result is silent writes the user didn't approve.
+
+## Current behavior
+
+- Every `nudge_interval` turns (default 10), a forked AIAgent replays the conversation, evaluates what to remember, and writes directly to MEMORY.md + USER.md
+- The user only discovers these writes through the "Self-improvement review" status notification (if at all)
+- Setting `nudge_interval: 0` disables it entirely, but also loses the useful auto-extraction capability
+- There is no middle ground between "auto-write everything" and "auto-write nothing"
+
+## Proposed solution: `review_mode` config option
+
+Add a write mode toggle under `memory:` config:
+
+```yaml
+memory:
+  nudge_interval: 10        # how often review runs (0 = off)
+  review_mode: auto         # new: "auto" (current) or "propose"
+```
+
+**`auto`** (default, backward compatible): current behavior — silent write.
+
+**`propose`**: the review fork evaluates what to save but does NOT write. Instead it emits a structured summary to the main conversation — something like:
+
+> "I found 3 things worth remembering:
+> 1. User prefers X over Y
+> 2. Project uses Z framework
+> Reply 'yes' to save all, or 'skip' to dismiss."
+
+The main agent reads this and asks the user before writing.
+
+## Implementation note
+
+The fork currently runs in a daemon thread with no communication channel back to the main agent. A `propose` mode would need either:
+
+1. A turn-queue mechanism (fork writes a pending-review entry, consumed on the next user turn)
+2. A lightweight callback that appends a synthetic user-turn with the proposal
+3. Defer the review to the main agent's next turn (inline, not forked)
+
+Happy to discuss trade-offs in the issue thread.

items.title: [Feature]: Define shared-metrics identity scope across profiles

labels.name: telemetry
labels.description: Touches outbound telemetry, usage attribution, or analytics — needs opt-in gating before merge

labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Draft PR #69416 stores the stable shared-metrics UUID in the telemetry database under one `HERMES_HOME`. Multiple profiles on the same Hermes installation therefore receive different UUIDs and count independently. The UUID is stable across that profile's packages until its metrics state is reset.

The current implementation is consequently a pseudonymous profile identity, not a physical-installation identity. Calling it an anonymous install ID makes the aggregation unit and linkability unclear.

## Proposed Solution

Confirm the intended aggregation unit before the shared-metrics schema is finalized.

Recommended for the current local-first slice:

- Keep identity scoped to one `HERMES_HOME` so consent, storage, reset, and package ownership stay within the same profile boundary.
- Describe it as a random, resettable pseudonymous profile ID.
- Document that packages from the same opted-in profile are linkable through this ID.
- Document that multiple profiles on one machine count separately.
- Align schema field names and metric terminology before declaring the package schema stable.

If product requirements instead require one count per physical Hermes installation, define a shared identity location and explicit cross-profile consent, reset, concurrency, migration, and deletion semantics before implementation. A shared machine-level ID must not allow one profile's opt-in to collect or link another profile's activity.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep the current implementation and continue calling it an anonymous install ID: rejected because the name does not match the actual identity boundary.
- Move the UUID outside `HERMES_HOME` immediately: rejected pending a product decision because this crosses existing profile consent and storage boundaries.
- Derive an identity from hardware, account, host, or path data: rejected for privacy reasons.

## Feature Type

Configuration option

## Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Product owners approve profile-level or installation-level counting.
- Identity terminology accurately states its scope and persistence.
- Linkability across packages is documented.
- Multi-profile counting behavior is documented and tested.
- Consent, reset, deletion, and migration semantics match the chosen scope.
- No identifier is derived from hardware, account, host, path, or credential data.

Related draft: #69416

items.title: Proposal: add a narrow, opt-in OCR tool for exact text extraction

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Proposal

I am considering whether to open an implementation PR for a provider-switchable, deterministic OCR capability for image-to-text extraction. Before opening a PR, I would like to confirm whether this direction is appropriate upstream and which delivery surface is preferred.

This issue is a design/placement question before any implementation PR. It does **not** request bundling a large OCR engine or model into every Hermes installation.

## Current shipped paths (audited against `main`)

Audit snapshot: `main` at [`fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b), observed 2026-07-22 UTC.

Hermes already has several adjacent internal paths, but none is a standalone deterministic OCR provider/tool:

- [`read_file`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/file_tools.py#L1128-L1195) delegates structured extraction to [`tools/read_extract.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/read_extract.py#L1-L50) for notebooks, DOCX, and XLSX. It is not raster-image OCR; binary images are directed to `vision_analyze` or `terminal`.
- [`vision_analyze`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/vision_tools.py#L1444-L1521) accepts an image source and either attaches pixels to a native-vision model or returns an auxiliary model-generated description. It does not expose a deterministic OCR result contract.
- [`tools/image_source.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/image_source.py#L1-L89) is the existing image resolver/security boundary that an OCR path should reuse rather than duplicate.
- The bundled [`ocr-and-documents` skill](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/skills/productivity/ocr-and-documents/SKILL.md#L30-L55) uses PyMuPDF for text PDFs and optional marker-pdf for scanned-PDF/image OCR. marker-pdf is documented as a heavy optional path (roughly 3–5 GB and 90+ languages), not a base dependency ([details](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/skills/productivity/ocr-and-documents/SKILL.md#L88-L105)).
- The current [`ToolRegistry`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/registry.py#L365-L455) already supports `check_fn` and `requires_env`, and filters unavailable tools before exposing them ([exposure filtering](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/tools/registry.py#L533-L554)). This is the existing precedent for a service-gated surface.
- The base dependency set contains Pillow for vision image normalization, but no OCR engine; provider-specific dependencies are intentionally kept out of the base dependency list ([dependency policy](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/pyproject.toml#L40-L44), [Pillow](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/pyproject.toml#L123-L130)).

## Engine and provider boundary

The proposed default is:

- **Do not bundle an OCR engine, model weights, language packs, or a vendor SDK into the base installation.** Tesseract, PaddleOCR, marker-pdf, and remote OCR services have materially different system dependencies, model sizes, languages, licenses, cost, and accuracy characteristics.
- If a shared abstraction is useful, keep only a small provider contract/resolver in the common layer. Provider implementations should be optional: for example, a local Tesseract adapter, an opt-in PaddleOCR adapter, or a user-operated OCR HTTP provider.
- Provider selection should be operator-controlled through the existing `config.yaml`/setup model, not model-controlled per call and not a new user-facing `HERMES_*` environment variable. The active provider should be health-checked and the capability exposed only when it is actually usable.
- If a structured tool is justified, it should be service-gated and reuse `image_source`, temporary-file cleanup, credential-read guards, SSRF checks, bounded timeouts, and off-event-loop execution. If these requirements do not justify a registered tool, keep the same provider contract behind the skill/MCP surface.

This separates **provider switching** from **engine bundling**: the user can switch providers without making every Hermes installation carry every engine.

## Related upstream work — status and actual scope

The following public items were checked directly for current state, body, reviews/comments, and merged status:

| Reference | Current state | What it actually proposes |
|---|---|---|
| [#2082](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/2082) | closed, unmerged | Registered `document_parse`/LiteParse tool. A review comment says it fits better as an optional skill rather than a registered tool because of schema footprint ([comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/2082#issuecomment-4097097027)). The commenter is recorded as `CONTRIBUTOR`; this is not presented here as an unqualified maintainer policy. |
| [#2154](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/2154) | closed, unmerged | Follow-up moving document parsing from a registered tool to an optional skill; that skill is not the current standalone OCR tool. |
| [#3932](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/3932) | open, unmerged | PaddleOCR scripts and provider guidance inside `ocr-and-documents`; not a registered tool. |
| [#13132](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/13132) | open, unmerged | Local Tesseract only as a timeout fallback inside `vision_analyze`; not independently callable OCR. |
| [#43024](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/43024) | open, unmerged | Optional LiteParse PDF fallback inside the document skill; not a core OCR provider. |
| [#50513](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/50513) | open, unmerged | Verbatim-first transcription prompts for non-vision preprocessing; model-generated transcription, not an OCR engine/tool. |
| [#45071](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/45071) | open issue | Screenshot recognition accuracy/preprocessing; no explicit OCR tool API. |
| [#45424](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/45424) | closed, `NOT_PLANNED` | Windows screenshot OCR request; the closure comment points to the existing vision pipeline, not a bundled Tesseract runtime ([comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/45424#issuecomment-4969691912)). |
| [#63733](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63733) | closed draft, unmerged | Windows `computer_use` local OCR and exact-window targeting; not current main. |
| [#2461](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/2461) | merged | PyMuPDF usage examples in the document skill; not an OCR engine or model tool. |
| [#34228](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/34228) | closed draft, unmerged | Optional LiteParse helper; author-closed without a maintainer rejection rationale. |

Taken together, these are related but different capability surfaces: registered tool, existing-tool fallback, prompt-level transcription, skill helper, and existing multimodal outcome. None establishes that a standalone OCR tool is currently accepted or shipped.

## Proposed smallest contract, if a tool is warranted

- Input: one image source accepted by the existing `image_source` security path (local path, `file://`, data URL, or approved HTTP(S) URL).
- Output: extracted plain text only for v1; line/box/confidence metadata can be deferred.
- No screenshot capture, visual description, PDF orchestration, layout editing, or automatic OCR of every attachment.
- No bundled OCR engine or model weights.
- Provider availability is explicit and service-gated; a missing/unhealthy provider means the tool is not exposed, rather than silently falling back to a different paid or model-based path.
- Execution is timeout-bounded, off the event loop, and covered by the existing image resolver, temporary-file lifecycle, SSRF, and credential-read protections.

## Policy question

The repository's current footprint ladder says to prefer existing code, CLI + skill, service-gated tool, plugin, and MCP before a new core tool ([policy](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/AGENTS.md#L71-L74), [ladder](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/AGENTS.md#L182-L206)). It also explicitly cautions against a new core tool when terminal + file or a skill already suffice ([policy](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/fea838c9f26ac00c5931a4ac13764ae49361428b/AGENTS.md#L108-L110)).

Could maintainers advise:

1. Should provider-switchable deterministic OCR remain a skill/MCP capability, with no registered core tool?
2. If structured tool I/O is justified, is a service-gated `ocr` tool acceptable even though the engines remain optional?
3. Should the shared layer contain only a provider contract/resolver, or should each adapter live entirely outside core?
4. Is operator-selected `config.yaml` provider switching the intended control surface?
5. Is plain text-only output the correct v1 contract?

I have not opened an implementation PR yet. I am asking for maintainer guidance on the placement and engine/provider boundary before deciding whether to open one, so #3932, #13132, #43024, #50513, and future OCR work do not continue as overlapping paths.

items.body:
Follow-up to #68777, which fixed a wrong config key on the Nous Portal page. That fix exposed a bigger gap on the same subject, so this issue proposes a page rather than a patch, because one question below needs a maintainer answer before I can write it accurately.

## the gap

`/docs/user-guide/features/tools` documents the browser toolset as three tool names (`browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_vision`) and stops. Nothing on that page, or anywhere else in the docs, covers cookie or login persistence, browser profiles, or attaching to a browser the user already runs.

That is the difference between a browser tool that reads public pages and one that does real work, and users are hitting it. One prompting case: a user needs the agent logged in to several sites, got there with Chrome remote debugging, and finds it takes over their daily browser (https://www.reddit.com/r/hermesagent/comments/1v24h15/the_ai_agent_friendly_brower/).

Verified on v0.19.0 rather than assumed: on a default install cookies do not survive between sessions. A cookie set in one session is gone in the next, with the browser starting from a clean context each time. The capability to change that ships, but is currently only discoverable by reading source.

A secondary discoverability gap: `/docs/user-guide/features/tool-gateway` DOES document enabling the managed backend, but the browser tools page does not link to it, so a user reading about browser tools never reaches it.

## proposed page: `website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md`

Three routes to authenticated browsing, plus a storage-and-safety section.

### 1. managed cloud browser (Nous Portal)

```yaml
browser:
  cloud_provider: browser-use
  use_gateway: true
```

Enable with `hermes tools` and pick Nous Subscription. The page should state plainly that this is a paid-subscription feature and that free accounts, including limited free-tool-pool accounts, report `not configured`. It runs server-side, so the user's own browser is never involved.

`browser.auto_local_for_private_urls` (default `true`) belongs here too: with a cloud provider set, LAN and localhost URLs auto-spawn a local Chromium instead of being sent to the cloud, which users deploying against internal services need to know.

### 2. persistent local profile via Camofox

```bash
docker run -p 9377:9377 -e CAMOFOX_PORT=9377 jo-inc/camofox-browser
```

```
# ~/.hermes/.env
CAMOFOX_URL=http://localhost:9377
```

```yaml
browser:
  camofox:
    managed_persistence: true
```

The page should lead with the fact that Camofox is a separate self-hosted service and is not bundled, because setting `managed_persistence: true` alone does nothing and reads as a broken feature.

With the service running, Hermes sends a deterministic profile-derived userId so Camofox maps to the same persistent browser profile directory across restarts (`tools/browser_camofox_state.py`). Auth state lives under `<HERMES_HOME>/browser_auth/camofox/`. Identity is profile-scoped: one Hermes profile, one persistent browser identity.

### 3. attach to a browser you already run (CDP)

```yaml
browser:
  cdp_url: "ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/<id>"
```

A persistent CDP endpoint is honoured from config alongside the env form (`tools/browser_camofox.py`), and `hermes_cli/browser_connect.py` provides the attach helpers. `browser.camofox.adopt_existing_tab` attaches to an already-open tab.

Worth stating explicitly that there is no `hermes browser` subcommand, since users look for one. The practical tip that answers the linked thread: point it at a second Chrome profile used only by the agent, so daily browsing is unaffected.

### 4. where state lives, and the safety switches

- `<HERMES_HOME>/browser_auth/camofox/` holds persisted browser auth. It is credential-equivalent and worth calling out as such, since users will not expect logged-in sessions on disk.
- `browser.restrict_evaluate` (default `false`): opt-in denylist blocking sensitive JS primitives (cookies, storage, clipboard, network, form values) inside `browser_console(expression=...)`.
- `browser.allow_unsafe_evaluate` (default `false`): legacy override that bypasses the denylist entirely.
- `browser.allow_private_urls` (default `false`): navigation to private/internal IPs.
- `browser.headed` (default `false`): local mode with a visible window that persists between turns.

Documenting `restrict_evaluate` matters beyond completeness. Users are reporting agents reaching for browser cookies unprompted and reading it as overreach, and a shipped mitigation that nobody can find does not reduce that.

### cross-links to add

- `features/tools` browser section, to this page and to the Tool Gateway page
- `integrations/nous-portal`, to this page, next to the snippet corrected in #68777

## question for maintainers

Is `cloud_provider` intended to accept values other than `browser-use`? The Browserbase and Modal plumbing suggests it might. The page should list the accepted values and I do not want to document a guess. This is the one thing blocking me from opening a PR instead of an issue.

## verification done

All claims above were read from a v0.19.0 install (`hermes_cli/config.py` browser defaults, `tools/browser_camofox.py`, `tools/browser_camofox_state.py`, `hermes_cli/browser_connect.py`), and the non-persistence behaviour was tested end to end with a two-session cookie round-trip.

The Camofox and CDP routes are source-verified but NOT run end to end. If that bar is required before a docs page lands, say so and I will stand up the Camofox container and test both first.

Happy to open the PR as soon as the `cloud_provider` question is answered.

items.title: Desktop SSH remote mode is broken whenever a non-default profile is active: token-path validation resolves against the profile-scoped HERMES_HOME while the client hardcodes ~/.hermes/desktop-ssh

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
# Desktop SSH remote mode is broken whenever a non-default profile is active: token-path validation resolves against the profile-scoped HERMES_HOME while the client hardcodes `~/.hermes/desktop-ssh`

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), install method: git (upstream `76e17bc3`)
- Remote host: Debian 13 (Linux 6.12), gateway + profiles managed via systemd user units
- Desktop client: Hermes Desktop on Windows 11, SSH remote mode
- Sticky profile on the remote: `~/.hermes/active_profile` = a non-default profile (`alfred`)

## Symptoms

Desktop boot fails in a retry loop with:

```
[ssh-lifecycle] spawned remote dashboard pid=110422
[ssh] connection closed (no-mux tunnels killed)
[boot] Desktop boot failed: Could not verify SSH backend process ownership.
```

Each retry opens several SSH connections per second (sshd log fills with `Accepted publickey` bursts), spawns a remote backend, and the backend dies instantly. The spawn log on the remote (`~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/<ownershipId>/<nonce>.log`) contains exactly one line:

```
--ssh-session-token-file must be under the desktop-ssh directory
```

## Root cause

Three pieces interact:

1. **The desktop client hardcodes the remote lock/token directory to the root home**: `REMOTE_LOCK_DIR = '~/.hermes/desktop-ssh'` in `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts` (line ~36). The token is uploaded to `~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/<ownershipId>/<nonce>.token` and that path is passed via `--ssh-session-token-file`.

2. **`hermes serve` (spawned without `--profile`) adopts the sticky profile**: `hermes_cli/main.py` (~lines 591–625) reads `active_profile` and re-homes the process into `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>` (via `resolve_profile_env` → `HERMES_HOME`).

3. **The token-path validator anchors to the (now profile-scoped) home**: `_read_ssh_session_token_file` in `hermes_cli/main.py` computes `token_root = get_hermes_home() / "desktop-ssh"` and requires `token_path.relative_to(token_root)`. With the sticky profile adopted, `token_root` becomes `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/desktop-ssh`, the client-provided path `~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/...` fails `relative_to`, and the process exits with `--ssh-session-token-file must be under the desktop-ssh directory` (main.py:12969).

The client then sees a dead PID; `pidIsOurDashboard` runs over an SSH connection that is being torn down, so the surfaced error is the misleading `Could not verify SSH backend process ownership` (transient-transport kind), and the client loops.

Net effect: **Desktop SSH mode only works when `active_profile` is `default`.** Setting an explicit profile in desktop settings should hit the same mismatch through the same validator (the client would pass `--profile <name>`, re-homing `serve` into the profile dir, while still writing the token under the root `~/.hermes/desktop-ssh`) — inferred from the code path; the sticky-profile variant is the one reproduced live.

## Reproduction

1. On a Linux remote with Hermes ≥ a version that has `serve --ssh-session-token-file`: `hermes profile create test && hermes profile use test`
2. Connect from Hermes Desktop (Windows/macOS) in SSH remote mode.
3. Boot fails in the ownership-verification loop; `~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/<id>/<nonce>.log` on the remote shows the token-path validation error.

Local minimal repro on the remote (no desktop involved):

```bash
hermes profile use <any-non-default>
mkdir -p -m 700 ~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
python3 -c "import secrets;open('/home/USER/.hermes/desktop-ssh/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.token','w').write(secrets.token_hex(32))"
env HERMES_DESKTOP=1 hermes serve --isolated --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 \
  --ssh-session-token-file ~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.token \
  --ssh-owner-nonce aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
# -> SystemExit: --ssh-session-token-file must be under the desktop-ssh directory
# With active_profile=default the same command prints HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=NNNNN
```

## Expected

Desktop SSH mode works regardless of which profile is sticky-active on the remote; profile selection affects which profile the backend serves, not whether the spawn credential can be read.

## Suggested fixes (any one of these)

- Anchor the validator to the **default** root: `token_root = get_default_hermes_root() / "desktop-ssh"` — matching the client contract, which is deliberately root-scoped (ownership dirs are shared across profiles by design of `remote-lifecycle.ts`).
- Or: make `serve` skip sticky-profile adoption when `--ssh-session-token-file` is passed (the desktop already passes the profile explicitly when it wants one), mirroring the `HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD` exception that exists for supervised gateways.
- Or: teach the client to resolve the remote profile home and place ownership dirs under it — more invasive, breaks lockfile sharing across profiles.

A secondary papercut worth fixing alongside: when the spawned backend dies this early, the client surfaces `Could not verify SSH backend process ownership` (a transport-classified error from the verification exec) instead of the actual stderr line from the spawn log, which made this considerably harder to diagnose. Reading back `<nonce>.log` on spawn-death would surface the real error in the desktop boot log.

## Workaround

Keep `active_profile` at `default` on hosts used as Desktop SSH remotes (pin gateway units to explicit profiles via `-p <name>` so switching the sticky profile isn't needed operationally).

items.title: [Bug]: # Vietnamese IME input (Unikey/EVKey) broken in TUI ΓÇö text dropped, garbled, misplaced diacritics

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Summary

Typing Vietnamese with IME-based input methods (Unikey, EVKey) in the Hermes TUI produces garbled text ΓÇö characters are dropped, duplicated, or diacritics are misplaced. The same IME works correctly in other TUI apps (e.g. opencode/bubbletea) in the same terminal, confirming the issue is in Hermes TUI's input pipeline, not the terminal or IME.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- **Terminal:** VS Code integrated terminal
- **IME:** Unikey (Telex, Unicode CRLF) ΓÇö also reproduced with EVKey
- **Hermes:** `hermes --tui` (Ink-based TUI, Node.js)
- **Comparison:** opencode TUI (Go/bubbletea) in the same terminal ΓÇö **no issue**

## Reproduction

1. Open VS Code integrated terminal
2. Run `hermes --tui`
3. Type Vietnamese using Unikey (Telex), e.g.: `xin ch├áo` ΓÇö the word "ch├áo" needs `a` then `a` + `f` (dß║Ñu huyß╗ün)

### Expected

Text appears as typed: `xin ch├áo`

### Actual

Characters are dropped, duplicated, or diacritics appear on wrong syllables. For example, typing "aa" to produce "├ó" may lose the first "a", or the composed character "├ó" never appears, or a stray backspace leaks as text.

## Root Cause Analysis

I traced the issue through the source code. The problem is in the **tokenizer** (`ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/termio/tokenize.ts`) combined with the **printable check** in `textInput.tsx`.

### How Vietnamese IME sends keystrokes

Unikey/EVKey uses a **compose-and-replace** strategy. To type "├ó" (a + circumflex), the IME sends:

```
'a'  (0x61)        ΓåÆ intermediate character appears
\x7f  (DEL/backspace) ΓåÆ delete the intermediate 'a'
'├ó'  (0xC3 0xA2, 3 UTF-8 bytes) ΓåÆ the final composed character
```

These bytes arrive as a **single chunk** on stdin (within one `readable` event).

### What the tokenizer does

In `tokenize.ts`, the `ground` state handler (lines 151ΓÇô160):

```typescript
case 'ground':
    if (code === C0.ESC) {
        flushText()
        seqStart = i
        result.state = 'escape'
        i++
    } else {
        i++  // ΓåÉ ALL non-ESC bytes are accumulated into one text token
    }
    break
```

Any byte that is not ESC (0x1B) is accumulated into a single text token. So the chunk `"a\x7fß║Ñ"` becomes **one text token**: `{ type: 'text', value: "a\x7fß║Ñ" }`.

### What parseKeypress does with the combined token

`parseKeypress("a\x7fß║Ñ")` is called with the full multi-character string. None of the pattern matches in `parseKeypress` (lines 639ΓÇô832) handle this correctly:

- `s === '\x7f'` ΓåÆ **NO** (s is 4+ chars, not 1)
- `s.length === 1` checks ΓåÆ **NO**
- `META_KEY_CODE_RE` ΓåÆ **NO**
- All other single-char checks ΓåÆ **NO**

The result is a `ParsedKey` with `name: ''`, `sequence: "a\x7fß║Ñ"`, `ctrl: false`, etc. ΓÇö **unrecognized as any key or printable input**.

### What textInput.tsx does

In `textInput.tsx`, line 1131ΓÇô1132:

```typescript
const isPrintableInput =
    (event.keypress.isPasted || inp.length > 0) &&
    PRINTABLE.test(inp.replace(BRACKET_PASTE, ''))
```

Where `PRINTABLE = /^[ -~\u00a0-\uffff]+$/`.

The `\x7f` byte (DEL) is **NOT** in the range `[ -~]` (0x20ΓÇô0x7E) and not in `[\u00a0-\uffff]`, so `PRINTABLE.test("a\x7fß║Ñ")` returns **false**.

Result: `isPrintableInput = false` ΓåÆ the entire input chunk is **silently dropped**.

### Why opencode doesn't have this problem

opencode (Go + bubbletea) reads stdin at the **byte level** and processes each byte independently:
- `0x61` ΓåÆ insert 'a'
- `0x7F` ΓåÆ backspace (delete 'a')
- `0xC3 0xA2` ΓåÆ insert '├ó'

Each control byte is handled as a separate event, so the compose-and-replace sequence works correctly.

### The same bug affects fast typing

When typing regular ASCII quickly, multiple characters can arrive in one stdin chunk. The tokenizer accumulates them into a single text token and `parseKeypress` is called with the full string. The `INPUTABLE` regex and `parseKeypress` happen to work for pure ASCII because all bytes are in the printable range ΓÇö but any control byte (0x7F from IME, or 0x08 backspace from rapid correction) mixed into the chunk breaks the entire token.

## Suggested Fix

### Option A: Split text tokens at control characters in the tokenizer

In `tokenize.ts`, `ground` state, emit control characters (0x00ΓÇô0x1F, 0x7F) as **separate text tokens** so `parseKeypress` sees each one individually:

```typescript
case 'ground':
    if (code === C0.ESC) {
        flushText()
        seqStart = i
        result.state = 'escape'
        i++
    } else if (code < 0x20 || code === 0x7f) {
        // Control chars (including DEL from IME compose-and-replace)
        // must be separate tokens so parseKeypress handles them
        // individually, not merged into a printable text run.
        flushText()
        tokens.push({ type: 'text', value: data[i] })
        i++
        textStart = i
    } else {
        i++
    }
    break
```

### Option B: Split text tokens in parseMultipleKeypresses

In `parse-keypress.ts`, when processing text tokens, split at control characters before calling `parseKeypress`:

```typescript
} else if (token.type === 'text') {
    if (inPaste) {
        pasteBuffer += token.value
    } else {
        // Split at control chars so each is parsed individually
        let start = 0
        for (let j = 0; j < token.value.length; j++) {
            const code = token.value.charCodeAt(j)
            if (code < 0x20 || code === 0x7f) {
                if (j > start) {
                    keys.push(parseKeypress(token.value.slice(start, j)))
                }
                keys.push(parseKeypress(token.value[j]))
                start = j + 1
            }
        }
        if (start < token.value.length) {
            keys.push(parseKeypress(token.value.slice(start)))
        }
    }
}
```

### Option C: Handle multi-character input in parseKeypress

Add a path in `parseKeypress` that splits multi-byte input containing control characters into individual key presses before pattern matching.

## Impact

This bug makes the TUI **unusable** for Vietnamese users (and likely any language that uses IME compose-and-replace, such as Japanese, Korean, or Chinese input methods that emit backspace/DEL as part of composition). Users must paste text from an external editor as a workaround.

## Related Code

- Tokenizer: `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/termio/tokenize.ts` (ground state, ~line 151)
- Key parser: `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/parse-keypress.ts` (`parseKeypress`, ~line 639)
- Text input: `ui-tui/src/components/textInput.tsx` (printable check, ~line 1131)
- Stdin reader: `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/components/App.tsx` (`handleReadable`, ~line 559)

## Workaround

Type Vietnamese text in an external editor (Notepad, VS Code file), then paste into the TUI with Ctrl+Shift+V. The bracketed-paste path handles multi-byte text correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code integrated terminal (`` Ctrl+` ``)
2. Run `hermes --tui`
3. Switch to Unikey (or EVKey), set to Telex + Unicode
4. Type Vietnamese text into the prompt, e.g.:
   - Type "xin chao" → expected: "xin chào"
   - Type "aa" → expected: "â"
   - Type "aws" → expected: "ă"
5. Observe the output: characters are dropped, duplicated, or diacritics appear on wrong syllables
6. For comparison: run `opencode` in the same terminal → Vietnamese typing works correctly

### Expected Behavior

Vietnamese text should appear exactly as typed, with diacritics placed on the correct syllables. For example:
- Typing "aa" should produce "â"
- Typing "aws" should produce "ă"
- Typing "xin chao" should produce "xin chào"
The IME compose-and-replace sequence (intermediate char → backspace → final composed char) should be handled transparently — the TUI should process each byte event individually, matching the behavior of other TUI apps like opencode (bubbletea) in the same terminal.

### Actual Behavior

characters are dropped, duplicated, or diacritics appear on wrong syllables

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
version:          0.19.0 [4999de8f] (2026-07-22)
os:               Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
python:           3.11.15
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
profile:          default
hermes_home:      ~/.hermes
model:            ocg/glm-5.2
provider:         custom
terminal:         local
toolsets:         hermes-cli
gateway:          running (systemd, pid 340)
platforms:        telegram
skills:           81
```

### Operating System

window + wsl 2

### Python Version

3.11.15 

### Hermes Version

v0.19.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: cron execution ledger leaks three SQLite connections per run, exhausting file descriptors

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

Every cron run leaks three SQLite connections from `cron/executions.py`, eventually exhausting the long-running gateway process's file-descriptor limit and causing unrelated cron jobs and gateway components to fail with:

```text
[Errno 24] Too many open files
```

This occurs on ordinary script-only (`no_agent`) cron jobs and is separate from the early-return `SessionDB` leak reported in #60859.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Gateway with recurring cron jobs enabled. Script-only `no_agent` jobs reproduce it.
2. Record the gateway PID and count its descriptors:

   ```bash
   ls /proc/$PID/fd | wc -l
   ```

3. Allow several cron jobs to complete.
4. Count descriptors again and inspect their targets:

   ```bash
   for fd in /proc/$PID/fd/*; do readlink "$fd"; done | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
   ```

5. Observe that each completed cron run leaves approximately six additional descriptors: three for `executions.db` and three for `executions.db-wal`.

## Expected Behavior

Cron execution-ledger operations close their SQLite connections after each transaction. The gateway's descriptor count should remain approximately flat across repeated cron runs.

## Actual Behavior

On a live gateway, the descriptor count increased from 34 to 58 immediately after four script-only cron jobs completed:

```text
34 -> 58 open descriptors
+12 executions.db descriptors
+12 executions.db-wal descriptors
```

That is exactly six leaked descriptors per job. With approximately 62 runs/hour, the process leaked roughly 372 descriptors/hour and reached its 1,024 soft limit in about three hours. Once exhausted, failures spread beyond cron scripts to config reads, gateway state files, SQLite stores, and sockets.

A gateway restart clears the descriptors temporarily, but the count immediately resumes increasing on subsequent cron runs.

## Affected Component

- Gateway
- Other: cron scheduler execution ledger

## Messaging Platform

Discord, although the leak is platform-independent.

## Debug Report

```shell
Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream d358280a
Linux 7.0.0-28-generic x86_64
Python 3.14.4
Gateway running under systemd user service
12 active cron jobs, primarily script-only no-agent jobs
Gateway RLIMIT_NOFILE: soft 1024, hard 524288
```

Full logs are not attached because this is a production gateway, but the deterministic `/proc/$PID/fd` reproduction above isolates the leaked resource.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04

## Python Version

Python 3.14.4

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream d358280a

## Additional Logs / Traceback

```shell
Cron 'Fred host local watchdog' failed: Script execution failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
Cron 'Shaggy Scooby production VM watch' failed: Script execution failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`cron/executions.py` repeatedly uses this pattern in `init_db`, `create_execution`, `mark_running`, `finish_execution`, `get_execution`, and `list_executions`:

```python
with _lock, _connect() as conn:
    ...
```

The `sqlite3.Connection` context manager manages commit/rollback; it does not close the connection on `__exit__`. No explicit `conn.close()` is called.

A normal cron run invokes at least:

1. `create_execution()`
2. `mark_running()`
3. `finish_execution()`

Each connection holds the main database and WAL descriptors in this environment, yielding the observed three connections / six descriptors per completed run.

## Proposed Fix

Explicitly close every connection, for example:

```python
from contextlib import closing

with _lock, closing(_connect()) as conn:
    ...
```

Alternatively, provide a small transaction context manager that guarantees rollback/commit and `close()` in `finally`, then use it consistently for all execution-ledger operations.

Regression coverage should repeatedly call the ledger lifecycle and assert that descriptor count or open SQLite handles does not grow. It would also be useful to run this test under Python 3.14, where the leak was reproduced.

## PR

I can help validate a fix against the live high-frequency cron workload, but I am not currently submitting a PR with this report.

items.title: Desktop app auto-updater always fails: no macOS zip asset published to releases

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

The Hermes desktop app (macOS, Electron + Squirrel.Mac) can never self-update. Clicking the in-app Update button quits the app, nothing is installed, and relaunch shows the same version. Root cause: the update feed returns 404 because GitHub releases for this repo do not include a macOS desktop build asset.

## Environment

- App: Hermes.app 0.15.1 (CFBundleShortVersionString), /Applications/Hermes.app
- Bundle ID: com.nousresearch.hermes
- Updater: Squirrel.Mac (Squirrel.framework present in Contents/Frameworks)
- Host: macOS 26.5.2, arm64 (Apple Silicon)

## Evidence

1. The app Squirrel updater queries update.electronjs.org for this repo:

   GET https://update.electronjs.org/NousResearch/hermes-agent/darwin-arm64/0.15.1

   Response (HTTP 404):
   No updates found (needs asset matching .*-(mac|darwin|osx).*.zip in public repository)

2. Latest release v2026.7.20 only ships Python artifacts:
   - hermes_agent-0.19.0-py3-none-any.whl.sigstore.json
   - hermes_agent-0.19.0.tar.gz.sigstore.json

   No *-mac.zip / *-darwin.zip / *-osx.zip asset is attached, so update.electronjs.org has nothing to serve and Squirrel silently aborts.

3. Local ShipIt logs (~/Library/Caches/com.nousresearch.hermes.ShipIt/) are empty — the updater fails before any download begins, consistent with the 404 feed response.

## User-visible behavior

Click Update → app closes → nothing happens → reopen → still on 0.15.1. No error is surfaced to the user.

## Suggested fixes (either/both)

1. Attach a properly named macOS zip (e.g. Hermes-0.19.0-mac.zip or Hermes-darwin-arm64.zip) to releases so update.electronjs.org can serve updates.
2. If the desktop app is not meant to update via update.electronjs.org, point autoUpdater at the correct feed (or disable the in-app Update button) and surface a clear message when no update is available instead of quitting silently.

## Workaround

Manually download the latest desktop build (when available) and replace /Applications/Hermes.app, or use the CLI (hermes update) which is on 0.19.0.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop app image uploads unreachable from profile Docker sandboxes

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### Bug Description

Desktop app image uploads unreachable from profile Docker sandboxes; terminal.docker_volumes in profile config.yaml not applied to sandbox containers (0.19.0)

Environment

Hermes Agent 0.19.0 (upstream 6b545824), install method: git
Host OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (container image is Debian-based nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20)
Terminal backend: docker
Multi-profile deployment: systemd user services, one hermes-gateway-<profile>.service per profile, each unit setting HERMES_HOME=/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/<profile>
Client: Hermes desktop app connecting to this self-hosted server

Problem 1 — desktop uploads land where profile sandboxes can't see them

Images attached in the desktop app are saved by the root gateway to the global path ~/.hermes/images/upload_*.png (confirmed via find). Profile sandbox containers, however, only mount profile-scoped paths:

profiles/<profile>/cache/documents -> /root/.hermes/cache/documents
profiles/<profile>/cache/images    -> /root/.hermes/cache/images
profiles/<profile>/cache/web       -> /root/.hermes/cache/web
profiles/<profile>/skills          -> /root/.hermes/skills
profiles/<profile>/sandboxes/docker/default/home      -> /root
profiles/<profile>/sandboxes/docker/default/workspace -> /workspace

So vision_analyze on any desktop-app upload fails with:

Error analyzing image: '/home/hermes/.hermes/images/upload_20260722_181019_1.png' is not reachable inside the sandbox and no active sandbox session is available to read it

The same image sent to the same profile via Telegram works fine, and vision against an HTTPS image URL works fine — the vision pipeline itself is healthy; the fault is isolated to local-file resolution of desktop uploads through the profile sandbox. This affects every multi-profile desktop-app deployment out of the box, no custom config involved.

Problem 2 — the obvious workaround (docker_volumes) is not honored

Attempted fix: mount the global upload dir into the profile sandbox via the profile's config.yaml:

yaml
terminal:
  backend: docker
  # ...
  docker_volumes:
    - "/home/hermes/.hermes/images:/home/hermes/.hermes/images:ro"

(Also tested with destination /root/.hermes/images:ro — same result.)

Steps:

Add the entry to ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml (profile has its own terminal: block; YAML validity confirmed).
systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway-<profile> (restart confirmed: new PID, fresh start time).
docker rm -f all existing containers for the profile (docker ps -a --filter "label=hermes-profile=<profile>").
Trigger a tool call so a fresh sandbox spawns.

Expected: new container's mounts include the configured volume.
Actual: docker inspect <new-container> --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -> {{.Destination}}{{println}}{{end}}' shows only the six built-in mounts listed above — the configured volume never appears, across multiple container recreations (container verified freshly created, age <1 min at inspect time).

Ruled out / verified along the way

YAML syntax valid, correctly indented list under terminal.docker_volumes.
The unit's HERMES_HOME points at the profile dir, so the gateway loads the intended profile config.yaml.
Source inspection (as of 0.19.0 / 6b545824): gateway/run.py (~line 1626) bridges terminal.docker_volumes → JSON-encoded TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES env var at startup; tools/terminal_tool.py (~line 1375) reads it via os.getenv("TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES", "[]") when constructing docker run. We could not conclusively determine where the value is dropped (a /proc/<pid>/environ check is not valid for this — it's an exec-time snapshot and doesn't reflect later os.environ mutations).

Suggested debugging step: a startup log line in the config-bridging block printing the exact TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES value written, and a matching log in terminal_tool.py printing what it read back, would show which side of the bridge fails without indirect /proc inspection.

Impact / workaround: desktop-app image analysis is broken for profile-based deployments; current workaround is sending images via Telegram (profile-scoped media path works).

### Steps to Reproduce

Setup: self-hosted multi-profile deployment. Systemd user services, one
hermes-gateway-<profile>.service per profile, each unit setting
HERMES_HOME=/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/<profile>. Terminal backend: docker
(nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20). Client: Hermes desktop app
connected to this server.

Problem 1 (upload path):
1. In the desktop app, open a session with a non-default profile.
2. Attach any image to a message ("What do you see?").
3. Image is saved by the root gateway to the GLOBAL path ~/.hermes/images/upload_*.png (confirmed via find).
4. vision_analyze fails — the profile's sandbox only mounts profile-scoped paths (cache/*, skills, sandbox home/workspace), not ~/.hermes/images.
5. Control tests: the same image sent to the same profile via Telegram works; vision_analyze against an HTTPS image URL works. Fault is isolated to local-file resolution of desktop uploads through the profile sandbox.

Problem 2 (docker_volumes workaround not honored):
1. Add to ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml under the existing terminal: block:
   docker_volumes:
     - "/home/hermes/.hermes/images:/home/hermes/.hermes/images:ro"
   (also tested destination /root/.hermes/images:ro — same result; YAML validity confirmed)
2. systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway-<profile>  (restart confirmed: new PID, fresh start time)
3. docker rm -f all containers for the profile (docker ps -a --filter "label=hermes-profile=<profile>")
4. Trigger a terminal tool call so a fresh sandbox spawns.
5. Inspect mounts: docker inspect <new-container> --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -> {{.Destination}}{{println}}{{end}}'

### Expected Behavior

Problem 1: Images attached in the desktop app should be readable by the profile's
vision_analyze — either saved to a profile-scoped path that is already mounted,
or the upload directory mounted into profile sandboxes.

Problem 2: A docker_volumes entry in the profile's config.yaml terminal: block
should appear in the mounts of newly created sandbox containers after a gateway
restart and container recreation.

### Actual Behavior

Problem 1: vision_analyze fails on every desktop-app upload with:

  Error analyzing image: '/home/hermes/.hermes/images/upload_20260722_181019_1.png'
  is not reachable inside the sandbox and no active sandbox session is available
  to read it

Same image via Telegram to the same profile: works. Same request with an HTTPS
image URL: works.

Problem 2: Fresh containers (verified age <1 min at inspect time) show only the
six built-in mounts:

  profiles/<profile>/cache/documents -> /root/.hermes/cache/documents
  profiles/<profile>/cache/images    -> /root/.hermes/cache/images
  profiles/<profile>/cache/web       -> /root/.hermes/cache/web
  profiles/<profile>/skills          -> /root/.hermes/skills
  profiles/<profile>/sandboxes/docker/default/home      -> /root
  profiles/<profile>/sandboxes/docker/default/workspace -> /workspace

The configured volume never appears, across multiple recreations and both
destination-path variants.

Source-inspection note (0.19.0, upstream 6b545824): gateway/run.py (~line 1626)
bridges terminal.docker_volumes to a JSON-encoded TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES env
var at startup; tools/terminal_tool.py (~line 1375) reads it via os.getenv when
building docker run. We could not determine where the value is dropped. Suggested
diagnostic: log the value written at the bridge and the value read in
terminal_tool — that shows which side fails without /proc inspection (which is
invalid here: /proc/<pid>/environ is an exec-time snapshot).

Current workaround: send images via Telegram (profile-scoped media path works).

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report uploaded:
  Report       https://paste.rs/QT6yG
  agent.log    https://dpaste.com/DZC576KV3
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/Z80DC
  gui.log      https://dpaste.com/866JH9FJ4
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream 6b545824

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
$ docker ps -a --filter "label=hermes-profile=moose-ads"
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE                                        COMMAND            CREATED          STATUS          PORTS     NAMES
255f18cb3374   nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20   "sleep infinity"   46 seconds ago   Up 46 seconds             hermes-f3231a3a

$ docker inspect 255f18cb3374 --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -> {{.Destination}}{{println}}{{end}}'
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/cache/images -> /root/.hermes/cache/images
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/cache/web -> /root/.hermes/cache/web
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/sandboxes/docker/default/home -> /root
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/sandboxes/docker/default/workspace -> /workspace
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/skills -> /root/.hermes/skills
/home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/moose-ads/cache/documents -> /root/.hermes/cache/documents

(Container created ~46s before inspect, i.e. freshly spawned after the config
edit + gateway restart + docker rm -f of all prior containers. The configured
docker_volumes entry — /home/hermes/.hermes/images:/home/hermes/.hermes/images:ro —
does not appear.)
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_
