items.title: [Bug]: /sessions and /models overlays invisible with ambient widget dock — cannot resume sessions or change models in TUI; /reload silent

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Impact (updated 2026-08-04)

**Day 13** since this broke. With ambient widgets loaded (the default for anyone using quota gauges, which is the documented TUI dock pattern), two core TUI workflows are dead:

1. **`/sessions`** (and `/switch` / `/resume`) — invisible blocked overlay. Prompt vanishes, no picker, Esc is the only exit. **Cannot resume or switch sessions.**
2. **`/models`** (model picker) — same failure. Cannot change the active model inside the TUI at all.

Both are blocking overlays (`$isBlocked` in `overlayStore.ts`) that render through `FloatingOverlays` → `WidgetGrid`. When the ambient widget dock is loaded, those overlays open into zero vertical space — they exist in state but cannot be seen or interacted with.

This means anyone running the ambient widget dock — the intended, documented setup for usage/quota widgets — **cannot load old sessions or change models from the TUI**. That is not a cosmetic glitch. It breaks two primary navigation surfaces.

Workaround of disabling ambient widgets is not acceptable as a daily driver; the dock is core UX for quota gauges and is the only reason the widget system exists.

Please re-triage severity: currently P2 / needs-repro, but repro is below and the functional impact is "cannot switch sessions or change models with widgets enabled."

## Problem

Typing `/sessions` (or `/switch`/`/resume`) or `/models` in the TUI opens an invisible overlay. The prompt line vanishes but no dialog appears — only `Esc` restores the prompt. The widget dock line (ambient widget cards above the composer) is the trigger.

Separately, `/reload` produces no visible feedback at all.

## Root cause: blocking overlays lose their layout anchor under ambient dock

The layout chain inside `ComposerPane` (`ui-tui/src/components/appLayout.tsx`):

```
<ComposerPane>
  <StatusRulePane at="top" />                              ← status bar (1 row)
  <AmbientDock placement="dock-top" />                     ← widget line (N rows)
  <Box position="relative">
    <FloatingOverlays />                                   ← position: absolute, bottom: 100%
    {!isBlocked && ( /* prompt/input */ )}
  </Box>
  <AmbientDock placement="dock-bottom" />                  ← bottom dock
  <StatusRulePane at="bottom" />
</ComposerPane>
```

When `/sessions` or `/models` fires `patchOverlayState({ sessions: true })` / `patchOverlayState({ modelPicker: true })`:

1. **Prompt hides correctly** — `$isBlocked` (overlayStore.ts:28-66) includes `sessions` and `modelPicker`, so `appLayout.tsx:384` `{!isBlocked && (...)}` hides the input line. This is working as designed.
2. **FloatingOverlays renders the overlay** — the `ActiveSessionSwitcher` or `ModelPicker` is placed into a `WidgetGrid` column inside a `position: absolute; bottom: 100%` box (`appOverlays.tsx:386-390`). It's supposed to float upward from the prompt position.

But the ambient widget dock at `dock-top` and the `StatusRulePane at="top"` consume real rows **above** the `position: relative` container. The floating overlay has zero or one row of vertical space to expand into before hitting the bottom of the ambient dock. The overlay still renders (at zero height), but is invisible.

Only `Esc` restores the prompt because `useInputHandlers.ts:421` catches `key.escape && overlay.sessions` (or `overlay.modelPicker`) and clears the overlay state.

**Affected blocking overlays** (all in `$isBlocked`, all rendered through `FloatingOverlays`):
- `sessions` — `/sessions`, `/switch`, `/resume`
- `modelPicker` — `/models`
- `skillsHub` — `/skills`
- `pluginsHub`
- `petPicker`
- `pager`

**Who sets the widget line:** User widgets in `$HERMES_HOME/tui-widgets/*.mjs` auto-launch via `sdk.openWidget(app, app.init(''))` on import (`ui-tui/src/sdk/userWidgets.ts` line 17 imports `openWidget`, and every widget file calls `if (!_opened) { _opened = true; sdk.openWidget(app, app.init('')) }`). This places them in `overlayState.ambient[]`. `AmbientDock` renders them at `dock-top`/`dock-bottom`, consuming real layout rows above the floating overlay.

## Root cause: `/reload` — guarded RPC handler swallows null response

The slash handler wrapper (`createSlashHandler.ts:27`) wraps every RPC callback with `ctx.guarded(fn)`:

```typescript
const guarded = <T>(fn: (r: T) => void) => (r: null | T): void => {
    if (!stale() && r) { fn(r) }
}
```

The `reload.env` RPC (`ops.ts:129-144`) sends `rpc('reload.env', {})` — no session_id. If the gateway returns `null` or `undefined`, `guarded()` bails silently. The user sees **nothing**.

## To reproduce

1. Have user widgets in `~/.hermes/tui-widgets/` (any ambient mode widget that auto-launches to the dock line)
2. Open TUI
3. Type `/sessions` (or `/models`) and press Enter
4. Expected: overlay appears between the ambient dock and the prompt area
5. Actual: prompt line disappears; no overlay visible; blank gap where the prompt was
6. Press `Esc` → prompt reappears (overlay state cleared)

## Fix direction

For blocking overlays: render them in-flow (not absolute) so they reserve real rows between the dock and the composer chrome. Completions can stay absolute since they float above a live prompt. PR #72208 implements exactly this split.

For `/reload`: print feedback before/during the RPC call (`sys('reloading .env …')`) so the guarded null-swallow can't silence the command entirely. Also handle the null case explicitly.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent TUI, current `main`
- User widgets loaded: 6+ ambient gauges in `$HERMES_HOME/tui-widgets/`
- Broken since 2026-07-22, still broken on 2026-08-04

items.title: state.db repair/re-corrupt cascade: schema surgery is only serialized in-process, and sqlite_master edits never bump the schema cookie

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Symptom

`state.db` gets repaired, then re-corrupts minutes later, repeatedly. On this host it happened four times in one day (17:54, 18:00, 22:05, 22:17), each time leaving another `state.db.malformed-backup-*` / `.prerepair-*` file behind.

```
Jul 22 17:54:47 ERROR hermes_state: state.db schema is malformed (fts5: error creating shadow table
                messages_fts_data: database disk image is malformed) — attempting automatic repair
Jul 22 17:54:47 ERROR hermes_state: state.db schema repair could not recover .../state.db automatically
Jul 22 18:00:16 ERROR hermes_state: state.db schema is malformed (...) — attempting automatic repair   <-- 6 min later
Jul 22 22:17:31 WARNING hermes_state: state.db write failed with an FTS-corruption error
                (database disk image is malformed) — attempting one-shot in-place FTS rebuild
Jul 22 22:17:32 WARNING hermes_state: state.db FTS indexes rebuilt in place (2); retrying the failed write.
Jul 22 22:17:32 WARNING gateway.session: state.db routing save failed: database disk image is malformed
```

Note the last two lines: the in-place rebuild reports success and the very next write fails again with the same error. Something is re-corrupting the file concurrently.

Filesystem is local ext4 (not NFS/virtiofs/SMB), so this is not #68545 or the WAL-on-network-fs class.

## Root cause

Two independent gaps, both in the `sqlite_master`-surgery path.

### 1. The repair lock is a `threading.Lock`, but the writers are separate processes

`_repair_attempt_lock` / `_claim_repair_attempt()` in `hermes_state.py` are documented as serialising "concurrent web_server / gateway opens against the same malformed file" — but a `threading.Lock` only covers threads inside one interpreter. `repair_state_db_schema()` itself has no cross-process guard at all, and it does `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON` + `DELETE FROM sqlite_master` + `VACUUM` on its own private connection.

A normal host has **four** independent processes on one `state.db`:

- `hermes-gateway.service`
- the Desktop app's own `hermes serve` backend — it spawns a full backend per launch, it is not a thin client (5 `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` lines in one day's `desktop.log` here)
- interactive CLI sessions
- `tui_gateway.slash_worker`

When two of them hit a malformed DB, both enter the critical section and each runs the full surgery while the other is mid-rewrite. That is the cascade: A repairs → B corrupts what A just wrote → B starts its own rebuild → …

Reproducible on current `main` — two processes calling `repair_state_db_schema()` on the same malformed DB both take a backup and both operate on `sqlite_master`.

### 2. Direct `sqlite_master` edits never bump the schema cookie

Ordinary DDL increments the schema cookie for free, and every other connection compares it before running a prepared statement — that is the mechanism by which they discard a cached schema. Editing `sqlite_master` under `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON` does **not** bump it.

So after the dedup strategy, a live connection in another process keeps compiling statements against the schema as it was *before* the surgery — including writing `messages` rows through triggers into `messages_fts*` shadow tables that were just deleted. SQLite's own `writable_schema` documentation calls out incrementing `schema_version` as the required companion to such an edit; the current code does not do it.

This one is a plain bug independent of the concurrency: strategy 2 happens to get away with it because its trailing `VACUUM` rewrites the file, strategy 1 (dedup) does not.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 26.04, local ext4, Python 3.11
- Gateway + Desktop backend + CLI on the same `~/.hermes/state.db`

## Fix

PR follows: bounded `flock` on `<db>.repair.lock` around the surgery (with the existing `_db_opens_cleanly()` check promoted to a double-check under the lock, so a queued process returns `already_healthy` instead of re-running surgery on a DB that was just repaired), plus a `schema_version` bump after each direct `sqlite_master` edit.

Related but distinct: #43742 makes the *in-process* claim loser retry instead of raising; it explicitly leaves `repair_state_db_schema()` unchanged and does nothing cross-process.

items.title: Desktop: session open ignores existing pagination and fetches the full active transcript

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

Desktop's session-read helper always requests the complete active transcript even though the backend already exposes `limit` and `offset` specifically to avoid loading an entire transcript.

`apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` currently builds:

```ts
path: `/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/messages${suffix}`
```

without pagination parameters. Cold and warm session resume paths then prefetch that full response (`use-session-actions`, session tile delegate, messaging reconciliation, artifacts, export, etc.). On the backend, `/api/sessions/{session_id}/messages` only applies its 500-row clamp when `limit` is supplied; omitted `limit` remains unbounded.

This becomes especially expensive because persisted user/tool messages may contain full `data:image/...;base64,...` values.

## Evidence from a real v0.19.0 database

Read-only aggregate measurements (no transcript content inspected or included):

- 120 sessions / 32,679 message rows; no orphan rows and no session message-count mismatches.
- 69 active message rows contain image data URLs.
- 5 active rows exceed 1 MiB; the largest active row is 7.81 MiB.
- The largest currently active transcript response is about 8.12 MiB for 73 messages.
- Across historical active transcripts, 76.91 MiB of serialized payload is eligible for these unbounded reads.

A single large row is enough to cause a visibly long session-open prefetch and large renderer allocations. The current code comment already recognizes that a "big session" affects resume wall time, but it still requests the whole transcript.

## Reproduction

1. Create a session with a few hundred active messages and several image/tool rows containing base64 image data.
2. Restart Desktop or select the session from a cold state.
3. Observe the request to `/api/sessions/<id>/messages` has no `limit` or cursor.
4. The backend reads, decodes, serializes, transfers, parses, and projects the complete active transcript before the cold prefetch resolves.

## Expected behavior

- Opening a session should fetch a bounded newest-message window.
- Older messages should load on demand as the user scrolls upward.
- Live gateway resume should reconcile against that bounded window rather than requiring a complete REST snapshot.
- Image payloads should ideally be represented by bounded thumbnails/asset references rather than repeated raw data URLs.

## Suggested approach

1. Add reverse/cursor pagination to the endpoint (`before_id`/`before_timestamp`, newest-first window, and `has_more` or total count). Offset-only ascending pagination cannot efficiently request the newest page without first knowing the count.
2. Change Desktop `getSessionMessages` to require a bounded window for interactive session opens (for example 100–200 messages).
3. Keep explicit full-transcript reads only for export, with progress/cancellation and a clearly named helper.
4. Load older windows from the virtualized timeline when the user approaches the top.
5. Add a regression test proving that cold resume does not issue an unbounded transcript request.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: v0.19.0, Linux build stamp `1bdd478efac6`
- Backend: v0.19.0
- Linux / KDE Plasma / Wayland
- Remote Desktop connection to the backend

items.title: Desktop keeps continuous RAF loops alive with terminal and pet roam enabled

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug description

Hermes Desktop keeps two continuous `requestAnimationFrame` loops alive after the terminal/log pane and pet roaming have been enabled:

1. `PersistentTerminal` calls `slot.getBoundingClientRect()` on every animation frame for the lifetime of the slot, even when its rectangle is unchanged. The component deliberately remains mounted after the pane has ever been opened.
2. `usePetRoam` schedules another animation frame in every phase, including the potentially long `pause` phase where it performs no DOM movement.

These loops prevent the corresponding renderer work from becoming fully event-driven and can also keep Chromium's GPU process active.

## Runtime observation and measurement caveat

After fixing an unrelated oversized Local Storage queue, restarting Desktop, waiting 60 seconds after the last **Hermes interaction**, and sampling `/proc` counters for 15 seconds, the Hermes process tree consumed:

- Total Desktop CPU: **24.91% of one CPU core**
- Renderer: **15.12%**
- GPU/zygote child: **6.73%**
- Main process: **2.86%**
- Total RSS: **1,179.3 MiB**
- Renderer RSS: **348.8 MiB**

**Correction / confounder:** the user later confirmed that the game *Per Aspera* was running during this delayed sample. The numbers above are still per-Hermes-process CPU counters, so the game's own CPU usage is not included. However, concurrent game/GPU/compositor load, display refresh behavior, and a visible Electron window on another monitor can affect how often Electron's renderer/GPU work is scheduled. Therefore this must be treated as **Hermes while otherwise interaction-idle but with a game running**, not a clean whole-machine idle baseline. The exact per-feature CPU impact still needs an A/B measurement with the game closed.

No agent turn, WebSocket reconnect, oversized Local Storage value, or Hermes log error occurred during the sample window. The relevant persisted settings were:

```text
hermes.desktop.logsOpen=true
hermes.desktop.terminalTakeover=true
hermes.desktop.pet-roam.v1=true
hermes.desktop.backdrop.v1=true
```

The source-level continuous loops are independently reproducible; the measurement establishes their presence under a real workload, not a definitive clean-idle CPU regression or their individual shares.

## Relevant code

### Persistent terminal

`apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/persistent.tsx`:

```ts
const tick = () => {
  const r = slot.getBoundingClientRect()
  // ...compare and maybe set state...
  frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick)
}
```

### Pet roam

`apps/desktop/src/components/pet/use-pet-roam.ts`:

```ts
switch (phase) {
  case 'pause':
    if (now >= pauseUntil) planNext(now)
    break
  // ...
}
raf = requestAnimationFrame(step)
```

## Expected behavior

An unchanged Desktop window should use event-driven geometry updates where possible, and animation frames should be requested only while something is actually moving or changing.

## Suggested fixes

1. Replace the terminal's permanent geometry RAF with event-driven observation:
   - `ResizeObserver` for size changes,
   - layout-tree/drag/resize subscriptions for position changes,
   - window/scroll listeners as needed,
   - a short RAF only while a pane is actively moving.
2. In pet roaming, use a timeout for the pause deadline and run RAF only during walk/jump/fall/drag phases.
3. Suspend both loops when `document.hidden`; honor reduced-motion/background throttling.
4. Add an automated idle performance case with terminal/logs mounted and pet roam enabled, asserting that frame callbacks/wakeups settle after layout stabilizes.
5. Repeat the CPU A/B with a controlled machine-idle baseline and each feature toggled independently.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: v0.19.0, Linux build stamp `1bdd478efac6`
- KDE Plasma / Wayland
- Local Linux Desktop build connected to a remote Hermes backend
- Concurrent game workload during the cited runtime sample (see caveat above)

items.title: [Bug]: New hardening breaks Obsidian skill and Hindsight use

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
## Bug Description

Three durable SQLite ledgers leak their connections on every operation,
eventually exhausting a long-running gateway's file-descriptor limit and
failing unrelated components with:

```text
[Errno 24] Too many open files
```

This is the same bug class as the cron execution ledger (#69567, fixed in
PR #69594), but in three ledgers that fix did not touch:

| Module | Leaking sites | Triggered by |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway/delivery_ledger.py` | 5 | every outbound final response (all platforms) |
| `tools/async_delegation.py` | 13 | every background delegation dispatch / completion / delivery-claim |
| `agent/verification_evidence.py` | 3 | every recorded terminal result, workspace edit, and status read |

`gateway/delivery_ledger.py` fires on essentially every delivered message, so
it is the highest-frequency leaker of the set.

## Root Cause

Each module opens connections with:

```python
with _connect() as conn:
    ...
```

`sqlite3.Connection`'s context manager commits or rolls back the transaction on
`__exit__`; it **does not close the connection**. No `conn.close()` is ever
called, so each call leaves the connection (and its `-wal` / `-shm` file
descriptors) open until the garbage collector eventually reclaims it. On a
long-running gateway process the descriptor count grows without bound.

There is no `.close()` or `contextlib.closing` anywhere in any of the three
modules.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with background delegations and/or active messaging
   platforms so `delivery_ledger` and `async_delegation` see traffic.
2. Record the gateway PID and count its descriptors:
   ```bash
   ls /proc/$PID/fd | wc -l
   ```
3. Deliver several messages / dispatch a few background delegations.
4. Count again and inspect targets:
   ```bash
   for fd in /proc/$PID/fd/*; do readlink "$fd"; done | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
   ```
5. Observe the count climbing, with extra descriptors pointing at `state.db`,
   `state.db-wal`, and `verification_evidence.db` after each operation.

## Expected Behavior

Ledger operations close their SQLite connections after each transaction; the
gateway's descriptor count stays approximately flat across repeated activity.

## Actual Behavior

Descriptors accumulate on every ledger call and are only released by GC, so a
busy gateway drifts toward its `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit and then fails
unrelated file/socket operations.

## Proposed Fix

Route every ledger operation through a `_transaction()` context manager that
guarantees `conn.close()` on exit (mirroring the accepted cron-ledger fix in
PR #69594), keeping `_connect()`'s schema-on-connect contract intact. I have a
branch with the fix plus per-module regression tests (asserting every opened
connection is closed, including the no-op-update and exception-mid-transaction
paths) and will open a PR.

## Affected Component

- Gateway (delivery ledger)
- Tools (async delegation ledger)
- Agent (verification evidence ledger)

items.title: Feature: Task Difficulty Router — use a cheap model to classify task complexity and route to the right model/provider

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem Background

Currently, Hermes Agent uses a single fixed model/provider per session. Whether the task is "check today's weather" or "analyze this 5000-line codebase and refactor it", the same model handles it. This causes:

- **Simple tasks overpaying**: Checking weather or translating a sentence uses the same expensive inference as complex work
- **Complex tasks underpowered**: When the default model is DeepSeek, tasks needing deep reasoning (architecture review, large-scale refactoring) may not get the capability they need
- **No dynamic routing**: Users must manually switch profiles or providers for different task types

## Goal

Introduce a **Task Difficulty Router** that evaluates task complexity with a **low-cost model** *before* the main agent loop, then automatically routes to the appropriate model/provider.

> **Core idea**: Let the task itself decide which model to use, not a fixed config.

## Proposed Design

### Routing Flow

```
User Message
    |
    v
+----------------------------+
|  Router (cheap model)      |  <- DeepSeek-V3 cache-hit / GLM-4.5-Flash / any low-$ model
|  - Analyze complexity      |
|  - Output difficulty tier  |
|  - Structured JSON         |
+------------+---------------+
             | difficulty: simple / medium / complex
             v
+----------------------------+
|  Route Decision            |  <- Configurable routing table
|  simple  -> cheap model    |
|  medium  -> default model  |
|  complex -> capable model  |
+------------+---------------+
             |
             v
    Agent Main Loop (selected model)
```

### Router Model Choice

- **Not a local model** (latency and accuracy requirements)
- Recommended: DeepSeek-V3 (ultra-low cache-hit price), GLM-4.5-Flash, or similar lightweight API models
- Router output should be structured JSON:

```json
{
  "difficulty": "simple",
  "reasoning": "User is asking for the current time, no external resources needed",
  "recommended_capability": "basic",
  "needs_tools": false,
  "needs_web_search": false
}
```

### Difficulty Tiers

| Tier | Definition | Example | Route Target |
|------|------------|---------|--------------|
| `simple` | Common knowledge, no tools, single-turn | Weather check, translation, "what time is it" | Flash / cheap model |
| `medium` | Needs reasoning or multi-step, simple tool use | Data analysis, code explanation, file ops | Default model |
| `complex` | Deep reasoning, large context, complex toolchains | Architecture review, major refactor, multi-stage research | High-capability model |

### Config Example

```yaml
router:
  enabled: true
  provider: deepseek
  model: deepseek-v3-flash       # cheap router model
  difficulty_tiers:
    simple:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-v3-flash
    medium:
      provider: openrouter       # inherit user default
      model: null                # null = use session default model
    complex:
      provider: anthropic
      model: claude-sonnet-4
  timeout: 5s                    # router timeout
  fallback_provider: openrouter  # degrade if router fails
  fallback_model: deepseek-v3
  cache_ttl: 300                 # cache routing results for similar tasks
```

### Routing Cache

Within the same session, semantically similar task patterns can cache their routing result to avoid calling the router model every turn.

### User Visibility

- Default: transparent (no user interruption)
- Optional: show routing info in reply footer or status bar
- `/route` command to manually override the difficulty tier
- Config override: `config set router.override simple` to force-lock a tier

## Open Questions

1. **Router overhead**: Every user message triggers an extra API call. Even if cheap, the latency and token cost aren't zero. Mitigation: routing cache enabled by default.
2. **Classification accuracy**: Router misclassifications (simple->complex, complex->simple) -- the former burns money, the latter under-delivers. Needs prompt tuning in real use.
3. **Tool impact on difficulty**: A task may look simple but requires heavy web search ("fetch the last 10 news articles"). The router should weight "needs_tools" in its decision.
4. **User override**: Should `config set router.override simple` let a user force-lock the routing tier regardless of classifier output?
5. **Interaction with fallback chains**: Router output should be the **primary** selection, with existing fallback chains as safety net.

items.title: feat(delegation): allow per-task model selection in delegate_task
items.body:
## Problem

`delegate_task` currently inherits the parent agent model for all spawned subagents. There is no way to assign different models to different subagents within the same batch.

## Use Case

A user wants to review a PR with three parallel reviewers, each using a different model suited to their focus:

```
delegate_task(
    tasks=[
        {"goal": "Security audit of the diff",       "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"},
        {"goal": "Architecture review",               "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro"},
        {"goal": "Quick style + naming scan",         "model": "qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23"},
    ]
)
```

Currently the only workaround is to:
1. Change `delegation.model` in config.yaml (pins ALL subagents — can't mix models)
2. Switch the active model before each `delegate_task` call (manual, loses parallelism)

## Proposed Solution

Add optional `model` and `provider` fields to each item in the `tasks` array of `delegate_task`:

```
{
    "goal": "...",
    "model": "model-name",    # optional — overrides parent model for this subagent
    "provider": "provider"     # optional — overrides parent provider
}
```

When `model` is set on a task item, that subagent uses the specified model (and provider, if given) instead of inheriting the parent model. When unset, current inheritance behavior is preserved.

### Context Merging Rules

The `context` field already exists at both levels today — top-level `context` merges with per-task `context`. This proposal extends the same pattern to `model`/`provider`:

| Level | Field | Inheritance |
|:------|:------|:------------|
| Top-level `context` | Shared context string | ✅ Merged into every subagent |
| Top-level `model` / `provider` | Default for all tasks | ✅ Used as fallback when per-task is unset |
| Per-task `context` | Task-specific context | ✅ Appended to top-level context for that subagent |
| Per-task `model` / `provider` | Per-task override | ✅ Overrides top-level for that subagent |

Example showing all levels together:

```python
delegate_task(
    context="Repo: hermes-agent. Branch: feat/whatsapp-history-api. Responde en español.",
    model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash",  # default for all tasks
    provider="nous",
    tasks=[
        {
            "goal": "Security audit of the WhatsApp bridge",
            "context": "Enfócate en inyección XSS y fuga de datos en endpoints HTTP",
            "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",  # override
        },
        {
            "goal": "Verify config.yaml and plugin.yaml documentation",
            # No model override → uses top-level deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
        },
    ]
)
```

## Safety Gate

Gate behind an environment variable to avoid cost surprises:

- `HERMES_DELEGATION_PER_TASK_MODEL` (default: `false`)
- When `false`, the `model`/`provider` fields in task items are silently ignored

## Implementation Sketch

In the delegation dispatch code, when spawning a child session:

```
child_model = task.get("model") if os.environ.get("HERMES_DELEGATION_PER_TASK_MODEL") == "true" else None
child_provider = task.get("provider") if os.environ.get("HERMES_DELEGATION_PER_TASK_MODEL") == "true" else None

# Fall back to parent model if not specified or gate is off
model = child_model or parent_model
provider = child_provider or parent_provider
```

## Alternatives Considered

- **`config.yaml` delegation.model** — pins all subagents, no per-task granularity
- **Multiple sequential `delegate_task` calls with model switching** — loses parallelism, more complex
- **Model routing via `auxiliary` config** — auxiliary models are tool-scoped, not agent-scoped

items.title: [Bug] auth: GBK codec fails to parse auth.json path when Windows username contains CJK characters

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
On Windows with a CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) username, the `hermes_cli.auth` module fails to parse `auth.json` on every startup. The root cause is that the module reads the file path string using the system default encoding (GBK on Chinese Windows) instead of UTF-8, but the path contains UTF-8 encoded CJK characters that are illegal in GBK.

This results in a flood of warnings on every startup (observed 30+ identical warnings per boot), and the auth store starts empty each time. While it doesn't crash the application directly, it causes:

1. Excessive logging noise
2. Auth store being reset to empty on each startup
3. `auth.json.corrupt` backup files being created repeatedly
4. Increased memory pressure during startup (the warning handler is invoked dozens of times)

## Error Output

```
WARNING hermes_cli.auth: auth: failed to parse C:\Users\<CJK_username>\AppData\Roaming\cn.org.hermesagent.desktop\runtime\hermes-home\auth.json ('gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xaf in position 78: illegal multibyte sequence) — starting with empty store. Corrupt file preserved at C:\Users\<CJK_username>\AppData\Roaming\cn.org.hermesagent.desktop\runtime\hermes-home\auth.json.corrupt
```

This warning appears **30+ times** per startup cycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Windows user account with CJK characters in the username (e.g., Chinese characters)
2. Install and configure Hermes Agent (any recent version)
3. Add a custom provider with a CJK label in `config.yaml` (e.g., a provider name containing Chinese characters)
4. Launch Hermes — observe the repeated GBK warnings in `errors.log`
5. Check that `auth.json.corrupt` is created alongside `auth.json`

## Root Cause Analysis

The `auth.json` file itself is valid UTF-8 JSON. The problem is NOT the file content — it's the **file path string** passed to the JSON parser.

When Python's `open()` or similar file-reading function is called without explicitly specifying `encoding='utf-8'`, it falls back to the system default encoding. On Chinese Windows, this is GBK (`cp936`). The CJK characters in the Windows user profile path are UTF-8 encoded on disk, but the path string is being decoded as GBK, causing the decode error at position 78 (which corresponds to the first CJK character in the username path).

Evidence:
- The hex bytes at the relevant position decode correctly as UTF-8 to CJK characters, but fail under GBK decoding.
- The file content is valid JSON when read with UTF-8 encoding.
- The `auth.json.corrupt` backup is identical in size and content to the original `auth.json` — confirming the file is not actually corrupt.

## Proposed Fix

In the `hermes_cli.auth` module, ensure that `auth.json` is always opened with explicit `encoding='utf-8'`:

```python
# Before (buggy — uses system default encoding):
with open(auth_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# After (fixed — explicitly uses UTF-8):
with open(auth_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = json.load(f)
```

This is a one-line fix that resolves the issue for all CJK Windows users.

## Affected Component

CLI / Core Runtime (`hermes_cli.auth`)

## Operating System

Windows 11 (Chinese locale, system default encoding: GBK/cp936)

## Hermes Version

0.17.0-cn.5 through 0.18.2 (observed across multiple versions)

## Additional Context

This bug only affects Windows users with CJK characters in their username path. It's likely underreported because:
- CJK users may not realize the repeated warnings indicate a real bug
- The app still functions (auth store is regenerated), so the impact appears cosmetic
- No English-language users encounter this, reducing visibility

Related to the broader Windows desktop stability issues tracked in #69016 (renderer OOM) — the excessive warning logging during startup may contribute to memory pressure.

items.title: supports_vision override not resolved for CLI --provider with named custom_providers

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Report

**Filed by:** GLaDOS (AI agent, Hermes Agent) — supervised by a human operator.

### Summary

When a user explicitly passes `--provider <name>` on the CLI (where `<name>` is a named custom provider declared under `custom_providers`), the runtime resolves the provider ID to the generic string `"custom"`. The `supports_vision` override lookup in `agent/image_routing.py` (`_supports_vision_override`) fails to match the user-declared provider name against the `custom_providers` list, so the override is never found — even though it is correctly declared in `config.yaml`.

### Background

`vision_analyze` has a native fast path (`_should_use_native_vision_fast_path` in `tools/vision_tools.py`) that short-circuits the auxiliary vision LLM when the active main model supports native vision. The escape hatch for custom/local providers is `supports_vision: true` declared in `config.yaml` under the provider's model entry.

The resolution chain in `_supports_vision_override` (`agent/image_routing.py`):

1. `model.supports_vision` (top-level shortcut)
2. `providers.<provider>.models.<model>.supports_vision` (dict-style providers)
3. Legacy `custom_providers` list — match by `name` field against candidate names derived from the runtime provider and `model.provider`

### Root Cause

When `--provider <name>` is passed on the CLI (where `<name>` is a named custom provider), the runtime resolves the provider to `"custom"` (via `_resolve_named_custom_runtime`). The override lookup then generates candidate names from:

- `provider` → `"custom"`
- `config_provider` → `model.provider` from config.yaml (the **default** model's provider, not the CLI override) — e.g. `"custom:litellm"`
- `stripped_suffix` → derived from `config_provider` — e.g. `"litellm"`

None of these candidates match the actual named custom provider the user selected on the CLI (e.g. `"kimi-free-proxy"`), so the search through the `custom_providers` list finds nothing and `supports_vision` is never resolved. The function returns `None`, `decide_image_input_mode` falls back to `"text"`, and the native fast path is skipped — silently routing through the auxiliary vision LLM instead.

### Reproduction

1. Declare a named custom provider with `supports_vision: true` in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  - name: my-vision-provider
    base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1
    api_mode: chat_completions
    key_env: MY_API_KEY
    models:
      my-model:
        supports_vision: true
```

2. Verify the override resolves when testing with the explicit name:
```python
from agent.image_routing import _lookup_supports_vision, _supports_vision_override
from hermes_cli.config import load_config
cfg = load_config()
print(_supports_vision_override(cfg, "my-vision-provider", "my-model"))  # True
print(_lookup_supports_vision("my-vision-provider", "my-model", cfg))     # True
```

3. Run a vision test with the CLI:
```bash
hermes chat -q "describe /tmp/image.jpg" -m my-model --provider my-vision-provider
```

4. Observe agent.log: `Processing image with vision model...` — the auxiliary path is taken, not the native fast path.

### Expected Behavior

`_supports_vision_override` should resolve `supports_vision: true` from the `custom_providers` entry the user explicitly selected via `--provider`.

### Actual Behavior

The runtime provider ID is `"custom"` (generic), not the named provider. The candidate names generated for matching do not include the original provider name passed on the CLI, so the lookup fails and silently falls back to the auxiliary vision LLM.

### Suggested Fix Direction

The CLI-provided provider name (before resolution to `"custom"`) should be propagated as a candidate in `_supports_vision_override`, so the `custom_providers` list can be searched by the user-declared name. Alternatively, the runtime override (`set_runtime_main`) could retain the original named provider name alongside the resolved `"custom"` ID.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent: current `main` branch
- Affected file: `agent/image_routing.py` — `_supports_vision_override()` (lines ~180-264)
- Related: `tools/vision_tools.py` — `_should_use_native_vision_fast_path()` (lines ~832-858)
- Provider resolution: `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` — `_resolve_named_custom_runtime`

### Workaround

Routing the same model through a provider entry that is already in the hardcoded `_supports_media_in_tool_results` allowlist (e.g. `openai`, `anthropic`) bypasses the issue. Alternatively, using the default model's provider (where `model.provider` in `config.yaml` matches the custom provider name) works because `config_provider` is included in the candidate set.

items.body:
## Bug Description

After upgrading from v0.18.2 to v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), typing in the Hermes Desktop composer becomes extremely laggy (200-500ms keystroke delay) on a fresh conversation — not just long ones. The lag persists across restarts and new conversations.

The desktop logs show:

```
[hermes] [renderer console] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
[hermes] [renderer console] Uncaught (in promise) Error: Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 60000ms
```

Rolling back to v2026.7.7.2 (v0.18.2) via git checkout immediately resolves the issue — typing is smooth again.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Upgrade to Hermes v0.19.0 on Windows 10/11
2. Open Hermes Desktop
3. Type in the composer — noticeable keystroke delay on every character
4. Open DevTools (Ctrl+Shift+I) — see ResizeObserver loop warnings
5. Start a `/new` conversation — same lag persists

## Expected Behavior

Typing in the composer should be responsive regardless of version.

## Actual Behavior

Every keystroke has a visible delay. Desktop app is borderline unusable.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10 22H2
- **Hermes version:** v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release (git commit e5b83633)
- **GPU:** Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (driver 32.0.101.7085, March 2026)
- **Display:** 1920x1200
- **RAM:** 32GB
- **Desktop App:** Electron-based (packaged build)

## Workaround

```bash
cd <hermes-agent-dir>
git checkout v2026.7.7.2
```

Rolling back to v0.18.2 resolves the issue immediately. The version mismatch warning between the v0.19 desktop app and v0.18.2 backend is cosmetic and doesn't affect functionality.

## Additional Context

The v0.19 release notes mention a ~20-PR desktop speed overhaul (14x faster streaming markdown, virtualized diffs, snappy session switching). One of these changes introduced a layout thrashing issue — the ResizeObserver loop warning suggests the renderer is struggling to process resize notifications within single animation frames, causing the compositor to skip frames on every interaction.

items.title: [Feature]: inject workflow vault env vars from task.metadata in kanban _default_spawn

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Summary

Add support for ephemeral shared memory across multi-agent kanban workflows by injecting `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKFLOW_VAULT` and `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKFLOW_TOKEN` env vars from `task.metadata.workflow_vault` when spawning workers.

## Problem

Currently, each kanban worker profile has its own MuninnDB vault (e.g., `hermes-researcher`, `hermes-coder`). Workers cannot see each other's memories without cross-vault entity graph lookups, which is complex and fragile.

For workflows where multiple agents need shared memory (research → analyze → implement), we need a way for all agents in a workflow to read/write to the same ephemeral vault.

## Solution

MuninnDB supports workflow vaults (`wf-*` prefix) with TTL and capability tokens. The orchestrator can create a workflow vault and pass it to all tasks via metadata.

### Changes needed in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` → `_default_spawn()`:

```python
# After env["HERMES_PROFILE"] = profile_arg

# Workflow vault injection: when task.metadata.workflow_vault is set,
# inject env vars so the MuninnDB plugin uses the ephemeral shared
# vault instead of the profile-scoped vault.  This gives all agents
# in a workflow shared memory for the duration of that workflow.
if task.metadata and "workflow_vault" in task.metadata:
    wv = task.metadata["workflow_vault"]
    if isinstance(wv, dict):
        if wv.get("name"):
            env["HERMES_KANBAN_WORKFLOW_VAULT"] = wv["name"]
        if wv.get("token"):
            env["HERMES_KANBAN_WORKFLOW_TOKEN"] = wv["token"]
```

### Metadata schema:

```json
{
  "workflow_vault": {
    "name": "wf-<identifier>",
    "token": "***"
  }
}
```

## Use case

```python
# Orchestrator creates workflow vault
vault = muninn_create_workflow_vault(name="wf-doc-processing", ttl_hours=24)

# All tasks share the vault via metadata
workflow_meta = {
    "required_tools": ["muninndb", ...],
    "workflow_vault": {
        "name": vault["vault_name"],
        "token": vault["capability_secret"]
    }
}

t1 = kanban_create(title="research", assignee="researcher", metadata=workflow_meta)
t2 = kanban_create(title="analyze", assignee="analyzer", parents=[t1], metadata=workflow_meta)
# Both workers now share the same wf-doc-processing vault
```

## Implementation status

- ✅ MuninnDB plugin: already merged and released (checks `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKFLOW_VAULT/TOKEN` env vars)
- ⚠️ Dispatcher: patch applied locally, needs upstreaming
- ✅ Skill: `workflow-vault-pattern` documents the full orchestrator playbook

## Related

- MuninnDB plugin PR: https://github.com/madeinoz67/hermes-memory-muninndb/commit/a9fd63a
- Feature: MuninnDB workflow vaults (RFC [#597](https://github.com/scrypster/muninndb/issues/597))
- Security: capability tokens are TTL-mandatory, recursion-safe, namespace-scoped

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Bug Report: Host Path Leakage in File Attachment Orchestration (v0.19.0)

**Severity:** High (Critical for Agent Functionality in Sandbox Environments)
**Version:** 0.19.0 (Windows Desktop App)
**Backend Environment:** WSL2 / Docker Container (`/root` environment)

---

## Description
There is a critical flaw in the orchestration layer between the Windows Host and the Linux-based Agent sandbox during file attachments.

When a user utilizes the "Attach File" function via the chat interface, the application fails to resolve and map the local host path (e.g., `C:/Users/[USER]/[DIR]/[FILE_NAME].jpg`) to the corresponding temporary directory within the Docker container (e.g., `/root/tmp/[uuid].png`). Instead, the orchestration logic passes the raw **Windows Host Path** directly into the AI Agent's context for tool calls.

Since the agent operates within an isolated sandbox with no access to the host's `C:` drive architecture, all file-dependent queries using these attached files fail with a `"file not reachable"` error.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Hermes Desktop on Windows.
2. Use the **"+" (Attach)** button in the chat interface.
3. Select an image or document from a local folder (e.g., `C:/Users/[USER]/[DIR]/[FILE_NAME].jpg`).
4. Observe that while the file appears in the chat UI, the agent receives the exact Windows path string as its input parameter for the tool call.

### Expected Behavior

Upon successful upload via the "Attach" button:
1. The Client should transfer the file to the container's temporary storage (e.g., `/root/tmp/[random_name].png`).
2. The Orchestrator must intercept the host-based path and replace it with the **internal, sandboxed container path**.
3. The Agent receives the internal, valid path (e.g., `image_url: "/root/tmp/[random_name].png"`), allowing successful tool execution.


### Actual Behavior

The application leaks the host-based Windows absolute path into the agent's instruction context, rendering the attachment inaccessible to the isolated LLM/Agent process.

items.title: [Bug]: Bundled SQLite 3.50.4 hits upstream WAL-reset corruption; clean on 3.51.3

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

Hermes' current uv-managed Python runtime embeds SQLite **3.50.4**, which is in the affected range for SQLite's newly documented **WAL-reset corruption bug**. A Hermes kanban churn harness that repeatedly corrupts on 3.50.4 completed cleanly when the SQLite library alone was changed to fixed 3.51.3.

This provides an upstream root-cause candidate for the recurring `kanban.db` / `state.db` corruption reports that have previously been attributed more generally to multi-process WAL access.

SQLite's documentation:

- WAL-reset bug description and affected/fixed versions: https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug
- "How To Corrupt" §8.1 (separate threads/processes, overlapping writers/checkpointers): https://www.sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html
- SQLite 3.51.3 release note recording the fix: https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_51_3.html
- SQLite 3.50.7 backport: https://sqlite.org/src/info/c7facf7ac58d2cda

SQLite documents the main affected range as 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, with the fix in 3.51.3 and backports including 3.50.7 and 3.44.6.

## Why Hermes matches the upstream trigger

The upstream race requires:

1. WAL mode;
2. two or more connections in separate threads/processes;
3. overlapping writes/checkpoints, including WAL reset/wraparound.

Hermes has exactly this topology: gateway, dispatcher, dashboard/CLI, cron and worker processes open the shared WAL databases, while auto-checkpoints and last-connection-close checkpoints overlap continued writes. The resulting damage also matches: table/index disagreement after a partially reflected transaction, often with an empty/truncated WAL.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- Python 3.11.15
- bundled SQLite 3.50.4
- SQLite source id: `2025-07-30 19:33:53 4d8adfb30e03f9cf27f800a2c1ba3c48fb4ca1b08b0f5ed59a4d5ecbf45e20a3`
- Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2
- database located on local `/dev/sdc` ext4 (`data=ordered`), **not** `/mnt/c`/DrvFS

This was observed under WSL2, but the storage location and SQLite's cross-platform race make WSL an unlikely prerequisite.

I also installed the currently available uv-managed CPython 3.13.13 in isolation. It embeds the same SQLite 3.50.4/source id, so changing the Python minor or reinstalling uv's Python does not currently resolve this.

## Reproduction and A/B result

The throwaway-board harness uses the real Hermes schema/connect path:

- one long-lived ticker connection;
- about 830 short-lived worker processes over 150 seconds;
- repeated fresh read-only health probes followed by fresh read/write connections and an early `BEGIN IMMEDIATE; SELECT; COMMIT` transaction;
- `wal_autocheckpoint=1000`;
- concurrent event writes, randomized process kills, periodic integrity checks and final page-cache eviction;
- never touches a live board.

Same `migwritetxnall1000` arm:

| SQLite | Workers | SIGKILLs | Mid-run anomalies | Final cache | Final disk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 3.50.4, run 1 | 846 | 77 | **14** | **corrupt** | **corrupt** |
| 3.50.4, run 2 | 855 | 75 | **18** | **corrupt** | **corrupt** |
| 3.51.3 | 837 | 38 | **0** | **clean** | **clean** |

Representative 3.50.4 result:

```text
Tree 9 page 499 cell 16: Rowid 6604 out of order
wrong # of entries in index idx_events_run
wrong # of entries in index idx_events_task
idx_task_delta=-1, idx_run_delta=-1
```

Fixed run:

```text
FINAL-CACHE: {"integrity":"ok","idx_task_delta":0,"idx_run_delta":0}
FINAL-DISK:  {"integrity":"ok","idx_task_delta":0,"idx_run_delta":0}
SUMMARY: spawned=837 sigkilled=38 mid-run-anomalies=0 final-cache=clean final-disk=clean
```

This is one fixed-version run rather than a proof over every possible schedule, but combined with two deterministic vulnerable runs and the exact upstream trigger/signature match, it is strong evidence that Hermes is exposed to the SQLite bug.

## Expected behavior

Hermes should not run its multi-process WAL databases on a SQLite version known to contain a database-corruption race.

## Actual behavior

The installer selects uv-managed Python builds containing SQLite 3.50.4. Health probes, quarantine and narrow auto-REINDEX can detect or repair some damage after it happens, but do not prevent the vulnerable SQLite checkpointer from producing it again.

## Suggested upstream response

Could maintainers consider:

1. **Ship/select a runtime with fixed SQLite** (3.51.3+, or a fixed backport such as 3.50.7).
2. **Version-gate WAL before opening shared databases.** On a vulnerable runtime, fail safely or deliberately fall back to rollback-journal mode after safely draining any existing WAL.
3. Report both Python and SQLite versions/source ids in `hermes doctor` and debug reports.
4. Add this process-churn workload as a runtime qualification test.
5. Document that `hermes update` / changing Python versions does not necessarily change the SQLite embedded by `python-build-standalone`.

A simple `pysqlite3` import swap is not currently a safe upstream fix: the latest published `pysqlite3-binary` available here embeds vulnerable SQLite 3.51.1. A custom 3.51.3 build passed the kanban suites and the corruption harness, but exposed DB-API transaction-behavior differences in 9 `hermes_state` tests, so it should not be adopted globally without compatibility work.

## Related Hermes work/reports

- #41795 — health re-probing/quarantine mitigation and the original harness investigation
- #68654 — merged auto-REINDEX, backup retention and checkpoint/repair work; useful recovery, but post-corruption
- #33169 — earlier kanban `idx_events_run` corruption report on SQLite 3.50.4, closed after application-level hardening
- #5563 — public `state.db` malformed/B-tree corruption reports under gateway + cron concurrency
- #57820 — open proposal to permit rollback-journal mode

I can provide the full harness and raw logs or turn the runtime check/fallback into a focused PR once maintainers indicate the preferred packaging strategy.

items.title: Feature Request: Add Ollama Web Search as a search backend

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw ships a bundled `ollama` web_search provider that routes through Ollama's `/api/experimental/web_search` endpoint (or `https://ollama.com/api/web_search` for cloud). This means OpenClaw users with Ollama Cloud don't need a separate search API key — the same Ollama Cloud credential handles both model inference and web search.

Hermes currently requires a separate search provider API key (Brave, Exa, Firecrawl, etc.) even when using Ollama Cloud as the model provider. This adds friction for users who want a single-credential setup.

## Proposed Solution

Add an `ollama` search backend to Hermes that mirrors what OpenClaw does:

1. **Local Ollama:** Hit `{baseUrl}/api/experimental/web_search` (defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`) — the local daemon signs and forwards to Ollama Cloud.
2. **Ollama Cloud (no local daemon):** Hit `https://ollama.com/api/web_search` with the `OLLAMA_API_KEY` as bearer auth.
3. **Fallback chain:** Try local proxy endpoint first, then direct cloud, with the API key as a last resort.

The search backend would reuse the existing `ollama-cloud` provider's `base_url` and API key from config, so no new env vars needed.

## Implementation Sketch

- New search backend in the web plugin system (similar to `brave-free`, `firecrawl`, etc.)
- Check `OLLAMA_API_KEY` env var and/or `ollama-cloud` provider config
- Route to `{baseUrl}/api/experimental/web_search` or `https://ollama.com/api/web_search`
- Return titles, URLs, snippets (same shape as other search backends)

## Alternatives Considered

- Keeping the status quo (separate Brave/Exa key) — works but adds credential overhead
- Adding a generic "reuse model provider for search" abstraction — more complex, less clear

## References

- OpenClaw's Ollama web search docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/ollama-search
- Ollama's web search API endpoint: `/api/experimental/web_search`

items.title: Desktop app never shows credit usage warnings — notification.show events are silently dropped
items.body:
Credit warnings like `• Credits 50% used · $220.00 cap` never show up in the desktop app. The backend already sends them to the desktop — the renderer just has no handler for them, so they are silently thrown away. **The fix is desktop-only.** The central event switch in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts` (~lines 237–895) has no branch for `notification.show` or `notification.clear`, and no fallback branch either. Nothing needs to change in the agent core or the gateway. ```mermaid flowchart LR H["Nous API response
x-nous-credits-* headers"] --> T["credits_tracker.py
50 / 75 / 90% bands"] T --> G["tui_gateway server
WS events:
notification.show / .clear"] G --> I["Ink TUI
renders in status bar ✓"] G --> D["Desktop renderer
gateway-event.ts
no handler, dropped ✗"] style I stroke:#2da44e,stroke-width:2px style D stroke:#cf222e,stroke-width:2px ``` ## Naming, quickly The same thing goes by three names depending on the layer. A **notice** is the struct the agent emits. On the wire it is the **`notification.show` event**, with payload `{text, level, kind, ttl_ms, key, id}`. In the desktop it should become a **toast**. Two fields are easy to mix up: - `level` is severity: `info | warn | error | success`. - `kind` is lifetime: `sticky` (stays until explicitly cleared) or `ttl` (expires after `ttl_ms`). There are four notices: | `key` | Example text | `level` | Lifetime | |---|---|---|---| | `credits.usage` | `• Credits 50% used · $220.00 cap` | info, then warn at 75/90% | Sticky. One line that escalates 50→75→90; each replaces the last. | | `credits.grant_spent` | `• Grant spent · $12.00 top-up left` | info | Sticky | | `credits.depleted` | `✕ Credit access paused · run /topup to top up` | error | Sticky | | `credits.restored` | `✓ Credit access restored` | success | TTL, 8s | ## Suggested implementation 1. **Subscribe to the two events.** Either add cases to the `gateway-event.ts` switch, or mount a single scoped subscriber near the session wiring: `gateway.on('notification.show', …)` / `gateway.on('notification.clear', …)`. The billing step-up flow already does the scoped-subscriber pattern at `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/billing/use-step-up.ts:85`, and it keeps this change out of the giant switch. 2. **Render as toasts** with `notify()` from `apps/desktop/src/store/notifications.ts`: - `level` → toast kind (info/warning/error/success map 1:1). - `sticky` → `durationMs: 0`, `ttl` → `durationMs: ttl_ms`. - Use the notice `key` as the toast `id`. `notify({id})` replaces an existing toast with the same id (`notifications.ts:144`), which gives you the 50→75→90 escalation for free, and lets `notification.clear` map to `dismissNotification(key)`. 3. **Optional: native OS notification** for the urgent pair (`credits.depleted`, `credits.restored`) via `dispatchNativeNotification()` in `apps/desktop/src/store/native-notifications.ts`. Needs a new `NativeNotificationKind` (none of the existing five fit) plus a toggle in `notifications-settings.tsx`. No Electron-main change; `hermes:notify` already takes any title/body. 4. **Optional: nudge the Billing page.** Settings → Billing polls `billing.state` every 30s. Invalidating that query when a notice arrives makes the page reflect the crossing immediately. ## Done when - Crossing the 50% band mid-session shows a toast in the desktop app. - The 75% warning replaces the 50% toast instead of stacking. - The `✓ Credit access restored` toast disappears on its own after ~8s. - `notification.clear` dismisses the matching toast. The Ink TUI is the reference for all of this behavior: `ui-tui/src/app/turnController.ts:173-230` (latest-wins, sticky vs TTL, key-matched clear). ## Gotchas - The notice text already starts with its glyph (`•` `⚠` `✕` `✓`). Don't add another icon. - No desktop-side gate is needed: notices only fire on the Nous provider, and the existing `display.credits_notices` config toggle already controls them upstream.
Background: how a notice reaches the desktop's wire (read-only context, no changes needed here) - After each turn, `agent/credits_tracker.py` parses the `x-nous-credits-*` response headers (Nous inference gateway only) and evaluates the bands in `CREDITS_USAGE_BANDS` (`credits_tracker.py:166-170`). The `AgentNotice` struct is at `:177-194`. A session that opens already inside a band warns immediately via `seed_credits_at_session_start` (`:741`). - `run_agent.py` emits through `_capture_credits` → `_emit_credits_notices` (~`run_agent.py:3418-3534`) to whatever `notice_callback` the front-end bound. - The TUI/desktop gateway binds that callback in `tui_gateway/server.py:4503-4520` and turns it into the `notification.show` / `notification.clear` WS events (spec: `tests/run_agent/test_notice_spine.py:118-206`). - The desktop connects to that same engine: Electron spawns `hermes serve` (`apps/desktop/electron/backend-command.ts`) → `/api/ws` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` → `tui_gateway.ws.handle_ws`. Every inbound event fans out through `JsonRpcGatewayClient.dispatchEvent` (`apps/shared/src/json-rpc-gateway.ts:390-398`) into the handler that currently drops these two.
## Related - #69809 — companion issue: broadcast the same notices to messaging-gateway home channels. - `docs/design/billing-ux-mockup-handoff.md` — copy/color reference from the terminal + portal workstream (thresholds and copy are shared via `credits_tracker.py`).

items.title: TUI auto-scroll to bottom during agent output

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Problem
When Hermes runs in TUI mode, long tool output streams into the conversation but scroll position stays fixed. The user must manually scroll down (Ctrl+End or mouse wheel) to see the latest output — missing real-time progress during long agent runs.

## Proposed solution
**"Follow" mode** for the TUI output pane:
- When scrolled to bottom → **auto-follow** new output
- When scrolled up manually → **pin** position (stop following)
- Standard pattern: `less -F`, Telegram, Discord, CI log viewers all do this

## Why
Without auto-scroll, TUI feels less interactive than CLI mode — the "live" feeling of watching the agent work is lost. Every user who runs long tool calls hits this.

## Possible path
Scroll logic in `ui-tui/src/app/scroll.ts`. A hook that detects bottom-of-viewport and calls `scrollRef.current.scrollToBottom()` on new content. Reset on user scroll-up.

items.title: [Bug]: CLI custom provider override loses native vision identity

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

Native image routing loses the named custom-provider identity when the active model and provider are selected on the command line.

For example, a profile may have `ollama-cloud/glm-5.2` as its configured default and a named custom provider with per-model vision metadata:

```yaml
model:
  default: ollama-cloud/glm-5.2
  provider: ollama-cloud

providers:
  qwen-token-plan:
    base_url: https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
    models:
      qwen3.8-max-preview:
        supports_vision: true
```

Starting chat with:

```shell
hermes -p sven chat -m qwen3.8-max-preview --provider custom:qwen-token-plan
```

resolves the custom endpoint correctly, but stores the live provider as bare `custom`. Image capability lookup can no longer find `providers.qwen-token-plan.models.qwen3.8-max-preview.supports_vision`, so `agent.image_input_mode: auto` selects the text or auxiliary vision path. The image is analyzed through `vision_analyze` instead of being sent to the selected model as native image content.

This is the remaining real CLI path after #69814. That fix handles a routing call that already receives `custom:<name>`, but initial CLI provider resolution supplies bare `custom` downstream.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a profile with a default provider other than the named custom provider.
2. Add `providers.qwen-token-plan.models.qwen3.8-max-preview.supports_vision: true`.
3. Start Hermes with:

```shell
hermes -p sven chat -m qwen3.8-max-preview --provider custom:qwen-token-plan
```

4. Attach an image and ask the model to inspect it.
5. Observe that Hermes runs the vision analysis path instead of attaching the image natively.

The same result can be reproduced without a provider call:

```python
from agent.image_routing import decide_image_input_mode
from hermes_cli.config import load_config
from hermes_cli.runtime_provider import resolve_runtime_provider

cfg = load_config()
runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(requested="custom:qwen-token-plan")
model = "qwen3.8-max-preview"

print(runtime["provider"])            # custom
print(runtime["requested_provider"])  # custom:qwen-token-plan
print(decide_image_input_mode(runtime["provider"], model, cfg))
# text
print(decide_image_input_mode(runtime["requested_provider"], model, cfg))
# native
```

### Expected Behavior

A named custom provider selected with `-m` and `--provider custom:<name>` keeps its routable identity for capability lookup. If the selected model declares `supports_vision: true`, CLI attachments, `AIAgent` preprocessing, and the `vision_analyze` native fast path all treat it as vision-capable.

### Actual Behavior

Runtime credential resolution keeps the endpoint and key but collapses the live provider to bare `custom`. Vision lookup misses the selected provider's per-model metadata and falls back to text analysis.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not a runtime crash. Provider identity propagation defect reproduced against
current main with the real CLI parser, runtime provider resolver, image routing,
AIAgent vision gate, and vision tool native fast path. No live provider call or
private configuration is required.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11. The provider identity defect is platform-independent.

### Python Version

3.12

### Hermes Version

main @ e59dcf46f

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
runtime.provider = custom
runtime.requested_provider = custom:qwen-token-plan
actual CLI routing decision = text
decision with requested identity = native
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`resolve_runtime_provider` correctly preserves both identities:

- `provider: custom` is the transport or billing class.
- `requested_provider: custom:qwen-token-plan` is the routable configuration identity.

`CLIAgentSetupMixin._ensure_runtime_credentials` then assigns `self.provider = resolved_provider`, discarding the namespaced identity. Both interactive and one-shot image routing use `self.provider`. `_resolve_turn_agent_config` also passes that value into `AIAgent`, so `_model_supports_vision` and the tool native fast path inherit the same miss.

The alias normalization inside `_resolve_named_custom_runtime` is not the fix point. It intentionally treats `ollama`, `vllm`, and similar aliases as the custom transport. The requested named identity is already available in the runtime result and should be retained at the downstream handoff.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

When the resolved transport is `custom` and `requested_provider` is a namespaced `custom:<name>` value, keep the requested identity as the live CLI provider. Leave credentials, base URL, API mode, and canonical transport resolution unchanged.

Use the retained identity for route-change detection so repeated credential refreshes do not rebuild the agent. Add a regression that parses the exact command-line flags with a different configured default provider, runs the real provider resolver, and verifies native routing through the CLI, `AIAgent`, and vision tool gates.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Custom provider /models probe hangs for full timeout on HTTP 401 responses (should fail fast)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When Hermes probes a custom provider's `/models` endpoint during CLI startup (`_resolve_active_context_length` → `get_model_context_length` → `_resolve_endpoint_context_length`), it does not distinguish between "no route (404)" and "requires auth (401)". A 401 response takes **the full connect+read timeout** before giving up, adding 10+ seconds per probe attempt.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a custom provider that has an authenticated `/models` endpoint (e.g., Alibaba Cloud Token Plan: `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`)
2. The probe at startup has no API key available at this stage (`api_key=""`)
3. `/compatible-mode/v1/models` returns **HTTP 401** (not 404)
4. Hermes waits the full timeout (10s) before falling through
5. A second probe to `/compatible-mode/models` (without `/v1`) returns 404 — another 10s

**Total: ~20-30 seconds** wasted on a provider that is fully functional (with API key, `/models` returns 200 in 0.27s).

## Expected behavior

HTTP 401/403 responses should **fail fast** (treated the same as 404 — endpoint not usable without auth). The probe should move on immediately rather than waiting for a read timeout.

## Context

- **Endpoint:** `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/models`
- **Without API key:** HTTP 401 (slow — 10s to return)
- **With API key:** HTTP 200 in 0.27s (returns model list correctly)
- **Affected version:** v0.19.0+ (after custom provider probe was added to `_resolve_active_context_length`)
- **Known providers (deepseek, openai, etc.)** are skipped entirely — this only affects custom/unknown providers

## Workaround

Set `model.context_length` in config.yaml — `get_model_context_length` step 0 short-circuits before any probe:

```yaml
model:
  context_length: 256000
```

For users switching models via scripts: read `context_length` from `providers.<name>.models.<model>.context_length` and write it to the top-level `model.context_length`.

## Related

- #69807 — same probe path, but for endpoints with no `/models` route (404 case)
- #69323 — feature request for native Token Plan provider support

items.title: [Bug] Steer/redirect messages not visible in Desktop chat after update
items.body:
### Description

After a recent Desktop app update, user messages sent while the agent is busy (via `busy_input_mode: steer`) no longer appear in the conversation chat area. The steer text is still delivered to the agent and processed correctly, but the optimistic user message insertion does not work — the chat shows nothing, as if no steer was sent.

Previously, steer messages would appear at the bottom of the chat (as a `steer:...` system note in older versions, then as a user message inserted before the active reply after the Jul 13 refactor).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running agent turn (tools executing / streaming)
2. Type text in the composer while the session is busy
3. With `display.busy_input_mode: steer`, the message is sent as a steer/redirect
4. **Expected:** The typed text appears as a user message bubble in the conversation
5. **Actual:** Nothing appears in the chat, though the agent receives and processes the text

### Technical Analysis

The steer message display is handled by `redirectPrompt()` in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts`:

1. **Line 655:** Calls `appendSessionTextMessage(id, 'user', text, undefined, { insertBeforeActiveReply: true })` — inserts an optimistic user message before the active reply
2. **Line 673:** Calls `session.redirect` RPC
3. On `"redirected"` / `"queued"` response → message is preserved
4. On any other status or error → `discardOptimisticMessage()` **removes the message** (line 694)

The most likely cause is that `session.redirect` returns an unexpected status (neither `"redirected"` nor `"queued"`), causing the optimistic message to be deleted.

### Relevant Commits

- `34d0de80e` (Jul 13) — Switched from `session.steer` (system note) to `session.redirect` (user message)
- `8a21df18a` (Jul 22) — Fixed steer message placement before redirected replies (#69739)
- `5fccc9aae` (Jul 22-23) — Modified the same file but only for session recovery profile routing, not steer logic

### Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Hermes Agent:** v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- **Desktop app:** Updated Jul 23
- **Config:** `display.busy_input_mode: steer`

items.title: [Feature]: Track upgrade to mcp==2.0.0b2 and MCP 2026-07-28 stateless migration

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

The MCP specification release candidate **2026-07-28** is scheduled for **July 28, 2026** ([official announcement](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)). Per the announcement, it is the largest revision of the protocol since launch and makes MCP **stateless**:

- The initialize **handshake is removed**.
- The `Mcp-Session-Id` header is **removed** — any request can be routed to any server, so MCP works behind a plain load balancer.
- Beta SDKs have been published: [`mcp==2.0.0b2`](https://libraries.io/pypi/mcp) for Python, plus betas for TypeScript, Go, and C# ([SDK announcement](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/sdk-betas-2026-07-28/)).

`hermes-agent` currently pins **`mcp==1.26.0`** on `main`, declared in three extras in `pyproject.toml` (`dev`, `mcp`, `computer-use`). There is an open Dependabot PR [#65926](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65926) bumping to `mcp==1.28.1`, but at the time of writing **4 of its 36 CI checks are failing** (Python tests slices 1/8, 2/8, and the live CI review comment job). Furthermore, 1.28.x is still a v1 release — its release notes state only that it *deprecates* the WebSocket transport and the experimental tasks API. It does not implement the stateless 2026-07-28 protocol. To actually speak the new spec, Hermes needs to move onto the `mcp==2.0.x` line.

A local grep of the repository confirms there is **no existing reference** to `Mcp-Session-Id` anywhere in the codebase, and the main MCP client logic in `tools/mcp_tool.py` does not import from the official `mcp` package (only two test files under `tests/tools/` do). That is good news for the migration — Hermes is not deeply entangled with the v1 session model — but there is still work to do, and no issue is currently tracking it.

## Proposed Solution

A staged migration, one PR per step:

### Step 1 — Resolve PR #65926
- Triage the four failing CI jobs and merge (or close-and-replace) the bump from `mcp==1.26.0` to `mcp==1.28.1`. 1.28.x surfaces the v2 `DeprecationWarning`s (WebSocket transport, `Server.experimental` / `ClientSession.experimental`) without breaking behavior, so it is a safe intermediate target.

### Step 2 — Adopt the v2 beta
- Pin `mcp==2.0.0b2` (or the first stable `mcp>=2.0` once it ships) in `pyproject.toml` across the `mcp`, `dev`, and `computer-use` extras, and regenerate `uv.lock`.

### Step 3 — Audit stateful MCP code paths
The following in-tree touch points should be audited for any remaining session-bound assumptions:
- `tools/mcp_tool.py` — Hermes' own MCP client loop (does not import from the official `mcp` SDK).
- `tools/mcp_oauth.py`, `tools/mcp_oauth_manager.py`, `tools/mcp_dashboard_oauth.py` — OAuth flows.
- `hermes_cli/mcp_startup.py`, `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py`, `hermes_cli/mcp_picker.py` — CLI-side MCP setup.
- `mcp_serve` (listed in `py-modules`) — Hermes' own outbound MCP server surface.

### Step 4 — Tests & compatibility matrix
- Add a CI job that exercises Hermes against a `mcp==2.0.0b2` reference server.
- Keep a `mcp==1.28.x` test leg for at least one minor release so users on older MCP servers are not broken.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `mcp>=2.0` (stable) or `mcp==2.0.0b2`.
- [ ] CI green against both an `mcp 1.28` server and an `mcp 2.0` server.
- [ ] Any stateful handshake / session-id handling identified in Step 3 is removed or gated.
- [ ] Release note / migration note added in `website/docs/` for users running custom MCP servers.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Stay on `mcp==1.28.x` indefinitely.** Rejected: 1.x will not speak the stateless protocol, so Hermes will stop interoperating with any server that upgrades after the spec goes final.
2. **Fork the SDK and patch in stateless support.** Rejected: the upstream v2 SDK is already in beta; forking would create a permanent maintenance burden.
3. **Wait for stable `mcp 2.0` before starting.** Risky: the RC drops on 2026-07-28 (five days from the time of writing) and the community migration is already underway (see the [r/devopsish discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/devopsish/comments/1to7nrs/the_20260728_mcp_specification_release_candidate/) and the [developer migration guide](https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/mcp-2026-07-28-breaking-changes)). Starting against the beta lets Hermes ship compatible on day one of the stable release.

## Related
- PR [#65926](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65926) — `chore(deps): bump mcp from 1.26.0 to 1.28.1` (open, CI failing)
- Issue [#55469](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/55469) — HTTP Streamable MCP connection failure
- Issue [#69097](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/69097) — MCP on-demand loading / session-scoped activation
- Issue [#66473](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/66473) — MCP Smart Loading (lazy connection, per-session scoping)

## References
- [The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification Release Candidate](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)
- [Beta SDKs for the 2026-07-28 MCP Spec Release](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/sdk-betas-2026-07-28/)
- [`mcp` package versions on PyPI](https://libraries.io/pypi/mcp)

## Contribution
- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

I'm happy to drive this migration end-to-end — starting with triaging PR #65926, then moving Hermes onto the `mcp==2.0.0b2` beta and wiring up the compatibility-matrix CI job.

### Bug Description

I used qwen3.6 35b a3b to generate this bug report containing my unintended behavior.

Ghost profiles. user deleted profiles are coming back with factory skills and templates.

### Steps to Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

### Affected Component
