### Debug Report

```shell
a/Desktop/Hermes_Profile_Ghost_Bug_Report.md → b/Desktop/Hermes_Profile_Ghost_Bug_Report.md
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+# Bug Report: Hermes Desktop App Re-creates Deleted Profiles from Internal Cache
+
+## Summary
+The Hermes desktop app stores a list of known profile names in its Electron LocalStorage (LevelDB). When the app starts, it scans this internal list and creates any profiles that don't exist on disk — even if they were intentionally deleted. This causes "ghost" profiles to reappear after deletion, making it impossible to permanently remove profiles through normal means.
+
+## Steps to Reproduce
+1. Create a named profile (e.g., `my-test-profile`) via `hermes profile create my-test-profile` or the desktop app UI
+2. Verify the profile directory exists at `~/.hermes/profiles/my-test-profile/`
+3. Delete the profile directory: `rm -rf ~/.hermes/profiles/my-test-profile/`
+4. Close and restart the Hermes desktop app
+5. Observe that `my-test-profile` reappears in `~/.hermes/profiles/`
+
+## Expected Behavior
+Deleted profiles should remain deleted. The profile list should be derived from the actual filesystem state, not from a stale cached list.
+
+## Actual Behavior
+The Hermes desktop app re-creates the deleted profile directory with a minimal set of files (SOUL.md, cache/, cron/, hooks/, image_cache/, logs/, pairing/, sessions/, skills/, state/, state.db) on every app restart, regardless of whether the user intentionally deleted it.
+
+## Technical Details
+- The profile name is stored in the Hermes app's Electron userData: `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/Local Storage/leveldb/`
+- The app appears to maintain a built-in list of known profiles that it syncs to disk on startup
+- This is separate from the `~/.hermes/profiles/` directory scan used by the CLI's `list_profiles()` function
+- The re-created profile has no meaningful config, skills, or memory — it's a skeleton that may confuse users about which profile is active
+
+## Impact
+- Users cannot permanently delete profiles, leading to confusion about which profile is actually in use
+- Config files and settings may appear to "save to the wrong profile" because the ghost profile has no config while the active profile does
+- Profile management becomes unreliable — the desktop UI shows profiles that don't have real data
+- New users following setup guides may create duplicate profiles with different data
+
+## Suggested Fix
+- Derive the profile list from the filesystem, not from a cached/internal list
+- If a built-in profile list is necessary for default profiles, ensure user-deleted profiles are removed from the cache
+- Add a "delete" command that removes the profile from both disk and the app's internal cache
+- Or: make the CLI the authoritative source of truth and have the desktop app respect filesystem state
+
+## Environment
+- OS: macOS
+- Hermes version: 0.19.0
```

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop /steer swallows the next typed word into the slash trigger instead of free text
items.body:
### Bug Description
In Hermes Desktop's composer, typing `/steer` and then typing a word right after it (with a space) does not start a normal message after the command — the next word gets absorbed into the `/steer` directive chip instead of becoming separate message text. The user cannot cleanly type `/steer <message>` and have it submit as one flowing message the way `/compress <topic>` or a normal message does.

### Root Cause Analysis
`/steer` is registered with `args: true` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts`:

```ts
{ name: '/steer', description: 'Steer the current run after the next tool call', surface: exec(), args: true },
```

`args: true` tells the composer's trigger engine (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-trigger.ts`, `replaceTriggerWithChip`) that the bare command has a discrete **options screen** to expand into — the same mechanism used for `/personality`, `/tools`, `/skin`, `/handoff`, and `/resume`, all of which have a finite, enumerable list of valid arguments (personality names, tool names, theme names, platforms, session ids).

```ts
// composer-utils.ts
export const slashArgStage = (query: string) => query.includes(' ')

// use-composer-trigger.ts
const expandsToArgs = trigger.kind === '/' && !serialized.includes(' ') && desktopSlashCommandTakesArgs(command)
```

When `expandsToArgs` is true, picking/committing the bare `/steer` command does **not** emit a pill immediately — it keeps the trigger popover open (`keepTriggerOpen = starter || expandsToArgs`) so the next characters the user types are treated as an **arg completion query** against `complete.slash`, not as free message text. Only once the popover run out of matches and the user hits Space/Tab does `commitTypedSlashDirective()` finally commit `/steer <query-so-far>` as one directive chip (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-trigger.ts:139-159`).

The practical effect: after typing `/steer` and a space, the very next word gets folded into the still-open slash trigger/chip instead of flowing as normal composer text, because `/steer`'s argument is **free-form message text**, not a fixed enumerable option — unlike every other `args: true` command in the registry. `/compress`'s `focus_topic` has the same free-text nature but does not exhibit the same symptom as sharply because it's an `action()` handler, not `exec()`, and its arg stage more reliably runs empty/commits — `/steer` is the one users hit this on in practice (see also #53659, a related Desktop composer/steer timing bug, and #34569 for a similar historic steer-buffer issue in CLI/TUI).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Hermes Desktop, start or resume a chat.
2. In the composer, type `/steer` then a space, then start typing a word (e.g. `please`).
3. Observe: the typed word is consumed into the still-open slash-command popover/chip instead of appearing as normal trailing message text.

### Expected Behavior
`/steer <message>` should behave like a normal free-text argument command: typing the command, a space, then any text should simply produce `/steer <message>` ready to submit — the same way it behaves for commands whose argument is arbitrary text rather than a fixed option (e.g. `/goal <text>`, `/queue <prompt>`).

### Suggested Fix
`args: true` conflates two different needs in `DesktopCommandSpec`: (1) "expand to an enumerable options screen" (`/personality`, `/tools`, `/skin`, `/handoff`, `/resume`) and (2) "takes a free-text argument, no options screen" (`/steer`, `/goal`, `/queue`). `/steer` should not set `args: true` — or `desktopSlashCommandTakesArgs`/`expandsToArgs` should distinguish an enumerable-options flag from a merely-takes-an-argument flag so free-text commands commit their bare directive immediately and let subsequent typing flow as plain composer text.

### Affected Component
Desktop (Electron app / UI) — composer / slash-command trigger engine.

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), commit `1b8e34e94`
- Windows 10, Hermes Desktop

items.title: [Bug]: Cron jobs cannot deliver to Photon — sidecar/token unavailable in cron subprocess (distinct from #51897)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
# [Bug]: Cron jobs cannot deliver to Photon — sidecar/token unavailable in cron subprocess (distinct from #51897)

**Repository:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Component:** comp/cron, comp/plugins (photon)
**Type:** bug
**Severity:** P2 (automation delivery silently fails for a configured platform)

## Summary

A `no_agent` cron job with `deliver: photon:<target>` fails at delivery time with:

```
delivery error: Photon standalone send requires a running sidecar with
PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN set in the environment. Cron processes cannot spawn
the sidecar themselves.
```

The cron script itself runs fine (stdout is produced), but the Photon delivery
step cannot reach the sidecar / does not have the sidecar token in its
environment. This is **distinct from #51897** (which is a free-tier *shared
line* `Target not allowed` auth error) — our error is about the **cron
subprocess not having the sidecar connection / PHOTON_* secrets**, regardless
of tier.

## Why it happens (evidence)

1. **Photon is a persistent-connection channel by design** (plugins/platforms/photon/README.md):
   > "Photon is a persistent-connection channel ... Hermes runs it inside a small
   > supervised Node sidecar and talks to it over loopback."
   > "Outbound: send ... are loopback POSTs to the sidecar (/send, ...),
   > authenticated with a shared X-Hermes-Sidecar-Token."

   So Photon delivery requires the **live gateway + sidecar** loopback. A cron
   subprocess does not have that.

2. **The sidecar token is dynamic / not in `.env`.** `~/.hermes/.env` contains
   `PHOTON_PROJECT_ID`, `PHOTON_PROJECT_SECRET`, `PHOTON_ALLOWED_USERS`,
   `PHOTON_HOME_CHANNEL` — but **no `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN`**. That token is
   generated at sidecar runtime (see `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`
   `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN`). So a script cannot inject it from `.env`.

3. **Cron runner strips secrets from the child env.** In `cron/scheduler.py`
   `_run_job_script()`, the subprocess env is built via
   `_sanitize_subprocess_env(os.environ.copy())` which (per its docstring)
   "provider credentials and other Hermes-managed secrets are not inherited."
   So even if the gateway process had `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN`, the cron child
   would not see it.

4. **`hermes send --to photon` also fails standalone**, confirming Photon send
   is not a plain CLI operation:
   ```
   $ echo hi | hermes send --to "photon:any;-;+628****4708"
   hermes send: Could not resolve 'any;-;+628****4708' on photon.
   ```
   (The target string came straight from `hermes send --list`, so the resolver
   itself does not handle Photon targets the way `--list` displays them.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Photon (dedicated number, `PHOTON_HOME_CHANNEL` set to a phone).
2. Create a `no_agent` cron job whose `script` prints to stdout, with
   `deliver: photon:<phone>`.
3. Let it run (or `hermes cronjob run <id>`).
4. Job executes (stdout generated) but delivery fails with the sidecar error
   above. Same failure whether the deliver target is the Photon DM or home
   channel.

## Expected behavior

Cron jobs should be able to deliver to Photon the same way live conversations
do — i.e. the cron delivery path should reuse the **already-running gateway
sidecar connection** (or the runner should forward the sidecar token / loopback
endpoint to the delivery step), instead of requiring the cron subprocess to
spawn its own sidecar.

## Actual behavior

Cron delivery to Photon unconditionally fails with the sidecar/token error,
even though Photon works perfectly for live (inbound-session) replies.

## Related

- #51897 — "Photon: shared/free-tier lines cannot send outbound cron deliveries
  (Target not allowed)". **Different root cause**: that one is a spectrum
  *tier/line* auth rejection (`space.phone=shared`). Ours is the cron subprocess
  lacking the sidecar connection / `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN` env, independent of
  tier. Possibly the same underlying "cron cannot do outbound Photon" gap, but
  the error chain is different — worth tracking whether one fix covers both.
- #69047 — "Feature: Default attach_to_session=true for Photon/iMessage-delivered
  crons" (related cron+Photon delivery surface).

## Suggested fixes (prioritized)

- **P1** — Route cron→Photon delivery through the **live gateway sidecar**
  (the gateway already holds the loopback connection + token). The cron runner
  should hand the delivery to the gateway's Photon adapter, not attempt a
  standalone sidecar spawn in the child process.
- **P2** — If a standalone path is kept, have the cron runner explicitly pass
  `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN` (and sidecar URL) to the delivery subprocess env,
  exempting it from `_sanitize_subprocess_env` for the Photon case.
- **P3** — Make `hermes send --to photon:<target>` resolve targets the same way
  `hermes send --list` displays them (the `any;-;+phone` form is not accepted
  by the resolver).

## Workaround (current)

Use a different platform for cron delivery (WhatsApp DM / Telegram DM both work
from cron in the reporter's env). No Photon workaround exists.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.2, Hermes Agent (current main), Photon configured with a dedicated
  number (`PHOTON_HOME_CHANNEL=+62...`).
- Cron: `no_agent=true`, `script=github_trending_daily.py`, `deliver=photon:<phone>`.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When configuring a custom OpenAI-compatible provider through the Desktop UI (Settings → Providers → Custom Endpoints), the **Test** button successfully calls `/v1/models` and discovers all available models. However, clicking **Save** only persists the single model name the user manually entered in the form field — the full discovered list is not written to config.

As a result, the main model picker, auxiliary model picker, and chat composer model selector all show only that one model for the custom provider.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Desktop → Settings → Providers → Custom Endpoints → Edit Endpoint
2. Fill in name, base URL, a model name, and API key
3. Click **Test** → "Endpoint is reachable. Found N models."
4. Click **Save**
5. Inspect `config.yaml` → `providers.<id>.models` contains only 1 entry
6. Settings → Model → select the custom provider → dropdown shows only 1 model
7. Chat composer → model picker → same result

## Expected Behavior

After Test discovers N models and the user clicks Save, all N models should be persisted to `config.yaml`. The configuration panel, main model picker, auxiliary picker, and chat composer should all immediately display the full model list.

## Actual Behavior

- `config.yaml` stores only the manually-typed model name
- All pickers show only 1 model
- The workaround involves activating the provider first, reopening the picker so the probe logic fires, then selecting the desired model — requiring two separate activation steps

## Affected Component

- Configuration (config.yaml)
- Desktop UI

## Root Cause Analysis

**Write path** — `hermes_cli/web_server.py: _write_custom_endpoint (L7379-7383)` upserts only the user-typed model:

```python
existing_models = entry.get("models")
models_map = dict(existing_models) if isinstance(existing_models, dict) else {}
current_model_entry = models_map.get(model)
models_map[model] = dict(current_model_entry) if isinstance(current_model_entry, dict) else {}
entry["models"] = models_map
```

The frontend holds `discoveredModels` in state (populated by Test), but `toPayload()` (L61-74) does not include it in the save request.

**Read path** — All downstream views read from `config.yaml`. The probe logic in `model_switch.py:2416` only fires when the provider is the current one (`_can_probe_custom_provider(row_is_current=True)`), so non-current providers do not auto-discover either.

## Proposed Fix

**Backend** — `web_server.py`:
1. Add `models: Optional[List[str]] = None` to `CustomEndpointUpdate` (L1211)
2. In `_write_custom_endpoint` (L7379-7383): when `body.models` is non-empty, build the models map from it rather than upserting a single entry

**Frontend** — `custom-endpoints-settings.tsx`:
1. `handleSave()` passes `discoveredModels` in the payload to `saveCustomEndpoint()`
2. After Test returns models, the model field switches from a text input to a dropdown populated from the discovered list

## Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes — will append this fix to existing PR #69488.

items.title: [Bug]: a single test kills pytest silently with exit 0 -- unstubbed os._exit in test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

A single test silently kills the entire pytest process with **exit code 0**:
`tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::TestSystemdServiceRefresh::
test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot`. The test's `run_gateway()`
call reaches the CLI wrapper's hard-exit path, which calls `os._exit` --
unstubbed -- so the interpreter dies mid-test: no result line, no summary,
exit 0.

The dangerous consequence is at directory scope: `pytest tests/hermes_cli -q`
terminates at ~33% (everything after `test_gateway_service.py` alphabetically
never runs) **with exit code 0 and no failure signal**. Any CI job or
contributor running the directory gets a green exit while roughly two-thirds of
the tests were never executed. Found while preparing #69737/#69763.

## Steps to Reproduce

Pristine checkout of `2a2474512` (also current main), plain pytest:

```
python -m pytest "tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::TestSystemdServiceRefresh::test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot" -v
```

## Expected Behavior

The test passes or fails and pytest prints a summary; a test must never be able
to take down the runner silently, and certainly not with exit 0.

## Actual Behavior

With `-v`: the test name prints, then the process exits immediately -- no
PASSED/FAILED, no summary, `$? == 0`. Same signature at directory scope
(progress output stops at ~33%, exit 0, no summary).

## Affected Component

Other (test suite), CLI (interactive chat)

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

N/A -- source-checkout test-suite issue, no runtime install involved.
Environment: Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.13 venv (`uv pip install -e ".[all,dev]"`),
plain pytest (xdist not involved).

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x86-64)

## Python Version

3.13

## Hermes Version

source checkout @ `2a2474512` (reproduces on current main)

## Root Cause Analysis

The test (tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py, `TestSystemdServiceRefresh::
test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot`) stubs
`get_systemd_unit_path`, `generate_systemd_unit`, and
`supports_systemd_services`, then drives `run_gateway()` -- but does not stub
the exit path. `run_gateway()`'s wrapper reaches
`_hard_exit_after_gateway_teardown` (`hermes_cli/gateway.py#L4978`), which
delegates to `gateway.run._exit_after_graceful_shutdown` -> `os._exit`. The
inline comment at `hermes_cli/gateway.py#L5002` ("unreachable in production
(os._exit); guard for test stubs") shows tests are expected to stub these exits;
this one misses it, and `os._exit` bypasses pytest entirely.

## Proposed Fix

Two layers, ideally both:

1. Fix the test: monkeypatch `_hard_exit_after_gateway_teardown` (or
   `gateway.run._exit_after_graceful_shutdown`) like sibling tests stub other
   exit guards, so the test observes the exit instead of dying from it.
2. Defense in depth: a conftest-level autouse guard for this test family that
   replaces `os._exit` with something raising, so any future unstubbed
   hard-exit becomes a loud failure instead of a silent green -- the
   exit-0-with-most-tests-skipped failure mode is the worst kind for CI.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Possibly, if maintainers agree with the two-layer approach.

items.title: Anthropic subscription OAuth token gets generic 429 through Hermes, while the genuine Claude Code binary works with the same token

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
**Environment:** Hermes Agent (Docker template, agent v0.19.x), Ubuntu VPS. Anthropic auth via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` generated by `claude setup-token` on an active Claude subscription.

## Summary
Configuring Anthropic as a provider in Hermes using a subscription OAuth token consistently fails with a generic `429 rate_limit` error on every request, even when the subscription window is fresh. The same token works perfectly when used by the genuine Claude Code CLI, both on macOS and inside the very same VPS container.

## What we tested
1. **Token validity:** direct use with the official Claude Code binary (v2.1.217) succeeds on macOS and on the VPS itself. The token is valid and authorized.
2. **Hermes adapter:** all requests through the Hermes Anthropic transport return `429 rate_limit`, at any time of day, including immediately after the subscription window reset.
3. **Header permutations:** we replayed the adapter's requests with adjusted user agent, client identification headers, and a spoofed Claude Code version string. Result unchanged: 429.
4. **Credential hygiene:** removed stale credential entries left by earlier failed OAuth device flows to rule out pool conflicts. No effect.

## Conclusion from testing
The Anthropic endpoint appears to honor subscription OAuth tokens only for the genuine Claude Code client, fingerprinted beyond plain HTTP headers. The Hermes transport is therefore rejected upstream regardless of configuration, so this does not seem fixable from user config.

## Current workaround
Primary model set to Gemini, with the real Claude Code binary installed inside the container and invoked as a terminal tool (`claude -p --model ...`) for heavy reasoning. Works, but loses native provider integration.

## Request
Either implement subscription OAuth support via the official transport (as Claude Code does), or document that Anthropic subscription tokens are not usable through the adapter so users configure API billing instead. Happy to provide logs or run tests on our instance.

items.title: test-safety: tui_gateway completion tests read the developer's real config.yaml (terminal.cwd) and fail on a pristine checkout

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`tests/gateway/test_complete_path_at_filter.py` fails 7 of 15 tests on a pristine checkout of current `main` (8fc278207) whenever the developer's real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` sets `terminal.cwd`. CI stays green because CI machines have no real Hermes config. The tests are not hermetic: they read the developer's live config through an import-time home capture.

## Mechanism

1. `tui_gateway/server.py:42` captures the home once at module import: `_hermes_home = get_hermes_home()`.
2. Test modules import at pytest collection time. The per-test `HERMES_HOME` redirect (autouse `_hermetic_environment` in `tests/conftest.py`) applies only later, per test. The canonical runner (`scripts/run_tests.sh`) starts pytest with a cleaned env, so `HERMES_HOME` is unset at import and `get_hermes_home()` falls back to the real `~/.hermes`.
3. The completion tests call `complete.path` with no `cwd`/`session_id`/`profile` params and rely on `monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)`. But `_completion_cwd()` consults `_launch_configured_cwd()` BEFORE `os.getcwd()`. `_launch_configured_cwd()` → `_load_cfg()` reads `<_hermes_home>/config.yaml` — the developer's REAL config.
4. When that config sets `terminal.cwd`, the handler lists that directory instead of `tmp_path`, and every assertion about `src/`, `docs/`, `readme.md` fails.

## Reproduction

Precondition: a real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` containing e.g.

```yaml
terminal:
  cwd: /some/existing/dir
```

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_complete_path_at_filter.py
# → 7 failed, 8 passed
```

Both directions:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_complete_path_at_filter.py -q
# → 7 failed, 8 passed  (real home visible at import)

HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_complete_path_at_filter.py -q
# → 15 passed           (neutral home at process start)
```

Failing tests: `test_at_file_bare_without_colon_lists_files`, `test_at_file_colon_only_files`, `test_at_folder_bare_without_colon_lists_dirs`, `test_at_folder_colon_only_dirs`, `test_fuzzy_hides_dotfiles_unless_asked`, `test_fuzzy_ranks_exact_before_prefix_before_subseq`, `test_fuzzy_paths_relative_to_cwd_inside_subdir`.

Example failure:

```
>       assert any(t == "@folder:src/" for t in texts)
E       assert False
```

The returned items list the configured `terminal.cwd` directory instead of the test's `tmp_path`.

## Notes

- The product behavior itself looks intentional (`_launch_configured_cwd`'s docstring explains why a configured `terminal.cwd` should win for in-memory dashboard sessions). This is a test-hermeticity defect, not a product defect.
- Same defect class as #69283 (kanban tests) and the updater-restart hermeticity fix in #68988: test isolation relies on env vars that are not yet set when module-level state is captured.

## Proposed fix (either works)

1. In `test_complete_path_at_filter.py`, add an autouse fixture that pins the leak points, e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr(server, "_launch_configured_cwd", lambda: None)` — or point `server._hermes_home` at the per-test `HERMES_HOME`.
2. Alternatively, set a neutral `HERMES_HOME` at interpreter start for the whole suite (e.g. export it in `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py` before spawning each per-file pytest), so no import-time capture can ever see the real `~/.hermes`. This closes the class, not just this file.

I am happy to submit either as a small PR if the shape is acceptable.

items.title: reasoning_effort: "ultra" rejected by GLM API (HTTP 400), triggers silent fallback to Claude Sonnet

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `reasoning_effort` is set to `"ultra"` (e.g., via `/reasoning ultra` or the desktop model picker's "Ultra" tier) and the active model is `z-ai/glm-5.2`, every API call fails with HTTP 400 because the GLM API does not accept `"ultra"` as a valid reasoning effort value. If `fallback_providers` is configured, the session silently switches to the fallback model (e.g., Claude Sonnet 5 via Anthropic) without surfacing the root cause to the user.

## Root Cause

`_reasoning_config_for_model()` in `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` (lines 20–31) only clamps `"ultra"` → `"max"` for GPT-5.6 models:

```python
def _reasoning_config_for_model(model: str, reasoning_config: dict | None) -> dict | None:
    if not isinstance(reasoning_config, dict):
        return reasoning_config
    if (
        "gpt-5.6" in (model or "").lower()
        and str(reasoning_config.get("effort") or "").strip().lower() == "ultra"
    ):
        normalized = dict(reasoning_config)
        normalized["effort"] = "max"
        return normalized
    return reasoning_config
```

For all other models — including `z-ai/glm-5.2` — `"ultra"` passes through verbatim. The GLM API returns:

```
HTTP 400: This request is not valid. Check the model name and other parameters.
Additional info: reasoning.effort: Invalid option: expected one of
"max"|"xhigh"|"high"|"medium"|"low"|"minimal"|"none"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure model `z-ai/glm-5.2` via the Nous provider
2. Set reasoning effort to `ultra` (via `/reasoning ultra` or the desktop model picker's "Ultra" option)
3. Optionally configure a fallback: `fallback_providers: [{provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5}]`
4. Send any message

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- `"ultra"` is clamped to `"max"` (the highest level GLM accepts) before the request is sent, OR
- The user is shown a clear error that `"ultra"` is not supported by the current model

## Actual Behavior

- **Without fallback**: API call fails with HTTP 400 after 3 retries; the user sees a generic error
- **With fallback configured**: The session silently switches to the fallback model. The user sees the model has changed (e.g., "Switched to fallback model: z-ai/glm-5.2 → claude-sonnet-5") but does not see the underlying 400 error or the reason it occurred. Subsequent turns continue on the fallback model

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- Model: `z-ai/glm-5.2` via Nous provider
- Reasoning effort: `ultra`
- Fallback: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (configured in profile)

## Suggested Fix

Extend the `"ultra"` → `"max"` clamp in `_reasoning_config_for_model()` to all models (or at minimum, to all models that don't accept `"ultra"`), not just GPT-5.6. Alternatively, clamp to each model's supported effort levels based on metadata.

## Log Evidence

From `~/.hermes/profiles/adg/logs/agent.log`:
```
2026-07-22 20:26:52 WARNING API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
  provider=nous model=z-ai/glm-5.2
  summary=HTTP 400: ... reasoning.effort: Invalid option: expected one of "max"|"xhigh"|"high"|"medium"|"low"|"minimal"|"none"
```

items.title: Windows: first terminal/file tool call hangs forever — _bash_starts probe pipes never EOF (timeout kill + untimed communicate() deadlock)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Summary

On Windows, the first terminal (or file) tool call in an agent session can hang **forever** — no timeout, no error, no log — at `Creating new local environment for task default...`. The agent turn never completes and the process must be killed.

Root cause (confirmed with a faulthandler stack dump and a verified fix, details below): `_bash_starts` in `tools/environments/local.py` probes bash candidates with

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    [bash, "--noprofile", "--norc", "-c", _BASH_EXTERNAL_PROGRAM_PROBE],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    timeout=15,
    ...
)
```

In a busy agent process this is a deadlock trap on Windows:

1. The MSYS/Git-Bash probe spawns children (`/usr/bin/true`, `/usr/bin/cat`) which inherit the captured stdout/stderr pipe write-handles.
2. If the pipes don't EOF within 15 s (bash itself exits quickly, but the handles survive in MSYS descendants — readily reproducible in a thread- and subprocess-heavy agent process, while the same probe takes 0.3 s in a quiet standalone process), `subprocess.run` hits `TimeoutExpired`, kills **bash only** — its MSYS children are orphaned and keep the pipe handles.
3. `subprocess.run`'s timeout path then calls `communicate()` again **with no timeout**, which joins the stdout/stderr reader threads until pipe EOF — which never comes.

Result: `init_session` never returns and never reaches its own timeout/fallback handling, because the hang is *inside* `_find_bash` before `_run_bash` even spawns the real login shell. Nothing is ever logged (the failure-path logging in `_bash_starts` is unreachable). Issues #16425 and #37230 look like plausible siblings of this failure class.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Home, ARM64 (Snapdragon X Elite)
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0, fresh native install via `install.ps1` (also reproduced on a git-clone install of main @ 2026-07-21)
- CPython 3.11.15 (`cpython-3.11.15-windows-x86_64-none` via uv, running under x64 emulation)
- Git for Windows 2.49.0 (x64), `HERMES_GIT_BASH_PATH` pointing at it; the same bash probes in 0.3 s from a plain console
- Driven over ACP (`hermes-acp` stdio server); also reproduced identically twice on separate days/installs

### Repro

1. Windows machine with Git for Windows; terminal toolset enabled.
2. Start `hermes-acp` (stdio), open a session, prompt: `Use your terminal tool to run exactly: echo ok && pwd`.
3. The tool call logs `tools.terminal_tool: Creating new local environment for task default...` and then nothing, indefinitely (observed >9 minutes before killing; reproduced 3/3 attempts across two installs).

Notably, constructing `LocalEnvironment` directly from a standalone Python process (same venv, same env vars, even with piped stdio and a hidden window) completes `init_session` in ~3 s every time — the hang needs the full agent process around it, which is consistent with the pipe-handle mechanism above.

### Stack dump at the hang (faulthandler, abridged; identical across four 60 s dumps)

```
Thread A (tool executor — hung):
  threading.py:1139 _wait_for_tstate_lock
  threading.py:1119 join
  subprocess.py:1628 _communicate
  subprocess.py:1209 communicate
  subprocess.py:559  run                      <- the *untimed* post-kill communicate
  tools/environments/local.py:807  _bash_starts
  tools/environments/local.py:674  _find_bash
  tools/environments/local.py:1336 _run_bash
  tools/environments/base.py:528   init_session
  tools/environments/local.py:1274 __init__
  tools/terminal_tool.py:1518 _create_environment
  tools/terminal_tool.py:2316 terminal_tool
  ...

Threads B, C (never finish — pipe write-ends still held by orphaned MSYS children):
  subprocess.py:1599 _readerthread
```

### Fix (verified)

Probing with DEVNULL streams removes the pipes entirely, so there are no reader threads to join and a timeout kill is clean:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    [bash, "--noprofile", "--norc", "-c", _BASH_EXTERNAL_PROGRAM_PROBE],
    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    text=True,
    timeout=15,
    creationflags=windows_hide_flags() if _IS_WINDOWS else 0,
)
```

With this one change, the identical setup that hung forever completes the terminal tool call in 2.5 s (session snapshot ~2 s), verified end-to-end over ACP. The existing `f"{result.stdout or ''}{result.stderr or ''}"` guards tolerate the now-`None` streams, though the probe-details diagnostics (`_bash_probe_details_cache`) lose their content — if that output matters for the ASLR remediation message, an alternative is capturing to a temp file, or a `Popen` + bounded drain instead of `run()`.

More generally: any `subprocess.run(capture_output=True, timeout=...)` against MSYS binaries on Windows has this orphaned-handle deadlock shape (the post-timeout `communicate()` retry in CPython's `run()` is unbounded), so other probe/exec sites may deserve the same treatment.

items.title: Feature request: first-class way to inject a message into an existing gateway session (cross-platform resume)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Use case

We run a Hermes agent (v0.19.0, self-hosted) as an autonomous support engineer: investigations are delegated to it as sessions on a **plugin platform** (Linear Agent Session webhooks via `ctx.register_platform()`), and it sometimes needs to ask a human a clarifying question **on a different surface** (Slack DM) and resume the *same* session when they answer — possibly hours later ("ask and park").

## What exists today (as far as we can tell)

- Outbound is covered: `hermes send` / `send_message` deliver cross-platform fine.
- Sessions are keyed `agent:main:{platform}:{chat_type}:{chat_id}`, and there is no supported path for an inbound message on platform B to continue a session on platform A.
- `hermes cron` runs are new-session-only; continuable cron seeds a *new* thread session, it doesn't resume the originating one.
- The TUI Gateway JSON-RPC has `session.resume` but is process-local; the OpenAI-compatible `api_server` creates its own sessions.

## Our workaround

A small poller watches the Slack DM thread (read-only) and, on the first human reply, re-enters the **originating platform's own ingress** with a synthetic, freshly-signed webhook event carrying the original `chat_id` — passing all the platform's normal auth gates. It works (probe-verified resume ~16 h after the session's last turn), but it means every new surface (email next, for us) needs another bespoke bridge, and each bridge has to re-implement dispatch confirmation.

## The ask

A first-class, documented primitive to inject a message into an existing gateway session, e.g.:

```
hermes session inject <session-key-or-id> --text "..." [--source <label>] [--untrusted]
```

or an equivalent gateway HTTP/JSON-RPC endpoint (auth'd, non-process-local). An `--untrusted` / source-labeling knob would let injected third-party content be framed distinctly from operator input in the agent's context.

That single primitive would replace per-surface bridges for what seems like a common pattern: **park an agent run, collect a human answer wherever the human actually is, resume with full context**.

Happy to share more details about our setup or test a prototype.

items.title: [Bug]: openai-codex pool replays a consumed (rotated) refresh_token and goes terminally DEAD despite adoptable fresh tokens; 'auth refreshed after 401' logged when refresh failed

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Summary

On `openai-codex`, a profile that is **idle across the ~10-day access-token expiry** while another client of the same grant (another Hermes profile, Codex CLI, VS Code) performs the rotation is left holding a **consumed** (rotated-out) `refresh_token` in its `credential_pool` entries. On its next call the pool replays that consumed token, gets `refresh_token_reused`, and the entry is marked terminally dead — even though fresh, adoptable tokens for the same grant exist. A second, smaller defect makes this hard to diagnose: the conversation loop logs `🔐 Codex auth refreshed after 401. Retrying request...` even when the refresh produced no new token, so the immediate second 401 looks like a server-side flap instead of a dead local credential.

Related but distinct from:
- #48415 (closed) — the **writer**-side gap (rotated chain not written through to global root). The write-through fix is present in the version below; this report is about the **reader**-side adoption path no-oping.
- #63413 (open) — recovery from `~/.codex/auth.json` for `manual:device_code` entries. Here the entries are `device_code`-seeded and the adoptable tokens are inside Hermes' own auth stores, not Codex CLI's.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream `7c1a0295`, `codex_responses` mode against `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`
- Docker fleet, multiple profiles sharing one ChatGPT Pro grant (device-code singleton seeded into per-profile pools)
- We also carry the cross-profile shared-store patch from PR #33574, but both defects below are in unpatched upstream code paths and reproduce without it (two profiles seeded from the same singleton suffice).

## Incident (2026-07-23, observed live)

Access token expired 2026-07-22 16:08 UTC. Profiles with in-flight Codex traffic at that instant refreshed inside the rotation window and got new access+refresh tokens. Two profiles idle at expiry made their first calls hours later:

```text
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=AuthenticationError provider=openai-codex ... summary=HTTP 401: Provided authentication token is expired.
🔐 Codex auth refreshed after 401. Retrying request...
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): AuthenticationError [HTTP 401]
   📋 Details: {'code': 'token_expired', ...}
❌ Non-retryable client error (HTTP 401). Aborting.
```

Afterwards `providers.openai-codex.last_auth_error` shows `code: refresh_token_reused`, and every subsequent call on those profiles hard-fails until manual operator intervention — while sibling profiles on the same grant keep working (proof the grant itself is healthy). Cron jobs on the affected profiles fail with `provider authentication error`.

## Defect 1 — adoption path silently no-ops, then the pool replays a consumed refresh token and dies terminally

`CredentialPool._sync_codex_entry_from_auth_store` (agent/credential_pool.py:653) is the designated recovery path and *is* called before refresh attempts. But it returns the entry unchanged whenever `providers.openai-codex.tokens` in the profile auth store has no `access_token` (in our fleet that dict legitimately contained only `last_refresh`):

```python
store_access = tokens.get("access_token", "")
...
if store_access and (...):   # empty store_access → silently no-op
```

With adoption skipped, `_refresh_entry` replays the entry's own consumed `refresh_token`. The result, `refresh_token_reused`, is in `_TERMINAL_AUTH_REASONS`, so the entry goes `STATUS_DEAD` — and per the code's own comment, device_code-seeded entries "remain in the pool marked DEAD until an explicit re-auth write-side sync". A fully recoverable situation (grant healthy, fresh tokens adoptable) is converted into a permanent per-profile outage requiring manual re-auth.

Aggravating factor: every replay of a consumed refresh token is exactly the pattern OpenAI's reuse detection watches for; in the worst case it revokes the whole grant family fleet-wide (the scenario the comments around `_TERMINAL_AUTH_REASONS` warn about).

## Defect 2 — false "auth refreshed" success log

conversation_loop.py:2613 prints the success line whenever `_try_refresh_codex_client_credentials(force=True)` returns True. That method (run_agent.py:4105) returns True whenever `resolve_codex_runtime_credentials(force_refresh=True)` hands back *any* non-empty credentials — including the same stale access token when the underlying refresh failed (failure is `logger.debug`-only). The observed log therefore claims a refresh happened immediately before the retry fails with the identical `token_expired`. This cost us real diagnosis time: it reads as a chatgpt.com flap, not a dead local credential.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `_refresh_entry`, when a refresh fails with `refresh_token_reused` / `invalid_grant`, re-attempt adoption from every available source **before** marking DEAD: sibling pool entries for the same `chatgpt_account_id` with a newer `last_refresh`, and the auth store even when its provider state is partial. Only mark DEAD when no adoptable source differs from the entry's current pair.
2. In `_sync_codex_entry_from_auth_store`, when adoption is skipped because the store has no token material, log at WARNING (not debug) — operators need to see why recovery didn't happen.
3. Make `_try_refresh_codex_client_credentials` (or `resolve_codex_runtime_credentials(force_refresh=True)`) report failure when no *new* token was actually minted (compare the access token or its JWT `exp` before/after), so the 401-retry path logs the truth.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Seed two profiles (A, B) from the same `openai-codex` device-code singleton.
2. Let the access token approach its ~10-day expiry. Keep A active through the expiry (it rotates the grant); keep B idle until well after.
3. Send a request through B: first 401 `token_expired`, a claimed "auth refreshed" retry that 401s again, then `refresh_token_reused` and a permanently DEAD pool entry — while A continues to work on the same grant.

## Operator workaround (for anyone else hitting this)

Copy the current tokens from whichever store/profile holds the fresh rotation head into the stale profile's `credential_pool.openai-codex` entries (and clear `last_status`/`last_error_*` + `providers.openai-codex.last_auth_error`), writing atomically while holding the same advisory flock on `auth.lock` that `_auth_store_lock()` uses. Do **not** let the stale profile retry-refresh its consumed token. Agents recover on the next call, no restart needed — verified live on 3 affected profiles.

items.title: Security Hardening: API Key Redaction, HTTPS, and Path Traversal

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Issue 1: API Key Redaction
Provide the `security_utils.py` code and update `config.py`.

```python
# hermes_cli/security_utils.py
def redact_sensitive_keys(config_dict):
    sensitive_keys = ['openai_api_key', 'anthropic_api_key', 'groq_api_key']
    redacted = config_dict.copy()
    for key in sensitive_keys:
        if key in redacted:
            redacted[key] = "**"
    return redacted
```

Update `hermes_cli/config.py` to import and wrap the configuration return:

```python
from hermes_cli.security_utils import redact_sensitive_keys

def get_config(...):
    cfg = ...  # original configuration loading logic
    return redact_sensitive_keys(cfg)
```

### Issue 2: HTTPS Enforcement
Add middleware to force HTTPS for all requests.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse

app = FastAPI()

@app.middleware("http")
async def enforce_https(request: Request, call_next):
    if request.url.scheme != "https":
        url = request.url.replace(scheme="https")
        return RedirectResponse(url)
    return await call_next(request)
```

### Issue 3: Path Traversal Protection
Sanitize file paths before accessing the filesystem.

```python
import os

def safe_join(base, *paths):
    final_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, *paths))
    if not final_path.startswith(os.path.abspath(base)):
        raise ValueError("Attempted path traversal")
    return final_path
```

Use `safe_join` wherever a file path is constructed from user input to prevent directory traversal attacks.

---
Please review the proposed changes and let me know if you would like a PR created with these fixes.

items.title: hermes sessions optimize-storage reports negative "reclaimed" size

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

`hermes sessions optimize-storage` reports "reclaimed" with a negative value when the database grows, which is confusing.

## Observed

```
Database size: 855.8 MB -> 1019.0 MB (reclaimed -163.2 MB)
```

## Expected

Either:
- Negative values use "grew by" format: `Database size: 855.8 MB -> 1019.0 MB (grew by 163.2 MB)`
- Or use neutral language: `Database size: 855.8 MB -> 1019.0 MB (change: +163.2 MB)`

## Root cause

`main.py` line 16086:
```python
saved = before_mb - after_mb
```

This always computes `before - after` and formats it as "reclaimed". When `after_mb > before_mb`, the result is negative and "reclaimed" is misleading.

## Suggested fix

Make the label conditional on the sign, or use neutral "delta" language.

File: `hermes_cli/main.py` lines 16083-16091.

items.title: Kanban completion notifications delivered by the wrong bot when multiple profiles share a board (cross-profile misdelivery → 403)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
**Summary**

When several profiles (each its own gateway process + its own messaging-platform bot) share one kanban board, a task's completion/terminal notification can be claimed and delivered by a *worker* profile's gateway instead of the profile that actually owns the subscribed channel. The worker gateway then tries to send using its own bot connection to a channel its bot has no access to, and the notification is silently lost.

**Setup**

- Multiple profiles, each running its own gateway, each bound to a *distinct* bot on the same platform (e.g. separate Discord bot applications).
- They share one kanban board (dispatch-in-gateway enabled). One profile ("origin") dispatches tasks and subscribes its own channel for completion notifications; other profiles ("workers") pick up and run the tasks.
- The subscribed channel is private to the origin bot (e.g. a Discord DM between the origin bot and the user).

**Observed**

- Origin dispatches N tasks, all subscribed to the origin's channel; tasks complete on worker gateways.
- No completion notification arrives at the origin channel.
- Worker gateway logs show each notify event claimed by the *worker*, waking its agent and attempting delivery to the origin's channel with the worker's own bot → `403 Forbidden (50001 Missing Access)` (the worker bot has no access to the origin bot's private channel). The origin's own gateway never claims these events, so it never delivers.

**Expected**

A completion notification for a channel owned by profile X should be delivered by profile X's gateway (which holds the bot connection that can actually reach that channel) — or by whichever gateway genuinely owns that channel's adapter — never by an unrelated worker gateway whose bot lacks access.

**Likely cause (from reading `gateway/kanban_watchers.py`)**

The notifier's ownership guard is roughly:

```python
owner_profile = sub.get("notifier_profile") or None
if owner_profile and owner_profile != notifier_profile:
    # if this gateway's profile has no adapter for the owner, skip
    ...
# otherwise fall through and deliver
```

If `notifier_profile` on the subscription is empty/NULL, the `if owner_profile and ...` short-circuits and the ownership check is skipped entirely — so **any** gateway that claims the event proceeds to deliver, including one whose bot cannot reach the channel. Two possible root causes (either or both):

1. Some subscription-creation path isn't persisting `notifier_profile`, leaving it NULL → guard bypassed.
2. Even with `notifier_profile` set, event *claiming* isn't restricted to the owning gateway, so a worker can claim-and-deliver a foreign-channel event before the owner's tick runs.

**Suggested fix**

- Ensure every notify-subscription persists its owning profile at creation time; and
- Gate both *claiming* and *delivery* of a terminal-event notification on "this gateway owns an adapter that can actually reach the subscribed channel" — treat a missing/unknown owner conservatively (don't let an arbitrary gateway deliver a channel it can't verify it owns), rather than falling through to deliver.

**Impact**

Silent loss of kanban completion notifications in any multi-profile / multi-bot shared-board setup — the notification is the only feedback that a dispatched task finished, so users are left polling manually. Single-profile setups are unaffected (only one gateway claims and it owns the channel).

items.title: [Bug]: xAI OAuth spending-limit 403 (`personal-team-blocked:spending-limit`) does not trigger fallback_providers chain

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

AI Generated Bug Summary:

When the primary `xai-oauth` provider hits a Grok spending/credit limit (HTTP 403 with code `personal-team-blocked:spending-limit`), the configured `fallback_providers` chain is not activated. The error is treated as a hard non-retryable `PermissionDeniedError` (or marks the provider unhealthy in auxiliary paths) instead of walking the fallback chain the way 429/503 errors do.

The error classifier already recognizes `_XAI_SPENDING_LIMIT_ERROR_CODE = "personal-team-blocked:spending-limit"` and puts it in `_BILLING_ERROR_CODES`, but the retry/fallback decision paths in `conversation_loop.py` (and `auxiliary_client.py`) do not consistently route `FailoverReason.billing` into the fallback chain the same way they do for `rate_limit`.

This was reproduced live on 2026-07-23 with the exact 403 payload shown in the logs.


### Steps to Reproduce

- Primary: `provider: xai-oauth`, model `grok-4.5`
- Fallback configured:
  ```yaml
  fallback_providers:
    - provider: xai
      model: grok-4.3
  ```
- Trigger: xAI OAuth account hits spending limit → returns 403.

items.title: [Feature]: Output-ceiling truncation (finish_reason=length) never triggers model fallback — only same-model continuation retries

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary

When a Bedrock/chat_completions/anthropic_messages response ends with `finish_reason == "length"` (model hit its max output token ceiling), Hermes's recovery path in `agent/conversation_loop.py` is **continuation retries against the same model** (up to 4 attempts, `_boost_base * (2 ** length_continue_retries)` on `max_tokens` each retry — see ~line 2110-2160 for the no-tool-calls path and ~line 2171-2200 for the truncated-tool-call path). `agent._try_activate_fallback()` is **never called** for this failure mode — I grepped every call site of `_try_activate_fallback` in the file and none of them sit inside the `finish_reason == "length"` block. Fallback only activates today for hard API errors (429/500/503, auth, billing — via `FailoverReason`) and one special case: a content-filter stream kill (`_cf_terminated`).

## Why this matters

This blocks a legitimate cost/capability tiering pattern: run a **small, cheap, low-output-ceiling model as the primary/cheap tier** (e.g. Meta Llama 4 Scout on Bedrock, real max output ~8,192 tokens) and **fail over to a larger-ceiling model** (e.g. Amazon Nova Premier at 25K max output, or Claude Sonnet 5 at 128K) specifically when the cheap tier's output ceiling — not an API error — is the failure. Today that tiering is impossible: a model with an 8K ceiling just retries itself 4 times against the same 8K wall and gives up with "Response truncated due to output length limit" (or, for the tool-call case, refuses to execute the truncated tool call at all). The retry/boost logic assumes `max_tokens` was under-configured, not that the underlying model's ceiling was already hit — boosting past a model's hard output cap is a no-op.

## Requested behavior

When continuation/tool-call retries are exhausted specifically due to `finish_reason == "length"` (as opposed to a network stream stall — the code already distinguishes stream-stall via `PARTIAL_STREAM_STUB_ID`), consult `agent._fallback_chain` before giving up, the same way the `_cf_terminated` content-filter branch already does a few lines above. A new `FailoverReason` (e.g. `output_ceiling_exhausted`) would let this be classified and logged distinctly from a genuine API failure, and let users configure a **fallback chain keyed on output-ceiling exhaustion specifically** (many users may want a different fallback for a 429 vs. for "my primary's output ceiling is too small for this turn").

## Where I looked

- `agent/conversation_loop.py` — the `finish_reason == "length"` block (~1963 onward), `length_continue_retries` / `truncated_tool_call_retries` loops, and every `_try_activate_fallback` call site in the file (confirmed none are inside this block; the one nearby exception is the pre-existing `_cf_terminated` content-filter escalation).
- `agent/error_classifier.py` — `FailoverReason` enum has no entry for output-ceiling exhaustion today.

## Context

Found while designing a cost-tiered fallback chain (cheap small-ceiling model → expensive large-ceiling model) for a Hermes multi-profile team. Real-world output-token distribution: sampling ~66.5K assistant turns across 6 profiles, only ~0.12% (82 turns) exceeded 8,192 estimated tokens — so an 8K-ceiling primary is viable IF it can escalate on the rare turn that needs more room. Without this fix, teams have to either overprovision every tier to the largest expected output (defeating the cost savings) or accept that ~1 in 800 turns fails outright on the cheap tier.

items.title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse transport never sets Anthropic cache breakpoints — fallback turns always pay full uncached input price

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Summary

`agent/bedrock_adapter.py` builds Bedrock Converse API requests with no `cachePoint` blocks anywhere — I grepped the file for `cachePoint`, `cache_point`, and `enable_prompt_cach` and got zero matches. Every Bedrock Converse call therefore sends the full system prompt + conversation history as **uncached** input on every single turn, even though Anthropic's Converse API on Bedrock supports `cachePoint` breakpoints for exactly this purpose (5-minute and 1-hour cache TTLs, ~10x cheaper cache-read input pricing vs. full-price input for Claude Sonnet 5: $0.20/M cache-read vs $2.00/M full input).

## Impact observed in production

Six Hermes profiles on this install run `ollama-cloud` as primary with a Bedrock (`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) fallback for when the primary provider's rate limit is hit. Comparing `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` in `state.db` sessions across billing_provider:

| profile | bedrock cache_read_tokens (14d) | bedrock input_tokens (14d) |
|---|---|---|
| dev | 0 | 146,159 |
| qa | 0 | 368,168 |
| pm | 0 | 657 |
| architect | 0 | 147 |
| em | 2,066 (0.4% of input) | 479,640 |
| default | 8,392 (33% of input) | 25,492 |

Four of six profiles show **exactly zero** cache reads/writes on the Bedrock path across two weeks and hundreds of millions of input tokens — despite these being long-lived agentic sessions (Kanban worker loops) with a large, mostly-static system prompt + tool schema prefix that would ordinarily be an ideal prompt-caching candidate on any other provider. The two profiles showing nonzero cache activity (em, default) still show cache-read as a small fraction of total input, well below what a properly cache-pointed long conversation should achieve.

Cost impact: recomputing the same 14-day token volume at the direct (uncached) Sonnet 5 rate vs. what it would cost with effective caching (using the $0.20/M cache-read rate for the repeated-prefix portion of each turn) suggests this is leaving a large, avoidable fraction of Bedrock fallback spend on the table — on top of the volume itself being a separate issue (rate-limit-driven fallback overuse, tracked separately).

## Where I looked

- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` — no `cachePoint` construction found anywhere in the file.
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — the `api_mode == "bedrock_converse"` branch (~line 403) builds the `client.converse(**api_kwargs)` call with no cache-breakpoint injection either.
- Compared against the `anthropic_messages` API mode, which (via the Anthropic SDK) does support `cache_control` on content blocks — this appears to be a Bedrock-Converse-transport-specific gap, not a general prompt-caching gap in Hermes.

## Requested behavior

Inject `cachePoint` blocks into the Bedrock Converse request at the same logical breakpoints Hermes already uses for the direct Anthropic Messages API (system prompt end, and/or the last-N-messages boundary) so long-lived Bedrock-routed conversations get the same cache economics as direct-Anthropic conversations. This is especially valuable for **fallback** scenarios (the common case here) where a session's full history has already been paid for once on the primary provider and is now being resent to Bedrock — every uncached resend compounds the fallback's cost premium.

items.title: [Feature] Fallback chain doesn't advance on output-cap (max_tokens) errors — only on availability errors

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes's primary-model fallback chain (`fallback_providers`) only advances to the next entry on **availability failures** — rate limits (429), server errors (5xx), auth failures (401/403), model-not-found (404), or malformed/empty responses. See `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py::try_activate_fallback`.

**Output-cap errors are handled by a completely separate code path that never touches the fallback chain.** When a model rejects a request because `max_tokens` exceeds its real output ceiling, `conversation_loop.py` classifies this via `is_output_cap_error()` / `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` (see `agent/model_metadata.py:1295-1415`) and either:

1. Retries the *same* model with a smaller `max_tokens`, when the provider's error message lets Hermes parse the "available tokens" figure (e.g. Anthropic's `"... = available_tokens: 10000"` phrasing), or
2. If it can't parse a safe smaller value, **fails the turn outright** (`conversation_loop.py:3775-3806`) with:
   > "max_tokens exceeds the provider's output cap for this model. Lower model.max_tokens in config.yaml."

Neither branch ever calls `agent._try_activate_fallback()`. This means a fallback chain like:

```yaml
fallback_providers:
  - provider: bedrock
    model: us.meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0   # 8,192 max output tokens
  - provider: bedrock
    model: us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0                # 64K max output tokens
  - provider: bedrock
    model: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5           # 128K max output tokens
```

...cannot actually use tiers 2/3 as an output-ceiling escape valve. If tier 1 (Scout) is active and a call genuinely needs more than 8,192 output tokens, the turn fails instead of escalating to a model with a larger ceiling — even though a perfectly good larger-ceiling fallback is configured right below it in the same chain.

## Why this matters

This is a deliberate cost-optimization pattern: put a very cheap, small-output-ceiling model as fallback tier 1, and a more expensive, larger-ceiling model as tier 2/3, accepting that most calls stay cheap and only the rare large-output call pays the escalation cost. Right now that pattern silently doesn't work — the chain is fully populated but the output-cap path never walks it.

Concretely, on our workload: 99.98% of calls need under 8,192 output tokens (so a cheap small-ceiling model works almost always), but the remaining ~0.02% would currently just fail the turn instead of escalating to a bigger model already sitting in the configured chain.

## Suggested fix

In `conversation_loop.py`, at the two output-cap-error branches (~line 3714 `available_out is not None`, and ~line 3775 `is_output_cap_error(error_msg)` with no parseable available-tokens figure):

- Before giving up and failing the turn, check whether `agent._fallback_index < len(agent._fallback_chain)`.
- If so, call `agent._try_activate_fallback(reason=FailoverReason.output_cap)` (a new `FailoverReason` value, or reuse an existing fallback-worthy reason) instead of returning the terminal failure result.
- Only fail the turn with the current "lower model.max_tokens" message once the chain is actually exhausted — mirroring the existing `_should_fallback` / chain-exhaustion pattern already used for rate-limit/server-error classes (`conversation_loop.py:3430-3502`).
- The existing `try_activate_fallback()` already resets `_ephemeral_max_output_tokens` and re-resolves context length for the new model (`chat_completion_helpers.py:1816-1843`), so the escalated call should just work with the new model's own ceiling — no extra plumbing needed beyond wiring the call.

## Alternatives considered

- **Retry the *same* model with a smaller max_tokens.** Already implemented for the case where the provider reports a parseable available-tokens number — but this truncates the response to fit the *current* model's ceiling rather than getting the *full* response from a model that can actually produce it. Good as a first-line recovery, not a substitute for chain fallback when a bigger-ceiling model is one step away.
- **Just don't use small-output-ceiling models as fallback tier 1.** Works today, but throws away a legitimate cost optimization (cheap-small-model-for-99%-of-calls, escalate-to-big-model-for-the-rare-large-output-call) that the existing `fallback_providers` list structure implies should be possible.

## Environment

- Discovered while designing a Bedrock fallback chain (Llama 4 Scout → Amazon Nova 2 Lite → Claude Sonnet 5) for a 5-agent Hermes team, sized against real completion telemetry (90 days, 136k+ calls) showing only 0.02% of calls exceed an 8,192-token output ceiling.
- Verified against live Bedrock `converse()` calls: `meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0` real output ceiling is 8,192 (not a documentation guess — confirmed via `ValidationException: ... exceeds the model limit of 8192`).

items.body:
# Bug Report — Desktop: Session list click doesn't open session

**Product:** Hermes Desktop app  
**Area:** Session list / sidebar  
**Reported:** 2026-07-23

## Symptom

Clicking a session in the session sidebar/list does not open it. The session highlights (shows as selected) but the main view area stays on the previous session or the welcome/empty state. The user stays looking at the old conversation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop app
2. Click on **Capabilities** (or any settings / non-chat panel)
3. Go back to session list
4. Click on any session from the list
5. **Expected:** The session opens in the main chat view
6. **Actual:** The session highlights in the list but the main view does not switch — stays on the previous panel

## Workaround

1. Click **"New Session"** button first
2. Then click the desired session from the list
3. Now it opens correctly

## Environment

- **App:** Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Trigger:** Happens every time after app restart; workaround resets the state

## Likely Root Cause

The session store/view likely has a stale initial state where the active session pointer is not initialized until "New Session" creates an explicit session context. The click handler checks `activeSessionId` but the welcome/empty view doesn't have one, so the click does not produce a navigation event.

## Area

`apps/desktop/src/store/` — session store or session list component, likely missing an initial active-session setter on first click when the viewport is in the empty/welcome state.

items.title: [Bug]: fallback_providers entries have no per-entry max_tokens override — global model.max_tokens is sent verbatim, breaking any fallback model with a lower output ceiling than the primary

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`fallback_providers` (list form, `config.yaml`) entries only accept `provider`, `model`, `base_url`, `api_key`/`key_env`, `context_length`, `rate_limit_delay` — there is no `max_tokens` field, and `agent.max_tokens` is never adjusted when a fallback activates (confirmed: no assignment to `agent.max_tokens` anywhere in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`'s fallback-activation code path, ~line 1690 onward, right where `agent.model`/`agent.provider`/`agent.base_url`/`agent.api_mode` ARE reassigned). This means every fallback call reuses whatever `model.max_tokens` the *primary* model needed, with zero adjustment for the fallback model's own output ceiling.

## Reproduction

- `model.max_tokens: 64000` set globally (needed for the primary model, GLM-5.2, which supports up to 131K output).
- Add a Bedrock fallback entry for `meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0` (real Converse API output ceiling: 8,192 tokens — confirmed via direct `aws bedrock-runtime converse` call).
- Every fallback call sends `inferenceConfig.maxTokens: 64000`, and Bedrock immediately rejects it:

```
An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the Converse operation: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 8192. Try again with a maximum tokens value that is lower than 8192.
```

This is a **hard, deterministic 100% failure rate** for this fallback entry — not a rare edge case. It made a cost-tiering fallback chain (cheap-small-ceiling-model → expensive-large-ceiling-model) completely non-functional as configured: every single fallback attempt to the cheap tier fails validation and falls through to the next chain entry, silently defeating the whole point of the tier.

## Why this is a distinct bug from #21498 / #37298

- #21498 is about `max_output_tokens` being dropped entirely from **custom provider** entries (a different config surface: `providers.<name>`, not `fallback_providers`).
- #37298 is about the Bedrock Converse transport's hardcoded 4096 *default* when `max_tokens` is unset — orthogonal; this bug is about the case where `max_tokens` **is** set (correctly, for the primary) but incorrectly reused for a fallback model with a lower real ceiling.
- Neither existing issue covers per-fallback-entry override.

## Requested behavior

Accept an optional `max_tokens` (and ideally `context_length` is already supported as precedent for the pattern) key on each `fallback_providers` list entry, and apply it as `agent.max_tokens` (or an ephemeral override, mirroring the existing `agent._ephemeral_max_output_tokens` mechanism used for truncated-tool-call retries) at fallback-activation time, alongside the existing `agent.model`/`agent.provider`/`agent.base_url`/`agent.api_mode` reassignment in `chat_completion_helpers.py`. Without this, no user can safely mix models with heterogeneous output ceilings in a single fallback chain — which is a real, common configuration (small/cheap models paired with larger/expensive ones specifically *because* they have different capability ceilings).

## Context

Found while building a cost-tiered Bedrock fallback chain for a 6-profile Hermes team (Ollama-Cloud primary, Bedrock fallback for rate-limit escalation). Wanted to insert a cheap Llama 4 Scout tier ahead of the existing Claude Sonnet 5 tier; discovered this blocker via a manual `aws bedrock-runtime converse` reproduction before shipping the config, so no production traffic was affected — but it would have silently 100%-failed-through on every activation had it gone live. See also #70216 (Bedrock Converse never sets Anthropic `cachePoint` breakpoints) and #70215 (output-ceiling truncation never triggers model fallback) — filed as part of the same investigation.

items.title: Bedrock Converse API never sends prompt cache breakpoints (cachePoint)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
### Problem

Bedrock has two transports in Hermes:

- Claude → `AnthropicBedrock` SDK → `api_mode=anthropic_messages` (dual-path routing in `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`). This path already gets prompt caching — it reuses `agent/prompt_caching.py`, the same logic used for direct Anthropic.
- Everything else (Amazon Nova, Llama, Mistral, Titan, DeepSeek...) and Claude under `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` auth (which `AnthropicBedrock` SDK doesn't support, SigV4-only — forces fallback, see #28156) → raw boto3 Converse API → `api_mode=bedrock_converse`, `agent/bedrock_adapter.py`.

`build_converse_kwargs()` never sends a `cachePoint` block on any of `system`, `toolConfig`, or `messages`. `normalize_converse_response()` / `stream_converse_with_callbacks()` never extract `cacheReadInputTokens`/`cacheWriteInputTokens` from the Converse response usage payload either — so even if AWS were caching implicitly, Hermes couldn't see or bill it.

Net effect: every Nova session, and every Claude session forced onto Converse by bearer-token auth, pays full input-token price on every turn — no prefix reuse across turns in the same conversation, unlike Claude's normal Bedrock path or direct Anthropic.

### Root cause

Not an invalidation bug (unlike #68191/#69704) — it's a feature gap. The Converse transport was built for cross-model support and never had cache-marker support added, while the Claude-specific `AnthropicBedrock` path got it "for free" by reusing the Anthropic caching code.

### Expected fix

- Conservative model allowlist (Nova + Claude-bearer-fallback) — AWS raises `ValidationException` if `cachePoint` is sent to an unsupported model, so unknown models must be skipped, not guessed.
- Insert `cachePoint` on system (end of block), tools (end of list, only if the model also supports tool calling), and the message before the newest turn (`messages[-2]`) — same "cache everything except the growing tail" strategy `prompt_caching.py` already uses for Anthropic.
- Extract `cacheReadInputTokens`/`cacheWriteInputTokens` from both the streaming and non-streaming response paths, fold them into `prompt_tokens` (Converse's `inputTokens` excludes cache tokens, opposite convention from OpenAI/Anthropic), and surface them under the Anthropic-named canonical fields (`cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens`) that `agent/usage_pricing.py::normalize_usage()` already falls back to — no changes needed there.

Fix implemented in #70231.
